st.mbh.aruni_lies_in_breach.title: Aruni lies down in the broken dyke
st.mbh.aruni_lies_in_breach.lesson: Wholehearted commitment to a task given in trust opens learning that no amount of instruction can.
st.mbh.aruni_lies_in_breach.summary: Aruni is sent by his teacher to close a breach in the field wall before the water drains away. He tries everything he knows and the water keeps pouring through. Evening is coming, he is alone, and the one task he was trusted with is failing in his hands.

st.mbh.upamanyu_refuses_the_cake.title: Upamanyu, starved by every test, still will not eat before offering
st.mbh.upamanyu_refuses_the_cake.lesson: Integrity that holds when you are at your lowest and unobserved is what makes a person fit to receive.
st.mbh.upamanyu_refuses_the_cake.summary: Upamanyu tends his teacher's cows and every way he finds to feed himself is taken away, one by one: the alms, the second round of alms, the milk, even the froth the calves leave. Hungry in the forest, he eats bitter leaves, goes blind and falls into a dry well.

st.mbh.veda_will_not_pass_it_on.title: Veda, who suffered as a student, decides his students will not
st.mbh.veda_will_not_pass_it_on.lesson: Hardship you lived through can be turned into care for those who come after you.
st.mbh.veda_will_not_pass_it_on.summary: Veda served his teacher for years like an ox under a yoke, through heat, cold, hunger and thirst, without complaint. Now he has students of his own living in his house, and the only model of teaching he has ever known is the one that hurt.

st.mbh.agni_cursed_for_truth.title: Agni is cursed for telling the truth
st.mbh.agni_cursed_for_truth.lesson: One who is questioned as a witness and conceals what he knows shares the wrong; honesty may be punished and still be what restores you.
st.mbh.agni_cursed_for_truth.summary: A rakshasa demands that Agni, the household fire and witness of all rites, say whose wife Puloma is. Agni knows that the truth will be used to carry her off and that a lie will make him false. He answers truthfully, the woman is seized, and her furious husband Bhrigu curses Agni to devour everything, clean and unclean.

st.mbh.ruru_gives_half_his_life.title: Ruru gives half his life for Pramadvara
st.mbh.ruru_gives_half_his_life.lesson: Love in this text is measured by what of your own life you are willing to share.
st.mbh.ruru_gives_half_his_life.summary: Days before the wedding, Pramadvara steps on a snake she did not see and falls dead. While everyone sits weeping around her, Ruru walks into the deep forest and cries aloud, calling on every good thing he has ever done to bring her back.

st.mbh.ruru_hatred_of_all_snakes.title: Ruru, hurt by one snake, vows to kill them all
st.mbh.ruru_hatred_of_all_snakes.lesson: Pain caused by one must not become punishment of all who look like them.
st.mbh.ruru_hatred_of_all_snakes.summary: Pramadvara lived, but Ruru cannot forget the day she lay dead. He takes a vow against the whole race of snakes and strikes every one he sees. One day he raises his staff over an old, harmless water snake that looks up and asks what it ever did to him.

st.mbh.jaratkaru_sees_his_ancestors.title: Jaratkaru sees his ancestors hanging by a thread
st.mbh.jaratkaru_sees_his_ancestors.lesson: A person stands in a line of givers; what you owe those who made you is part of your dharma, even on a path of renunciation.
st.mbh.jaratkaru_sees_his_ancestors.summary: Jaratkaru has built a whole life around solitude and austerity and wants nothing from the world. Wandering, he finds emaciated men hanging head down over a pit, held by one clump of grass that a rat is gnawing through. They tell him they are his own forefathers, and that the last blade of grass is him.

st.mbh.jaratkaru_wife_must_wake_him.title: Jaratkaru's wife must choose between his anger and his duty
st.mbh.jaratkaru_wife_must_wake_him.lesson: When both paths carry a cost, choose by which loss is heavier, and say plainly why you chose.
st.mbh.jaratkaru_wife_must_wake_him.summary: Her husband married her on the condition that he would leave the first time she displeased him. Now he is asleep with his head in her lap and the sun is going down. If she wakes him he will be angry. If she lets him sleep he will miss his evening rites.

st.mbh.vinata_impatience_and_wager.title: Vinata cannot wait, and then cannot refuse a bet
st.mbh.vinata_impatience_and_wager.lesson: What is still forming is harmed by being forced open, and comparison is what makes us force it.
st.mbh.vinata_impatience_and_wager.summary: Her sister's thousand eggs have already hatched while Vinata's two lie silent year after year. Ashamed and unable to bear the wait, she breaks one open and finds a son whose body is only half formed. Later, still stung by rivalry, she lets her sister draw her into a wager about the colour of a horse's tail, with slavery as the stake.

st.mbh.garuda_frees_his_mother.title: Garuda is born into his mother's debt and pays it without tasting the prize
st.mbh.garuda_frees_his_mother.lesson: Great strength shows its worth when it serves someone else's freedom and leaves the prize untouched.
st.mbh.garuda_frees_his_mother.summary: Garuda is born the strongest creature alive and finds himself carrying snakes on his back because they say so. He asks his mother why he must obey them, and she tells him she has been her sister's slave since before his birth, through a bet won by trickery.

st.mbh.shesha_leaves_his_brothers.title: Shesha walks away from a family that lives on envy
st.mbh.shesha_leaves_his_brothers.lesson: You may leave what is poisoned by envy; let the steadiness you save become something others can stand on.
st.mbh.shesha_leaves_his_brothers.summary: Shesha is the eldest of a thousand brothers who spend their days resenting one another and hating their stepbrother Garuda and his mother. He wants no part of it. He leaves home and takes up austerities so severe that his body dries to skin and sinew.

st.mbh.parikshit_tired_and_cruel_for_a_m.title: Parikshit, exhausted, insults a silent sage
st.mbh.parikshit_tired_and_cruel_for_a_m.lesson: A single act done in tired anger can outrun a lifetime of good conduct; remorse is right, and it does not undo the act.
st.mbh.parikshit_tired_and_cruel_for_a_m.summary: Parikshit is a good king, sixty years old, on a long hunt. He is hungry, thirsty and worn out, and has lost the deer he wounded. He asks a sage sitting in a cow pen which way it went. The sage is under a vow of silence and does not answer.

st.mbh.shamika_corrects_his_angry_son.title: Shamika tells his son the curse was wrong, though it was for him
st.mbh.shamika_corrects_his_angry_son.lesson: Anger steals the merit that hard practice has stored; a parent keeps correcting a child, however grown or gifted.
st.mbh.shamika_corrects_his_angry_son.summary: Shamika comes out of his silence to learn that his teenage son, mocked by a friend about the dead snake on his father's shoulder, has cursed the king to die within a week. The boy did it out of love and wounded pride. The father is the one who was insulted, and he is not pleased.

st.mbh.astika_stops_the_snake_sacrifice.title: Astika, a boy, ends a king's war on a whole race
st.mbh.astika_stops_the_snake_sacrifice.lesson: Revenge that began with one wrong will consume the innocent unless someone asks, at the right moment, for it to stop.
st.mbh.astika_stops_the_snake_sacrifice.summary: Janamejaya has learned how his father died and has turned his grief into a rite that drags every snake in the world into the fire, guilty or not. The snakes are falling by the thousand. Astika, born of a snake mother and a human sage for this hour, walks into the sacrifice as a boy with nothing but his words.

st.mbh.shakuntala_before_the_king.title: Shakuntala states the truth to a king who denies knowing her
st.mbh.shakuntala_before_the_king.lesson: The self within is the witness of every act; there is no dharma higher than truth, and a person denied may say so to anyone.
st.mbh.shakuntala_before_the_king.summary: Shakuntala walks into the royal court with her young son and asks the king to honour what he promised her in the forest. In front of everyone he says he does not remember her, calls her a liar and insults her mother. She has no witness, no document and nowhere else to go.

st.mbh.kacha_learns_among_enemies.title: Kacha studies for years in a house that wants him dead
st.mbh.kacha_learns_among_enemies.lesson: The one who gives you knowledge is owed the loyalty you owe a parent, whatever camp he belongs to.
st.mbh.kacha_learns_among_enemies.summary: Kacha is sent alone into the camp of his people's enemies to learn the one knowledge only their teacher holds. He serves that teacher faithfully for years. The others in the camp know why he has come, and they kill him, again and again.

st.mbh.devayani_refused_by_kacha.title: Devayani is refused by the man she saved
st.mbh.devayani_refused_by_kacha.lesson: Help freely given creates gratitude and does not create a claim on another person's heart.
st.mbh.devayani_refused_by_kacha.summary: For years Devayani has sung with Kacha, waited for him, and three times begged her father to bring him back from death. On the day his studies end she asks him to marry her. He answers, kindly and firmly, that she is his teacher's daughter and so a sister to him.

st.mbh.devayani_in_the_well_and_her_fath.title: Devayani, thrown in a well, is counselled to forbear and then backed completely
st.mbh.devayani_in_the_well_and_her_fath.lesson: Mastering anger is strength, and a self-respecting person does not go on living among those who hold them in contempt.
st.mbh.devayani_in_the_well_and_her_fath.summary: A quarrel over mixed-up clothes turns vicious. The princess Sharmishtha tells Devayani that her father is a beggar who lives by praising the king, and pushes her into a dry well and leaves her there. Pulled out by a passing king, Devayani refuses to enter the city again.

st.mbh.sharmishtha_accepts_servitude_for.title: Sharmishtha gives up her rank so her people keep their teacher
st.mbh.sharmishtha_accepts_servitude_for.lesson: Owning a wrong fully, at cost to your pride, can protect many people besides yourself.
st.mbh.sharmishtha_accepts_servitude_for.summary: Sharmishtha is a king's daughter who lost her temper and did something cruel. Now her whole people stand to lose their protector unless she becomes the maid of the girl she insulted, and follows her wherever she is married.

st.mbh.yayati_desire_never_ends_by_feedi.title: Yayati spends a thousand borrowed years on pleasure and finds it has no bottom
st.mbh.yayati_desire_never_ends_by_feedi.lesson: Desire is not exhausted by being fed; it grows with feeding, and peace comes from letting the thirst go.
st.mbh.yayati_desire_never_ends_by_feedi.summary: Yayati is cursed with sudden old age while his appetite for life is undiminished. He pleads that he has not had enough, and is allowed to trade his age for a son's youth. He takes it and gives himself to every pleasure that is lawful for a king, for a thousand years.

st.mbh.puru_gives_his_youth.title: Puru, the youngest, takes on his father's old age
st.mbh.puru_gives_his_youth.lesson: What is given to a parent freely and without calculation returns as blessing.
st.mbh.puru_gives_his_youth.summary: An aged king goes to each of his five sons and asks for their youth in exchange for his decrepitude. The four elder sons each explain, reasonably, why they cannot: old age ruins food, pleasure, strength and looks. Then he comes to the youngest.

st.mbh.yayati_falls_from_heaven.title: Yayati falls from heaven for one proud sentence
st.mbh.yayati_falls_from_heaven.lesson: Contempt for others burns up what a lifetime of effort has earned.
st.mbh.yayati_falls_from_heaven.summary: Yayati has earned heaven and lived there for ages. Indra asks him, casually, whom he equals in austerity. Yayati answers that he sees no one among gods, men or sages who is his equal. In that moment his merit is spent and he begins to fall.

st.mbh.shantanu_silent_until_the_eighth.title: Shantanu keeps his promise of silence while seven sons are drowned
st.mbh.shantanu_silent_until_the_eighth.lesson: There are promises a person keeps at great cost, and there is a point where speaking is the truer act.
st.mbh.shantanu_silent_until_the_eighth.summary: Shantanu married a woman he adored on one condition: he would never question or stop anything she did, or she would leave. Each time she bears him a son she carries the newborn to the river and lets him go under. Seven times he says nothing, because speaking means losing her.

st.mbh.devavrata_becomes_bhishma.title: Devavrata gives up throne and marriage so his father can marry
st.mbh.devavrata_becomes_bhishma.lesson: A vow made out of love for a parent can be magnificent and binding beyond anything its maker foresaw.
st.mbh.devavrata_becomes_bhishma.summary: Devavrata is the crown prince, gifted and adored. He notices his father has grown withdrawn and sad and will not say why. From an old minister he learns the cause: his father loves a fisherman's daughter, and her father will give her only if her son, and not Devavrata, inherits.

st.mbh.bhishma_refuses_satyavati.title: Bhishma will not break his vow even when the vow's own beneficiary begs him
st.mbh.bhishma_refuses_satyavati.lesson: A person's word, once given as a vow, is not altered because circumstances have made it inconvenient.
st.mbh.bhishma_refuses_satyavati.summary: Both of Satyavati's sons are dead without children. The line her father bargained for is about to end. She turns to the stepson who gave up everything for her marriage and asks him to take the throne and father heirs. The reason for his vow is gone, and the person asking is the one it was made for.

st.mbh.mandavya_punished_out_of_proporti.title: Mandavya, impaled for a crime he did not commit, asks Dharma why
st.mbh.mandavya_punished_out_of_proporti.lesson: Punishment must fit the act and the understanding of the one who acted; even Dharma answers for excess.
st.mbh.mandavya_punished_out_of_proporti.summary: Mandavya is standing in silent meditation when thieves hide their loot in his hermitage. The king's men find it, he does not break his vow of silence to defend himself, and he is impaled on a stake with the thieves. He stays alive on it by the strength of his practice, and when he is finally taken down, the tip remains in his body.

st.mbh.gandhari_binds_her_eyes.title: Gandhari learns her husband is blind and covers her own eyes
st.mbh.gandhari_binds_her_eyes.lesson: A vow taken freely to share another's condition becomes a source of inner power.
st.mbh.gandhari_binds_her_eyes.summary: Gandhari hears that her parents have agreed to give her to the Kuru prince, and that he was born blind. Nobody asked her. Before she ever meets him she must decide how she will enter that marriage.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_give_up_the_.title: Dhritarashtra is warned about his newborn son and keeps him
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_give_up_the_.lesson: Affection that cannot refuse its child anything becomes the child's ruin and the family's.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_give_up_the_.summary: After a two-year pregnancy and much anguish, Dhritarashtra finally has a son. The moment the child cries, jackals howl and the sky turns strange. His wisest brother and the court brahmins tell him plainly that this child will destroy the family, and that he has ninety-nine others.

st.mbh.pandu_one_arrow.title: Pandu's one careless arrow changes the rest of his life
st.mbh.pandu_one_arrow.lesson: A moment's heedlessness can set the terms of a whole life; what remains is how one lives inside those terms.
st.mbh.pandu_one_arrow.summary: Pandu is a victorious young king on a hunt. He shoots a stag in the act of mating. The stag speaks with a human voice: it was the sage Kindama, and he curses Pandu to die the moment he approaches a wife in love. In one afternoon Pandu loses the possibility of children and of ordinary married life.

st.mbh.madri_entrusts_her_sons.title: Madri admits she could not love Kunti's sons as her own and asks Kunti to love hers
st.mbh.madri_entrusts_her_sons.lesson: Knowing the limits of your own impartiality, and entrusting children to the one who has none, is itself an act of love.
st.mbh.madri_entrusts_her_sons.summary: Pandu lies dead in Madri's arms, the curse fulfilled. Kunti arrives, and the two women who shared a husband and a forest stand over him with five small boys nearby. Each claims the right to follow him. Then Madri says something no one would have blamed her for hiding.

st.mbh.bhima_poisoned_duryodhana_resentm.title: Duryodhana, beaten at every game, decides to remove his cousin
st.mbh.bhima_poisoned_duryodhana_resentm.lesson: Envy that cannot bear another's strength stops trying to grow and starts trying to remove.
st.mbh.bhima_poisoned_duryodhana_resentm.summary: The fatherless cousins arrive at court and one of them, Bhima, is stronger than all hundred brothers together. He wins every race, ducks them in the river, shakes them out of trees like fruit. To him it is play. To Duryodhana, the eldest prince, it is daily public defeat with no end in sight.

st.mbh.drona_son_cries_for_milk.title: Drona watches his son dance for joy over flour stirred in water
st.mbh.drona_son_cries_for_milk.lesson: A parent can bear his own want; seeing his child go without, and be mocked for it, is what moves him.
st.mbh.drona_son_cries_for_milk.summary: Drona is among the most learned men alive and owns nothing. His little son sees rich boys drinking milk and cries for some. Drona searches everywhere for a cow he can honestly accept and finds none. He comes home to see other children give the boy flour mixed in water, and his son drinking it and dancing, shouting that he has had milk.

st.mbh.drupada_friendship_is_between_equ.title: Drupada tells his boyhood friend that kings have no poor friends
st.mbh.drupada_friendship_is_between_equ.lesson: Contempt shown to an old friend in need is remembered longer than any kindness, by both sides.
st.mbh.drupada_friendship_is_between_equ.summary: Drona and Drupada grew up studying together, and the prince once said that when he was king his kingdom would be Drona's too. Years later Drona, poor and with a family to feed, walks into the court and greets the king as "friend".

st.mbh.ekalavya_shut_out_and_self_taught.title: Ekalavya, refused as a student, teaches himself and pays for it
st.mbh.ekalavya_shut_out_and_self_taught.lesson: Faith and practice can make a master without anyone's permission, and a person's truthfulness remains theirs even when what is asked of them is harsh.
st.mbh.ekalavya_shut_out_and_self_taught.summary: Ekalavya, son of the Nishada chief, comes to the greatest teacher of the age and is not accepted, because of who his people are. He touches the teacher's feet, goes into the forest, shapes Drona's likeness from clay and practises before it with complete faith until his hand is faster than anyone's.

st.mbh.arjuna_sees_only_the_eye.title: Arjuna sees only the eye of the bird
st.mbh.arjuna_sees_only_the_eye.lesson: Skill is completed by attention that has narrowed to one point and holds nothing else.
st.mbh.arjuna_sees_only_the_eye.summary: Drona sets a wooden bird high in a tree and calls his students up one at a time, bow drawn. He asks each what they see. Each answers honestly: the tree, the bird, you, my brothers. Each is told to step aside without shooting.

st.mbh.arjuna_practises_in_the_dark.title: Arjuna notices his hand finds his mouth in the dark, and starts practising at night
st.mbh.arjuna_practises_in_the_dark.lesson: Mastery belongs to the one who turns an accident into a method and practises when no one requires it.
st.mbh.arjuna_practises_in_the_dark.summary: Drona has quietly told the cook never to serve Arjuna in the dark. One night the wind blows out the lamp while Arjuna is eating. He goes on eating and notices his hand reaching his mouth without any light, from habit alone.

st.mbh.karna_at_the_tournament.title: Karna is asked for his lineage and has no answer
st.mbh.karna_at_the_tournament.lesson: A person shut out for his birth will give everything to the one who first treats him as an equal.
st.mbh.karna_at_the_tournament.summary: Karna walks into the royal arena uninvited and matches every feat Arjuna has just performed. He challenges him to single combat. Then Kripa asks him to announce his mother, father and royal house, because princes do not duel men of unknown family. Karna's face falls like a lotus beaten down by rain.

st.mbh.karna_bows_to_adhiratha.title: Karna, minutes after being crowned, bows to the charioteer who raised him
st.mbh.karna_bows_to_adhiratha.lesson: Honouring the parents who raised you, at the moment the world is judging you by them, is its own nobility.
st.mbh.karna_bows_to_adhiratha.summary: Karna has just been made a king in front of the whole city. Into the arena comes an old man, sweating and trembling, leaning on a stick, his cloth slipping: Adhiratha the chariot driver, calling out "my son". Everyone now knows exactly where Karna comes from.

st.mbh.vidura_warns_in_code.title: Vidura warns Yudhishthira in words only he will understand
st.mbh.vidura_warns_in_code.lesson: When open opposition is impossible, the wise still find the act that protects, and say what must be said in the way it can be heard.
st.mbh.vidura_warns_in_code.summary: Dhritarashtra, pressed by his son, sends the Pandavas to a festival town where a house of lac and resin has been built to burn them. Vidura knows. He holds no power to stop it and cannot accuse the king's son openly. He has a few moments at the city gate, among a crowd, to say goodbye.

st.mbh.a_year_in_the_house_of_lac.title: The Pandavas live a year in a house they know is built to burn
st.mbh.a_year_in_the_house_of_lac.lesson: When you cannot yet leave a danger, live in it awake: show nothing, learn every exit and prepare your own.
st.mbh.a_year_in_the_house_of_lac.summary: Yudhishthira walks into the new mansion and smells ghee, lac and resin in the walls. He tells Bhima quietly that it is a firetrap and that their smiling host has been set to kill them. Bhima wants to leave at once or strike first.

st.mbh.bhima_keeps_watch_over_his_sleepi.title: Bhima watches his mother sleep on the bare ground
st.mbh.bhima_keeps_watch_over_his_sleepi.lesson: The one who carries everyone is allowed his grief, and keeps watch all the same.
st.mbh.bhima_keeps_watch_over_his_sleepi.summary: Bhima has carried his mother and four brothers on his body through the night, away from the fire. They collapse under a banyan tree and sleep. He fetches water and comes back to find them lying on the earth: his mother, sister of Vasudeva and queen of Pandu, who used to sleep on the finest beds.

st.mbh.hidimba_asks_kunti.title: Hidimba, an outsider, asks the mother for her son
st.mbh.hidimba_asks_kunti.lesson: One who has given up everything to come to you in good faith is to be received, not judged by where she came from.
st.mbh.hidimba_asks_kunti.summary: Hidimba is a rakshasi sent by her brother to kill the sleeping travellers. She sees Bhima and loves him at once. She warns him instead, her brother is killed in the fight, and now she stands before a human family that has every reason to fear and reject her. Bhima says rakshasas remember grudges and she should go the way of her brother.

st.mbh.brahmin_family_decides_who_will_g.title: A family argues over which of them will go to the demon
st.mbh.brahmin_family_decides_who_will_g.lesson: In a family's worst hour each one's love shows as readiness to take the blow, and rescue often comes from someone who simply overheard.
st.mbh.brahmin_family_decides_who_will_g.summary: In Ekachakra each household must in turn send one person with a cartload of food to the rakshasa Baka, who eats both. Tonight it is this family's turn. Through the wall Kunti hears them: the father cursing a life that is all sorrow, the mother insisting she must go, the daughter saying a girl is given away anyway, so let it be her.

st.mbh.kunti_offers_her_son_for_her_host.title: Kunti repays her hosts with the one thing she has
st.mbh.kunti_offers_her_son_for_her_host.lesson: A favour received is repaid in greater measure, and gratitude is shown in what you are willing to risk.
st.mbh.kunti_offers_her_son_for_her_host.summary: Kunti is a widow in hiding, living on alms in a stranger's house. Her hosts are in mortal trouble and she has no money or influence to offer. She does have five sons. She promises one of them to the demon before asking anyone.

st.mbh.vishvamitra_shame_on_this_power.title: Vishvamitra, a king with an army, is beaten by a sage and changes his life
st.mbh.vishvamitra_shame_on_this_power.lesson: Outer force meets its limit before inner power; seeing that clearly can turn a person toward a different kind of strength.
st.mbh.vishvamitra_shame_on_this_power.summary: King Vishvamitra, hunting with his army, is fed royally at Vasishtha's hermitage by the wish-giving cow Nandini. He wants her. He offers a fortune, is refused, and tries to take her by force. From the cow's body pour armies that scatter his own. The sage has not even stood up.

st.mbh.vasishtha_cannot_die_of_grief.title: Vasishtha, grieving a hundred sons, hears a voice behind him
st.mbh.vasishtha_cannot_die_of_grief.lesson: Even the wisest can be flattened by loss; what calls a person back is often a life that still depends on theirs.
st.mbh.vasishtha_cannot_die_of_grief.summary: Vasishtha learns that all his sons have been killed. He has the power to destroy the one responsible and does not use it. He bears the grief as the mountain bears the earth, and then cannot bear it. He throws himself from a peak, walks into fire, binds himself and enters a river in flood. Each time he is set down unharmed, and he returns to an empty hermitage.

st.mbh.aurva_puts_his_anger_in_the_ocean.title: Aurva is told to let go of a justified rage and asks where it should go
st.mbh.aurva_puts_his_anger_in_the_ocean.lesson: Anger born of real injustice is not to be suppressed into oneself or loosed on the world; it must be given a place where it does not destroy.
st.mbh.aurva_puts_his_anger_in_the_ocean.summary: Aurva was carried hidden in his mother's thigh while kings slaughtered his whole clan, down to the unborn, for their wealth. From the womb he heard his mothers scream and no one came. Now he is grown, and his austerity has kindled a fire that can burn the worlds. His dead ancestors appear and ask him to stop.

st.mbh.arjuna_unknown_at_the_svayamvara.title: Arjuna, in a beggar's deerskin, stands up where kings have failed
st.mbh.arjuna_unknown_at_the_svayamvara.lesson: What a person can do is not announced by their present circumstances.
st.mbh.arjuna_unknown_at_the_svayamvara.summary: The Pandavas are officially dead, living as begging brahmins. At Draupadi's svayamvara the great kings of the earth strain at the bow and are flung to the ground. Then a young man in deerskin rises from among the brahmins. Some of them wave their skins and cheer. Others mutter that he will make all brahmins a laughing stock.

st.mbh.drupada_who_took_my_daughter.title: Drupada does not know who has taken his daughter home
st.mbh.drupada_who_took_my_daughter.lesson: A parent's fear for a child's choice is best met by finding out who the person is, from how they live.
st.mbh.drupada_who_took_my_daughter.summary: Drupada held the contest hoping Arjuna would somehow appear. Instead his daughter has walked off behind two unknown men in deerskin to a potter's hut. He sits in his palace sick with worry: has she gone to a low man, has a foot been set on his head, has a garland been thrown on a cremation ground?

st.mbh.given_the_wasteland.title: The Pandavas are given the barren half and build a city on it
st.mbh.given_the_wasteland.lesson: What is given grudgingly can be made great by those who put their effort into building it.
st.mbh.given_the_wasteland.summary: The Pandavas return alive and married into a powerful house, and the court has to give them something. Bhishma, Drona and Vidura argue for their rightful half. Dhritarashtra agrees, and gives them Khandavaprastha: forest and wilderness, far from the capital, "so that there may be no quarrel again".

st.mbh.sunda_upasunda_and_the_rule.title: Two inseparable brothers destroy each other, and five brothers make a rule
st.mbh.sunda_upasunda_and_the_rule.lesson: Those who are closest should set their boundaries before a conflict of desire tests them.
st.mbh.sunda_upasunda_and_the_rule.summary: Narada visits the newly settled Pandavas, who share one wife, and tells them of Sunda and Upasunda: brothers who shared one kingdom, one bed, one plate and one will, who could be killed by no one but each other. The gods sent Tilottama. Each took one of her hands and said "she is mine".

st.mbh.arjuna_will_not_take_the_loophole.title: Arjuna breaks a rule for a good reason and refuses to be excused
st.mbh.arjuna_will_not_take_the_loophole.lesson: Dharma is not to be kept through a technicality; whoever breaks an agreement for a good reason still honours its price.
st.mbh.arjuna_will_not_take_the_loophole.summary: A brahmin runs to Arjuna crying that thieves are driving off his cattle. Arjuna's weapons are in the room where Yudhishthira is sitting with Draupadi, and entering means twelve years of exile by the brothers' own rule. If he does not enter, a man who asked for protection goes unprotected.

st.mbh.jarita_and_her_fledglings_in_the_.title: Jarita and her four chicks in the burning forest
st.mbh.jarita_and_her_fledglings_in_the_.lesson: Sometimes love means letting the other go to safety, and trusting what cannot be controlled.
st.mbh.jarita_and_her_fledglings_in_the_.summary: The Khandava forest is on fire. Jarita, a mother bird, has four chicks too young to fly, and their father left some time ago for another mate. She cannot carry all four. She runs through the choices aloud: cover them with her body, take one, hide them in a rat hole.

st.mbh.narada_asks_do_you.title: Narada asks the new king a hundred questions beginning "do you"
st.mbh.narada_asks_do_you.lesson: The time to examine how you are running your life is when everything is going well.
st.mbh.narada_asks_do_you.summary: Yudhishthira has a new hall, a new kingdom and everyone's praise. Narada arrives and, instead of congratulating him, asks question after question. Do you divide your time between dharma, wealth and pleasure? Do you wake in the last watch and think about what must be done? Are your workers paid on time? Do you see to the widows, the old, the farmers?

st.mbh.yudhishthira_asks_krishna_for_the.title: Yudhishthira distrusts the yes of everyone around him and sends for Krishna
st.mbh.yudhishthira_asks_krishna_for_the.lesson: Before a great undertaking, seek the one counsellor who has no reason to flatter you, and hear the obstacle named.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_asks_krishna_for_the.summary: Yudhishthira is urged to perform the Rajasuya, the rite of an emperor. His brothers, ministers and priests all say he is worthy and able. He keeps turning it over and is not convinced, because he knows why people say yes to a king.

st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hundred_offences.title: Krishna bears a hundred insults because he promised, and then stops
st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hundred_offences.lesson: Forbearance is a strength when it is chosen and has a limit; the limit, once reached, is to be stated and held.
st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hundred_offences.summary: At the great sacrifice Krishna is chosen for the first honour. His cousin Shishupala stands up and pours out years of grudge in front of every king: Krishna is no king, no elder, no priest, a cowherd. He insults Bhishma for proposing him and the Pandavas for agreeing. Krishna sits and lets him speak.

st.mbh.duryodhana_falls_in_the_pool.title: Duryodhana walks into a wall and falls into a pool while his cousins' household laughs
st.mbh.duryodhana_falls_in_the_pool.lesson: A small humiliation, replayed and fed, grows into a grievance large enough to justify anything.
st.mbh.duryodhana_falls_in_the_pool.summary: Duryodhana stays on as a guest to look around his cousins' new hall. He takes a crystal floor for water and lifts his clothes. He takes a pool for a floor and falls in fully dressed. He walks into a closed crystal door and stretches his hands toward an open one. Each time, people laugh, and the servants bring him dry clothes at the king's order.

st.mbh.duryodhana_names_his_envy.title: Duryodhana, who has everything, tells his father he cannot bear what his cousins have
st.mbh.duryodhana_names_his_envy.lesson: Envy makes a person poor in the middle of plenty, and it will dress itself as ambition if you let it.
st.mbh.duryodhana_names_his_envy.summary: Duryodhana is a prince with a kingdom, wealth, fine clothes and food, and he is thin, pale and sleepless. His father asks what he could possibly lack. He answers that he eats and dresses like any ordinary man, and that he has seen Yudhishthira's fortune: kings waiting at the gate with tribute, a hundred thousand fed on gold plates.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_knows_and_gives_in.title: Dhritarashtra sees the dice game is wrong, is warned, and orders it anyway
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_knows_and_gives_in.lesson: Calling a choice fate, because refusing a loved one is painful, is how the clear-sighted go wrong.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_knows_and_gives_in.summary: Dhritarashtra's son wants a gambling match with a master cheat on his side. The king says he must ask Vidura. Duryodhana replies that Vidura will talk him out of it, and that if it is refused he will die. Vidura comes and tells him plainly that this game will split the family.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_goes_to_the_game.title: Yudhishthira knows the game is a trap and goes because he was called
st.mbh.yudhishthira_goes_to_the_game.lesson: A rule kept without discernment can deliver you to those who know your rule.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_goes_to_the_game.summary: Vidura arrives with the invitation and tells Yudhishthira the truth: he does not approve, and there are cheats waiting. Yudhishthira says gambling breeds quarrel and he has no wish to play. He also holds a vow never to refuse when challenged, and the summons comes from the king who stands as his father.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_cannot_stop.title: Yudhishthira loses, stakes more, and loses his brothers, himself and his wife
st.mbh.yudhishthira_cannot_stop.lesson: In the grip of a game, each loss argues for one more throw, and a person will stake what was never theirs to stake.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_cannot_stop.summary: Yudhishthira stakes a necklace and loses. He stakes gold, chariots, elephants, servants, his army, his treasury, his cities. After every throw Shakuni says the same word: won. Each loss becomes the reason for the next stake, which will win it all back.

st.mbh.vidura_told_to_leave_for_speaking.title: Vidura speaks up mid-game and is called a snake in the house
st.mbh.vidura_told_to_leave_for_speaking.lesson: The adviser who says what is true and unwelcome is rare, and so is the one who can hear him.
st.mbh.vidura_told_to_leave_for_speaking.summary: Halfway through the game Vidura stands and addresses the king in front of everyone. He says Duryodhana howled like a jackal at birth and should be given up for the family's sake, that they are milking a cow to death, that the Pandavas are worth more as friends than their wealth is as winnings. Duryodhana turns on him.

st.mbh.draupadi_asks_her_question.title: Draupadi, dragged into the hall, asks a question no elder will answer
st.mbh.draupadi_asks_her_question.lesson: Where a person is wronged in public and those with authority stay silent, the silence is itself the adharma.
st.mbh.draupadi_asks_her_question.summary: Draupadi is in her private rooms, in a single garment, when a messenger says she has been won at dice. She sends him back with a question. Then Duhshasana drags her by the hair into the full assembly, where her husbands sit with lowered heads and her elders, teachers and father-in-law look on.

st.mbh.vikarna_stands_up.title: Vikarna, the youngest in the room, says what the elders will not
st.mbh.vikarna_stands_up.lesson: When those with rank stay silent, the one who sees clearly must speak, whatever his place.
st.mbh.vikarna_stands_up.summary: Draupadi's question hangs in the hall. Bhishma has declined to rule. Drona, Kripa and the king are silent. Vikarna is one of Duryodhana's own younger brothers, with no standing to speak before his elders, and he can see that no one is going to.

st.mbh.bhishma_cannot_answer.title: Bhishma, who knows the law better than anyone, says he cannot decide
st.mbh.bhishma_cannot_answer.lesson: Learning and good character do not by themselves produce the courage to rule against those you serve.
st.mbh.bhishma_cannot_answer.summary: Bhishma is the grandfather of both sides, the guardian of the throne and the highest living authority on dharma. His granddaughter-in-law stands before him, dishevelled and held by the hair, and asks him directly whether she has been lawfully won.

st.mbh.vidura_on_the_silent_witness.title: Vidura tells the hall that those who watch and say nothing share the wrong
st.mbh.vidura_on_the_silent_witness.lesson: A witness who knows what is right and stays silent takes a share of the wrong.
st.mbh.vidura_on_the_silent_witness.summary: Vikarna has been shouted down and the garment is being pulled. Vidura raises his arms for silence and addresses the kings who are watching. Draupadi has asked her question and is weeping like one with no protector, he says, and you do not answer.

st.mbh.draupadi_takes_only_two_boons.title: Draupadi is offered anything and asks only for her husbands' freedom
st.mbh.draupadi_takes_only_two_boons.lesson: Dignity takes what is right and no more, and trusts its own strength for the rest.
st.mbh.draupadi_takes_only_two_boons.summary: Frightened by the omens, the old king finally speaks to Draupadi and tells her to choose a boon. Minutes ago she was being called a slave. Now she can ask for the kingdom, the wealth, revenge, anything.

st.mbh.bhima_rages_at_his_own_brother.title: Bhima wants to burn the hands of the brother who gambled them away
st.mbh.bhima_rages_at_his_own_brother.lesson: Anger at one's own who caused the harm is real; do not let it serve the purpose of those who set the trap.
st.mbh.bhima_rages_at_his_own_brother.summary: Bhima sits in the hall as a slave, watching his wife dragged in. The man who caused it is the elder brother he has obeyed all his life. Gamblers keep women in their houses, Bhima says, and do not stake even them. You staked her.

st.mbh.called_back_for_one_more_throw.title: Freed and on the road home, Yudhishthira is called back for one last throw
st.mbh.called_back_for_one_more_throw.lesson: Having escaped once is no protection against going back; the pull returns wearing the face of obligation.
st.mbh.called_back_for_one_more_throw.summary: The Pandavas have left with everything restored. Duryodhana tells his father they will come back armed and angry, and asks for one more game with a single stake: the loser goes to the forest for twelve years and lives a thirteenth unrecognised. A messenger overtakes Yudhishthira on the road.

st.mbh.kunti_watches_them_leave.title: Kunti watches her sons and daughter-in-law walk into exile
st.mbh.kunti_watches_them_leave.lesson: A parent's part, when the children must go, is to bless them truthfully and bear the waiting.
st.mbh.kunti_watches_them_leave.summary: Kunti is too old for the forest, so Vidura will keep her in his house. She watches her five sons leave in deerskins, heads down, mocked by Duhshasana. Draupadi comes to take her leave in a single stained garment with her hair loose.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_drives_vidura_away.title: Dhritarashtra drives his brother away in anger and cannot breathe until he is back
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_drives_vidura_away.lesson: A man may drive away in anger the person he most relies on; remorse can bring the person back, but only listening changes the course.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_drives_vidura_away.summary: The Pandavas have just left for the forest and the city is muttering. Dhritarashtra asks Vidura what to do, and Vidura gives the same answer as always: return what was taken and restrain your son. The king loses his temper. You always speak for them, he says, I have had enough of you, go or stay as you please.

st.mbh.draupadi_why_no_anger.title: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
st.mbh.draupadi_why_no_anger.lesson: Anger rarely heals anything; forgiveness has limits. Wisdom is knowing which a moment needs.
st.mbh.draupadi_why_no_anger.summary: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_dharma_not_a_trade.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
st.mbh.yudhishthira_dharma_not_a_trade.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_dharma_not_a_trade.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.

st.mbh.bhima_count_the_months_as_years.title: Bhima cannot bear to wait thirteen years
st.mbh.bhima_count_the_months_as_years.lesson: A pledge is not broken by a clever reading of it; time that must be waited out can be spent getting ready.
st.mbh.bhima_count_the_months_as_years.summary: Bhima is sick of waiting. The years we wait, he tells Yudhishthira, are years off our lives, and death does not pause for a pledge. He even offers a scholar's loophole: the texts allow a substitute, so count the thirteen months we have already lived here as thirteen years, and let us go and fight now.

st.mbh.arjuna_beaten_by_the_hunter.title: Arjuna, the best archer alive, is beaten by a mountain hunter
st.mbh.arjuna_beaten_by_the_hunter.lesson: When every skill one has fails, the one we face may be the very one we came to meet; surrender to him is not defeat.
st.mbh.arjuna_beaten_by_the_hunter.summary: After months of austerity Arjuna shoots a charging boar at the same moment as a hunter from the hills. He insults the man for breaking the rule of the hunt. The hunter laughs, and then swallows every arrow Arjuna shoots, takes the inexhaustible quivers, takes Gandiva itself, and in the end crushes Arjuna in a wrestling hold until he falls senseless.

st.mbh.arjuna_refuses_urvashi.title: Arjuna refuses Urvashi in Indra's heaven and is cursed for it
st.mbh.arjuna_refuses_urvashi.lesson: A boundary rooted in one's own dharma may be kept courteously and completely, even against a powerful person, even at a cost.
st.mbh.arjuna_refuses_urvashi.summary: In Indra's heaven Arjuna is the honoured guest. One night Urvashi, the most celebrated of the apsaras, comes to his rooms with Indra's blessing. Arjuna lowers his eyes and greets her as an elder: she was the wife of Pururavas, the founder of his line, and to him she stands in the place of a mother.

st.mbh.is_anyone_unluckier_than_me.title: Nala and Damayanti
st.mbh.is_anyone_unluckier_than_me.lesson: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
st.mbh.is_anyone_unluckier_than_me.summary: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

st.mbh.nala_leaves_her_sleeping.title: Nala and Damayanti
st.mbh.nala_leaves_her_sleeping.lesson: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
st.mbh.nala_leaves_her_sleeping.summary: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

st.mbh.damayanti_alone_sets_her_terms.title: Nala and Damayanti
st.mbh.damayanti_alone_sets_her_terms.lesson: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
st.mbh.damayanti_alone_sets_her_terms.summary: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

st.mbh.nala_as_bahuka.title: Nala and Damayanti
st.mbh.nala_as_bahuka.lesson: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
st.mbh.nala_as_bahuka.summary: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

st.mbh.ashtavakra_cursed_for_correcting_.title: Ashtavakra at Janaka's court
st.mbh.ashtavakra_cursed_for_correcting_.lesson: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.
st.mbh.ashtavakra_cursed_for_correcting_.summary: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.

st.mbh.ashtavakra_too_young_at_the_door.title: Ashtavakra at Janaka's court
st.mbh.ashtavakra_too_young_at_the_door.lesson: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.
st.mbh.ashtavakra_too_young_at_the_door.summary: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.

st.mbh.yavakrita_and_the_sand_dam.title: Yavakrita wants the Vedas without a teacher, and finds Indra building a dam of sand
st.mbh.yavakrita_and_the_sand_dam.lesson: Learning taken by force, without a teacher and the time it needs, breeds pride instead of wisdom.
st.mbh.yavakrita_and_the_sand_dam.summary: Yavakrita sees his father Bharadvaja, an ascetic, go unhonoured while their neighbour Raibhya and his learned sons are honoured by everyone. Stung, he decides to get the Vedas the fast way: by fierce austerity, without a teacher. Indra comes and tells him that the Vedas can only be got from a teacher's mouth over a long time. He refuses and doubles his austerity.

st.mbh.shibi_and_the_dove.title: King Shibi and the dove
st.mbh.shibi_and_the_dove.lesson: When duties collide, weigh them honestly, and keep your word to those who trust you.
st.mbh.shibi_and_the_dove.summary: A frightened dove flies to King Shibi for refuge; a hawk demands it back as its rightful food. Shibi offers the hawk anything else, finally his own flesh weighed against the dove, and climbs onto the scale himself. The birds reveal themselves as gods.

st.mbh.bhima_cannot_lift_the_tail.title: Bhima meets Hanuman
st.mbh.bhima_cannot_lift_the_tail.lesson: Strength without humility is blind. The one blocking your path may be family.
st.mbh.bhima_cannot_lift_the_tail.summary: Searching for a flower for Draupadi, mighty Bhima finds an old monkey blocking the path and orders it to move. Told to lift its tail himself, he cannot budge it. The monkey is his elder brother Hanuman, who embraces him and teaches him.

st.mbh.bhima_in_the_pythons_grip.title: Nahusha the python and Yudhishthira's answers
st.mbh.bhima_in_the_pythons_grip.lesson: Success can blind anyone. What makes a person good is conduct, not birth.
st.mbh.bhima_in_the_pythons_grip.summary: A giant python seizes Bhima. It is King Nahusha, once lord of heaven, cursed for making sages carry his palanquin. He frees Bhima after Yudhishthira answers his questions on goodness, and is freed himself.

st.mbh.markandeya_finds_the_child.title: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf
st.mbh.markandeya_finds_the_child.lesson: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
st.mbh.markandeya_finds_the_child.summary: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.

st.mbh.kaushika_and_the_housewife.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
st.mbh.kaushika_and_the_housewife.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.
st.mbh.kaushika_and_the_housewife.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.

st.mbh.dharmavyadha_sends_him_home.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
st.mbh.dharmavyadha_sends_him_home.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.
st.mbh.dharmavyadha_sends_him_home.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.

st.mbh.mudgala_declines_heaven.title: Mudgala, who lives on gleaned grain, is offered heaven and asks what is wrong with it
st.mbh.mudgala_declines_heaven.lesson: A peace that does not change when everything is taken is worth more than any reward that can run out.
st.mbh.mudgala_declines_heaven.summary: Mudgala lives with his wife and son on grain gleaned from the fields after harvest, a measure gathered over two weeks. Each fortnight he feeds guests first. Durvasa, naked and acting like a madman, arrives at mealtime and eats everything, and smears the rest on himself. He comes back six fortnights in a row. Mudgala's family goes hungry each time.

st.mbh.draupadi_and_the_empty_pot.title: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens
st.mbh.draupadi_and_the_empty_pot.lesson: When you have nothing left to offer, calling out is enough; help can come from a single leaf.
st.mbh.draupadi_and_the_empty_pot.summary: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.

st.mbh.draupadi_no_one_is_mine.title: Draupadi tells Krishna her sorrow
st.mbh.draupadi_no_one_is_mine.lesson: You can bring God your rawest pain, even your sense of being abandoned, and be heard.
st.mbh.draupadi_no_one_is_mine.summary: Krishna visits the exiled Pandavas in the Kamyaka forest and tells Arjuna 'you are mine and I am yours'. Draupadi then comes to him 'seeking refuge with the refuge', tells him, out of closeness, everything done to her in the dice-hall and since, and weeps that she has no one, not even him. Krishna promises she will see justice.

st.mbh.duryodhana_goes_to_gloat.title: Duryodhana goes to the forest to show off, and is taken prisoner
st.mbh.duryodhana_goes_to_gloat.lesson: Prosperity paraded to wound others carries its owner into disgrace.
st.mbh.duryodhana_goes_to_gloat.summary: Karna and Shakuni urge Duryodhana: go to the forest where the Pandavas live, in all your splendour, and let them see you, like the sun scorching them. The excuse is an inspection of the royal cattle herds. Duryodhana sets out with his brothers, his queens and an army.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_rescues_his_enemy.title: Yudhishthira sends his brothers to rescue the cousin who exiled them
st.mbh.yudhishthira_rescues_his_enemy.lesson: Between ourselves we may be divided; against outsiders the family stands together, and helping a fallen enemy is a greater deed than winning a kingdom.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_rescues_his_enemy.summary: Duryodhana's ministers come running: the gandharvas have taken the king and the Kuru women. Bhima is delighted: the gandharvas have done our work for us; he came here to mock us and got what he deserved. Yudhishthira stops him.

st.mbh.duryodhana_cannot_bear_being_save.title: Rescued by the people he hates, Duryodhana decides he would rather die
st.mbh.duryodhana_cannot_bear_being_save.lesson: Envy can make being helped by a rival feel worse than death; such shame, unexamined, feeds the very feud that caused it.
st.mbh.duryodhana_cannot_bear_being_save.summary: Freed by the Pandavas and politely sent home, Duryodhana walks away with his head down, as if his insides were being torn. On the road he tells Karna: when the gandharva said who I was, I wanted the earth to open. I have been saved by those I always scorned and treated as enemies; they gave me my life. Death in battle would have been better.

st.mbh.draupadi_pushes_jayadratha.title: Alone at the hermitage, Draupadi refuses a king and knocks him down
st.mbh.draupadi_pushes_jayadratha.lesson: A woman alone may meet a powerful man's entitlement with plain rebuke and force, and the truth of her own conduct is her strength.
st.mbh.draupadi_pushes_jayadratha.summary: The Pandavas are out hunting and Draupadi is alone at the hermitage with the priest Dhaumya. Jayadratha, king of Sindhu and husband of Duryodhana's sister, passes with his army, sees her and sends a man to ask who she is. She receives him as a guest, offers food, and says her husbands will be back soon. He tells her to leave those beggared exiles and come be his queen.

st.mbh.savitri_chooses_with_open_eyes.title: Savitri and Satyavan
st.mbh.savitri_chooses_with_open_eyes.lesson: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.
st.mbh.savitri_chooses_with_open_eyes.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.

st.mbh.savitri_follows_yama.title: Savitri and Satyavan
st.mbh.savitri_follows_yama.lesson: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.
st.mbh.savitri_follows_yama.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.

st.mbh.karna_gives_his_armour.title: Karna is warned in a dream and gives away his armour anyway
st.mbh.karna_gives_his_armour.lesson: For a person whose word is his self, keeping it is worth more than the protection breaking it would bring.
st.mbh.karna_gives_his_armour.summary: Karna was born with armour and earrings grown from his body; while he wears them he cannot be killed. Surya comes to him in a dream: Indra will come disguised as a brahmin to beg for them, for Arjuna's sake. Do not give them. Karna's vow is known to everyone: he never refuses a brahmin who asks.

st.mbh.kunti_sets_the_basket_adrift.title: Kunti, an unmarried girl, sets her newborn son adrift on the river
st.mbh.kunti_sets_the_basket_adrift.lesson: A mother may let a child go out of fear and still bless him with her whole heart; the secret, kept, does not stop costing.
st.mbh.kunti_sets_the_basket_adrift.summary: Kunti is a girl in her father's house, given a mantra to call any god. Out of curiosity she tries it on the Sun. He comes and will not leave without a son; he warns her that if he goes back with nothing, he will burn her father and the brahmin who gave her the mantra. A child is born, with armour and earrings like the sun. She is still unmarried and terrified of disgrace.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_at_the_lake.title: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
st.mbh.yudhishthira_at_the_lake.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_at_the_lake.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_chooses_nakula.title: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
st.mbh.yudhishthira_chooses_nakula.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_chooses_nakula.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.

st.mbh.arjuna_chooses_krishna_unarmed.title: Offered an army or one unarmed friend, Arjuna chooses the friend
st.mbh.arjuna_chooses_krishna_unarmed.lesson: One trusted guide who will stand beside you is worth more than numbers that will only fight for you.
st.mbh.arjuna_chooses_krishna_unarmed.summary: Both sides go to Dvaraka to ask Krishna for help. Krishna is asleep. Duryodhana arrives first and takes the seat at the head of the bed; Arjuna comes in after and stands at his feet with folded hands. When Krishna wakes he sees Arjuna first.

st.mbh.shalya_bound_by_hospitality.title: Shalya comes to help one side and is bound to the other by its hospitality
st.mbh.shalya_bound_by_hospitality.lesson: Favours received unawares can bind a person to a side he did not choose; once bound, he serves divided.
st.mbh.shalya_bound_by_hospitality.summary: Shalya, king of Madra and the twins' maternal uncle, sets out with his army to join the Pandavas. All along the road he finds beautiful rest-houses with food, wells and servants waiting for him. Pleased, he asks whose men built them, so he can reward them; Yudhishthira's, he assumes. Duryodhana steps out: they were mine. Grant me a boon. Lead my army.

st.mbh.shachi_and_nahusha.title: Shachi is pursued by the new king of heaven, and the gods tell her to go to him
st.mbh.shachi_and_nahusha.lesson: One who comes for refuge must not be given up to keep peace with the powerful; a harasser drunk on power can be undone by his own arrogance.
st.mbh.shachi_and_nahusha.summary: Indra has gone into hiding and the gods have made the mortal king Nahusha ruler of heaven. Power goes to his head. He demands Indra's wife: let Shachi come to my house today. Shachi, frightened, goes to Brihaspati, the gods' teacher: protect me, I have come to you for refuge.

st.mbh.five_villages.title: Yudhishthira's case for peace
st.mbh.five_villages.lesson: Winning a feud still costs you peace. Hostility only ends when someone stops feeding it.
st.mbh.five_villages.summary: Before Krishna sets out as peace envoy, Yudhishthira opens his heart: poverty humiliates, greed corrodes, victory breeds enmity, and hostility is never ended by hostility. He asks only for five villages.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_sleep.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_sleep.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_sleep.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.

st.mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness_is_death.title: Sanatsujatiya: the sage on death and the self
st.mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness_is_death.lesson: Carelessness is the real death. Stay awake to your life and be who you are.
st.mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness_is_death.summary: At Vidura's request the ancient sage Sanatsujata answers Dhritarashtra's fear of death. Death, he says, is heedlessness; desire drags us down; pretending to be what we are not is self-theft.

st.mbh.krishna_goes_knowing_it_will_fail.title: Krishna's peace embassy to the Kauravas
st.mbh.krishna_goes_knowing_it_will_fail.lesson: You can make the best case for peace and still be refused. Speak anyway.
st.mbh.krishna_goes_knowing_it_will_fail.summary: Krishna travels to Hastinapura to plead for peace between the cousins. Elders, sages and finally Gandhari urge Duryodhana to share the kingdom; he refuses, even plotting to seize Krishna, and war becomes certain.

st.mbh.draupadi_shows_her_hair.title: Before the peace mission, Draupadi holds up her hair: remember this
st.mbh.draupadi_shows_her_hair.lesson: When others speak of making peace, the one who was wronged has the right to be remembered first.
st.mbh.draupadi_shows_her_hair.summary: Everyone is speaking of peace: Yudhishthira wants it, and even Bhima, to everyone's surprise, has spoken gently. Krishna is about to leave for Hastinapura. Draupadi takes her long dark hair in her left hand, the hair Duhshasana dragged her by, and comes to him with her eyes full of tears.

st.mbh.not_a_needles_point.title: Duryodhana will not give up as much land as a needle's point
st.mbh.not_a_needles_point.lesson: One who would rather break than bend, and will not yield even a needle's point, brings ruin on himself and all who follow him.
st.mbh.not_a_needles_point.summary: In the full assembly Krishna has made the case for peace, and Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and his own father have urged Duryodhana to accept it. He answers that he has done nothing wrong; the Pandavas lost at dice by their own choice. The share his father once gave them was given when he was a child, out of ignorance or fear. It will not be given again while he lives.

st.mbh.gandhari_speaks_to_her_son.title: Gandhari counsels her son
st.mbh.gandhari_speaks_to_her_son.lesson: Master yourself first. Greed never made anyone rich, and indulgent parents share the blame.
st.mbh.gandhari_speaks_to_her_son.summary: Summoned to the court, Queen Gandhari first blames her husband for indulging their son, then tells Duryodhana that whoever cannot rule himself cannot rule a kingdom, and that half the earth is enough.

st.mbh.vidula_rouses_her_son.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
st.mbh.vidula_rouses_her_son.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
st.mbh.vidula_rouses_her_son.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.

st.mbh.krishna_offers_karna_the_throne.title: Krishna tells Karna who he is and offers him the throne
st.mbh.krishna_offers_karna_the_throne.lesson: Loyalty to those who raised and stood by you outweighs a birthright offered too late.
st.mbh.krishna_offers_karna_the_throne.summary: Leaving Hastinapura after the failed embassy, Krishna takes Karna into his chariot and tells him the secret: you are Kunti's son, born before her marriage; by law you are Pandu's eldest. Come with me. The Pandavas will touch your feet, Draupadi will honour you, you will be crowned king, and Yudhishthira will hold the umbrella over you.

st.mbh.kunti_meets_karna.title: Kunti comes to Karna at the river, and he tells her what she did
st.mbh.kunti_meets_karna.lesson: One who was abandoned may name the wrong in full and still be generous; loyalty to those who stood by him is not betrayal of the one who did not.
st.mbh.kunti_meets_karna.summary: On the eve of war Kunti goes alone to the bank of the Ganga where Karna prays to the sun. She waits behind him in the heat until he finishes. He turns, sees her, and says: I am Karna, son of Radha and Adhiratha. What can I do for you? She tells him: you are my son, born in my father's house, with armour and earrings. Come to your brothers.

st.mbh.amba_turned_away_by_everyone.title: Amba is taken by force, released, and then refused by everyone
st.mbh.amba_turned_away_by_everyone.lesson: When each person's rule adds up to another's ruin, she may name every one of them and seek redress.
st.mbh.amba_turned_away_by_everyone.summary: Amba, eldest princess of Kashi, has given her heart to King Shalva and was about to choose him at her svayamvara when Bhishma carried her and her sisters off for his half-brother. In Hastinapura she tells Bhishma she loves Shalva, and he lets her go to him. Shalva says: go back to Bhishma. I do not want a woman Bhishma took by force.

st.mbh.amba_will_not_turn_back.title: Amba refuses to be talked out of her resolve
st.mbh.amba_will_not_turn_back.lesson: A wronged person's resolve, held through every refusal and failure, may be granted by the gods themselves.
st.mbh.amba_will_not_turn_back.summary: Parashurama, the greatest warrior-sage alive, has fought Bhishma for twenty-three days and failed. He tells Amba to take refuge with Bhishma. She will not. I will go where Bhishma is, she says, and bring him down myself. She goes into the forest by the Yamuna and does austerities beyond human measure: without food, thin, matted, for six months living on air.

st.mbh.pandavas_choose_their_disguises.title: Five princes and a queen choose the humble jobs they will live in for a year
st.mbh.pandavas_choose_their_disguises.lesson: When circumstances force one into a humbler role, choose the one your real skills can serve, and live it fully until the time is complete.
st.mbh.pandavas_choose_their_disguises.summary: The twelve years of forest are over; now comes the thirteenth, which must be lived in a city without being recognised, or the exile starts again. Yudhishthira asks each brother in turn what work he will do in King Virata's court. He grieves at each answer: how will Bhima, who never served anyone, cook for a king? How will Draupadi, a queen, serve as a maid?

st.mbh.dhaumya_how_to_live_in_a_kings_ho.title: Dhaumya teaches the Pandavas how to work in another man's court
st.mbh.dhaumya_how_to_live_in_a_kings_ho.lesson: In another's house be discreet, speak when asked, never presume, and keep what you learn to yourself.
st.mbh.dhaumya_how_to_live_in_a_kings_ho.summary: The Pandavas have only ever been masters. Now they must serve a king who must not guess who they are. Their priest Dhaumya, before they go in, sits them down and teaches them how a person lives safely in the service of a powerful man.

st.mbh.sairandhri_kicked_before_the_cour.title: Draupadi, harassed by the commander, is kicked in front of the king, and no one moves
st.mbh.sairandhri_kicked_before_the_cour.lesson: A court whose king will not protect the weak is no court; one who is wronged in public may say so to everyone present.
st.mbh.sairandhri_kicked_before_the_cour.summary: Kichaka, the queen's brother and commander of the army, has been pressing himself on the maid Sairandhri. The queen, his sister, sends her to his house to fetch wine. He grabs her; she breaks free and runs into the king's hall. He chases her and, in front of the king and the court, knocks her down and kicks her.

st.mbh.draupadi_wakes_bhima_in_the_kitch.title: Draupadi goes to the kitchen at night and wakes the one who will act
st.mbh.draupadi_wakes_bhima_in_the_kitch.lesson: When those responsible will not act, the wronged may go to the one who will, and act with a plan.
st.mbh.draupadi_wakes_bhima_in_the_kitch.summary: After the hall, she cannot sleep. At night she goes to the palace kitchen where Bhima sleeps, wakes him and holds him, and pours it out: what she has suffered since the dice game, and now this. She says she cannot bear to live like this; serving, grinding sandalwood with blistered hands, frightened of Kichaka every day.

st.mbh.uttara_boasts_and_runs.title: Prince Uttara boasts in front of the women, then sees the army and runs
st.mbh.uttara_boasts_and_runs.lesson: Fear can undo the boaster; the right companion turns panic into a task one can do.
st.mbh.uttara_boasts_and_runs.summary: The Kurus raid Virata's cattle while the king and his army are away. The young prince Uttara, left in the city, tells the women he would defeat the whole Kuru army himself, if only he had a proper charioteer. Sairandhri says Brihannala, the dance teacher, once drove for Arjuna. So the prince rides out with Brihannala at the reins, boasting all the way.

st.mbh.kanka_struck_with_the_dice.title: The king throws the dice in Yudhishthira's face, and he catches the blood
st.mbh.kanka_struck_with_the_dice.lesson: Holding back in the moment of injury can protect others from a greater harm; truth comes out, and the one who struck apologises.
st.mbh.kanka_struck_with_the_dice.summary: Virata comes home and hears that his son has beaten the Kurus. Overjoyed, he plays dice with Kanka and keeps praising Uttara. Kanka says quietly: with Brihannala driving him, how could he not win? The king, enraged that a eunuch is praised beside his son, throws the dice in Kanka's face. Blood runs from his nose.

st.mbh.arjuna_will_not_marry_his_student.title: Arjuna refuses to marry the princess he taught, and protects her name
st.mbh.arjuna_will_not_marry_his_student.lesson: One who has been trusted as a teacher must protect that trust, even by refusing what is offered.
st.mbh.arjuna_will_not_marry_his_student.summary: The Pandavas have revealed themselves. Virata, grateful and ashamed, offers his daughter Uttara to Arjuna in marriage. Arjuna, as Brihannala, has spent a year in the women's quarters teaching her dance and music.

st.mbh.krishna_left_mathura.title: Krishna tells Yudhishthira how his people abandoned their city to a stronger enemy
st.mbh.krishna_left_mathura.lesson: When an enemy cannot be beaten now, it is wise to withdraw, rebuild, and return when the time and means are right.
st.mbh.krishna_left_mathura.summary: Yudhishthira wants to perform the royal sacrifice and asks Krishna's honest advice. Krishna tells him that Jarasandha of Magadha stands in the way, and tells him a story of his own clan: Jarasandha attacked Mathura again and again; we fought him off many times, but we saw we could not finally defeat him and his allies. So the Yadavas left Mathura and went west to build Dvaraka.

st.bg.dhritarashtra_mine_and_pandus.title: The great warriors of both armies are named
st.bg.dhritarashtra_mine_and_pandus.lesson: Insecurity shows in how we size up rivals before anything has happened.
st.bg.dhritarashtra_mine_and_pandus.summary: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened at Kurukshetra. Sanjaya describes Duryodhana going to Drona and nervously naming the great warriors on both sides.

st.bg.duryodhana_counts_the_enemy.title: The great warriors of both armies are named
st.bg.duryodhana_counts_the_enemy.lesson: Insecurity shows in how we size up rivals before anything has happened.
st.bg.duryodhana_counts_the_enemy.summary: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened at Kurukshetra. Sanjaya describes Duryodhana going to Drona and nervously naming the great warriors on both sides.

st.bg.arjuna_collapse_between_armies.title: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
st.bg.arjuna_collapse_between_armies.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
st.bg.arjuna_collapse_between_armies.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.

st.bg.arjuna_i_will_not_fight.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
st.bg.arjuna_i_will_not_fight.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
st.bg.arjuna_i_will_not_fight.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.

st.bg.arjuna_i_am_your_student.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
st.bg.arjuna_i_am_your_student.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
st.bg.arjuna_i_am_your_student.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.

st.bg.arjuna_mixed_messages.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
st.bg.arjuna_mixed_messages.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.
st.bg.arjuna_mixed_messages.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.

st.bg.arjuna_what_drives_wrong.title: Restraining desire
st.bg.arjuna_what_drives_wrong.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.
st.bg.arjuna_what_drives_wrong.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.

st.bg.arjuna_mind_like_wind.title: Mastering the mind
st.bg.arjuna_mind_like_wind.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.
st.bg.arjuna_mind_like_wind.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.

st.bg.arjuna_what_if_i_fail.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
st.bg.arjuna_what_if_i_fail.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.
st.bg.arjuna_what_if_i_fail.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.

st.bg.arjuna_sees_and_is_afraid.title: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
st.bg.arjuna_sees_and_is_afraid.lesson: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.
st.bg.arjuna_sees_and_is_afraid.summary: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.

st.bg.arjuna_apology_to_friend.title: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
st.bg.arjuna_apology_to_friend.lesson: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.
st.bg.arjuna_apology_to_friend.summary: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.

st.bg.i_am_time_be_the_instrument.title: "I am Time": Krishna urges Arjuna to fight
st.bg.i_am_time_be_the_instrument.lesson: Do your part without imagining everything rests on you.
st.bg.i_am_time_be_the_instrument.summary: Krishna declares he is Time, the destroyer of worlds; the warriors will die even without Arjuna, so he should rise and be the instrument.

st.bg.if_you_cannot_then.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
st.bg.if_you_cannot_then.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.
st.bg.if_you_cannot_then.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.

st.bg.reflect_and_do_as_you_wish.title: Action with devotion: surrender
st.bg.reflect_and_do_as_you_wish.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.
st.bg.reflect_and_do_as_you_wish.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.

st.bg.my_delusion_is_gone.title: The glory of the Gita
st.bg.my_delusion_is_gone.lesson: Clarity, once found, turns into action.
st.bg.my_delusion_is_gone.summary: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.

st.bg.sanjaya_remembering.title: The glory of the Gita
st.bg.sanjaya_remembering.lesson: Clarity, once found, turns into action.
st.bg.sanjaya_remembering.summary: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_refuses_sight.title: Offered eyes to watch the war, Dhritarashtra says no
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_refuses_sight.lesson: What a person refuses to look at does not go away; it is only heard about later, when nothing can be done.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_refuses_sight.summary: On the eve of the war his own father, Vyasa, comes to him and offers what he has never had: sight, so that he can watch what is about to happen to his sons. He has had every chance to prevent this and has let each one pass.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_walks_unarmed.title: Yudhishthira takes off his armour and walks to the enemy's elders
st.mbh.yudhishthira_walks_unarmed.lesson: Respect for elders and firm opposition to them can be held in the same hour.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_walks_unarmed.summary: The armies are drawn up and the conches have sounded. He puts down his weapons, removes his armour, gets off his chariot and walks on foot, hands folded, toward the enemy line. His brothers run after him, alarmed. The other side jeers that he has lost his nerve.

st.mbh.yuyutsu_crosses_over.title: Yuyutsu leaves his brothers' side when the drum sounds
st.mbh.yuyutsu_crosses_over.lesson: When one's own side is in the wrong, leaving it openly is also a dharma.
st.mbh.yuyutsu_crosses_over.summary: He is Dhritarashtra's son by another mother, raised in the same palace as Duryodhana, standing in the Kaurava ranks. Yudhishthira, walking back to his own lines, calls out one last time: anyone who chooses us, I will accept as an ally.

st.mbh.krishna_breaks_his_vow.title: Krishna breaks his own vow and runs at Bhishma
st.mbh.krishna_breaks_his_vow.lesson: The Lord holds his devotee dearer than his own vow.
st.mbh.krishna_breaks_his_vow.summary: He has promised to take no weapon in this war. He is driving for a friend who keeps fighting his grandfather gently, half-heartedly, while Bhishma cuts the Pandava army down. Day after day he watches the man he came to protect fail to do what must be done.

st.mbh.bhishma_accused_of_partiality.title: Bhishma, giving everything, is told at night that he is not really trying
st.mbh.bhishma_accused_of_partiality.lesson: The one who serves faithfully is often suspected by the one he serves; his conduct answers for him.
st.mbh.bhishma_accused_of_partiality.summary: He is the oldest man on the field, fighting ten days running for a king whose cause he argued against. The king comes to his tent at night and says: you are soft on the Pandavas; if you will not fight properly, step aside and let Karna do it.

st.mbh.bhishma_tells_how_to_fell_him.title: The Pandavas ask their grandfather how to defeat him, and he tells them
st.mbh.bhishma_tells_how_to_fell_him.lesson: The elder who knows his time has come can help the young do what they must, and free them of the guilt of it.
