st.mbh.bhishma_tells_how_to_fell_him.summary: Nine days in, their army is being destroyed by the man who raised them. They cannot beat him and cannot bear to keep trying. At night, without weapons, the five brothers walk into his tent and ask him: how do we win, and how do you fall?

st.mbh.bhishma_pillow_of_arrows.title: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows
st.mbh.bhishma_pillow_of_arrows.lesson: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.
st.mbh.bhishma_pillow_of_arrows.summary: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.

st.mbh.karna_visits_bhishma.title: Karna comes alone to the man who insulted him
st.mbh.karna_visits_bhishma.lesson: A harsh word can come from concern, and an old quarrel can be ended at a deathbed without either side giving up what he stands for.
st.mbh.karna_visits_bhishma.summary: For years the old commander belittled him in open court, and Karna swore not to fight while Bhishma led. Now Bhishma lies on the arrows, the crowd has gone, and Karna comes in the dark, falls at his feet and says, his voice breaking: I am Radha's son, the one you always looked at with dislike.

st.mbh.abhimanyu_way_in_not_out.title: Abhimanyu knows the way in and not the way out
st.mbh.abhimanyu_way_in_not_out.lesson: When elders send the young into what they themselves cannot handle, the young pay; courage does not make up for a rule broken by the powerful.
st.mbh.abhimanyu_way_in_not_out.summary: He is sixteen. His father is away on another part of the field, and the enemy has formed a wheel only four men know how to break. The king, his uncle, turns to him: we are being destroyed, only you can open it. He answers honestly: I learned how to go in. I was never taught how to come out.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_guilt_abhimanyu.title: 'I sent the child in': Yudhishthira after Abhimanyu
st.mbh.yudhishthira_guilt_abhimanyu.lesson: Death comes to every creature and no one is its author; grief has to be carried, and the work in front of one still done.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_guilt_abhimanyu.summary: The fighting stops for the night and he sits among silent men. It was his request. The boy said he did not know the way out and he asked him anyway. Arjuna will be back within the hour. Subhadra will have to be told. 'What will I say to them?'

st.mbh.arjuna_returns_to_silence.title: Arjuna comes back to a silent camp
st.mbh.arjuna_returns_to_silence.lesson: The heart knows before it is told; and grief, unattended, reaches for an oath.
st.mbh.arjuna_returns_to_silence.summary: He is riding back at dusk after winning his part of the day and something is wrong. No music from the camp. No drums. Soldiers see him and look at the ground. He says to Krishna: my heart is sinking, why does no one meet my eyes, why does my son not come running out with his brothers to greet me?

st.mbh.krishna_sleepless_before_the_vow_.title: Krishna cannot sleep and quietly prepares his own chariot
st.mbh.krishna_sleepless_before_the_vow_.lesson: A friend's care shows in what he readies quietly, before he is asked.
st.mbh.krishna_sleepless_before_the_vow_.summary: His friend has sworn to die by fire if he fails tomorrow, and the enemy now knows exactly whom to hide. Krishna first sits with his sister Subhadra and the young widow Uttara and consoles them. Then, in the middle of the night, he lies awake.

st.mbh.arjuna_rests_the_horses.title: In the middle of the hardest day, they stop to water the horses
st.mbh.arjuna_rests_the_horses.lesson: Those who carry you must be cared for, most of all when there is no time.
st.mbh.arjuna_rests_the_horses.summary: The sun is moving, his life is forfeit at sunset, and Jayadratha is still miles behind layers of the enemy. Krishna says: the horses are exhausted and wounded, they need water and there is none here.

st.mbh.bhurishravas_and_two_wrongs.title: Bhurishravas: a rule broken to save a friend, and a worse act after
st.mbh.bhurishravas_and_two_wrongs.lesson: Dharma in a crisis is subtle; a wrong done in revenge on the helpless does not fade with time.
st.mbh.bhurishravas_and_two_wrongs.summary: Satyaki, his student and friend, is spent after a day of fighting. Bhurishravas has him by the hair, foot on his chest, sword raised. Arjuna is some way off, engaged with others. Krishna says: your student is about to die in front of you.

st.mbh.ghatotkacha_and_the_spent_weapon.title: Ghatotkacha dies, the camp weeps, and Krishna dances
st.mbh.ghatotkacha_and_the_spent_weapon.lesson: What saves the whole can cost a beloved one; the one who sees further is not thereby excused from honouring the loss.
st.mbh.ghatotkacha_and_the_spent_weapon.summary: Bhima's son by a forest wife, the boy who carried them on his back through the exile, is sent against Karna at night. Karna, hard pressed, throws the one weapon he had saved for Arjuna. Ghatotkacha falls. The Pandavas weep. And Krishna shouts for joy and embraces Arjuna.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_half_truth.title: 'Ashvatthama is dead', and under his breath, 'the elephant'
st.mbh.yudhishthira_half_truth.lesson: A half-truth told for a good end still lowers the one who tells it, and is accounted for.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_half_truth.summary: His teacher is burning through the army and cannot be stopped while he holds a weapon. Krishna says: he will put it down only if he hears his son is dead, and he will believe it only from you, because you have never lied. Bhima kills an elephant named Ashvatthama and shouts the news. Drona turns to Yudhishthira and asks: is it true?

st.mbh.after_drona_the_allies_turn_on_ea.title: After the shameful win, the allies turn on each other
st.mbh.after_drona_the_allies_turn_on_ea.lesson: Shame after a wrongful success turns companions against each other; it is quieted by a gentle word and by forgiving, with the wrong still named.
st.mbh.after_drona_the_allies_turn_on_ea.summary: They have won the day by a deceit. Arjuna says to his elder brother in front of everyone: he trusted you as a son, and you lied to him for a kingdom; this will stay on us as Vali's killing stayed on Rama. Bhima snaps back. Dhrishtadyumna defends the killing. Satyaki calls him a guru-killer. Dhrishtadyumna reminds Satyaki of Bhurishravas. Hands go to weapons.

st.mbh.narayanastra_lay_down_arms.title: The weapon that grows stronger the more you resist it
st.mbh.narayanastra_lay_down_arms.lesson: Some forces are met by setting down one's weapons and bowing; knowing which is discernment, and no shame.
st.mbh.narayanastra_lay_down_arms.summary: Ashvatthama, mad with grief for his father, releases the Narayana weapon. The sky fills with fire. Krishna shouts to the whole army: get down from your chariots, put your weapons on the ground, do not even think of fighting it. It spares only those who do not resist. Everyone obeys except one.

st.mbh.karna_spares_bhima.title: Karna has Bhima at his mercy and remembers a promise
st.mbh.karna_spares_bhima.lesson: A word given is kept even when breaking it would be easy, profitable and unseen.
st.mbh.karna_spares_bhima.summary: Days earlier his birth mother, who abandoned him as an infant, came to him for the first time and asked for her other sons' lives. He gave her his word: I will kill none but Arjuna. Now Bhima, who has mocked him for years as a driver's son, lies weaponless under the tip of his bow.

st.mbh.shalya_asked_to_drive.title: A king is asked to be the driver, and a driver who undermines
st.mbh.shalya_asked_to_drive.lesson: A person who knows his own measure can do his work even beside one who keeps telling him he will fail.
st.mbh.shalya_asked_to_drive.summary: He has waited his whole life for this command. On the day he gets it, the man holding his reins is a king who took the job under protest, who was tricked onto this side, and who has promised the enemy to wear him down. All morning Shalya tells him he is a crow who has challenged a swan and will drown.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_arjuna_quarrel.title: Two exhausted brothers nearly destroy each other in a tent
st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_arjuna_quarrel.lesson: Dharma is subtle, and a vow is not kept by an act that destroys what the vow was for.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_arjuna_quarrel.summary: Yudhishthira lies wounded and humiliated; Karna beat him and let him live with a taunt. Arjuna leaves the fight to check on him. The elder brother assumes he has come with news that Karna is dead. He has not. Seventeen days of fear pour out: you have failed us, your bow is useless, give your Gandiva to someone else.

st.mbh.kaushika_the_truth_teller.title: The ascetic whose truthful answer got people killed
st.mbh.kaushika_the_truth_teller.lesson: A rule followed without understanding its purpose can do the very harm it exists to prevent.
st.mbh.kaushika_the_truth_teller.summary: An ascetic who was no great scholar had taken one vow: I will always speak the truth. He was known for it. One day terrified travellers ran past his hut and hid in the forest. Robbers came after them and asked the famous truth-teller: which way did they go?

st.mbh.karna_wheel_in_the_mud.title: The wheel sinks and the mantra will not come
st.mbh.karna_wheel_in_the_mud.lesson: Old acts ripen at their own hour; a person's dignity is in how he stands when they do.
st.mbh.karna_wheel_in_the_mud.summary: It is the duel his whole life pointed toward and he is holding his own. Then the left wheel of his chariot goes down into the earth and sticks. He reaches for the great weapon his teacher gave him and the words are gone from his mind. Two old matters, a brahmin's cow he once killed by accident and a lie he told to get his training, have both come due in the same minute.

st.mbh.duryodhana_refuses_kripa.title: 'It is too late for peace': Duryodhana answers Kripa
st.mbh.duryodhana_refuses_kripa.lesson: Pride that will not take the offered way out goes on to finish what it began.
st.mbh.duryodhana_refuses_kripa.summary: Bhishma, Drona and Karna are gone, his brothers are dead, his army is a remnant. His old teacher Kripa, weeping, says what is obvious: make peace now, Yudhishthira is kind and will leave you a kingdom; there is no shame in saving what is left.

st.mbh.duryodhana_in_the_lake.title: Duryodhana in the lake: 'I do not want the kingdom any more'
st.mbh.duryodhana_in_the_lake.lesson: Emptiness after loss is no renunciation; and pride can still choose the honourable way to end.
st.mbh.duryodhana_in_the_lake.summary: Eleven armies are gone. He walks off the field alone, on foot, wounded, carrying only his mace, and lowers himself into a cold lake to rest where no one can see him. When the Pandavas find him and call him out, he says: I have no wish to rule an earth emptied of my brothers and friends. Take it. I will go to the forest in deerskins.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_weeps_for_duryodhana.title: Bhima kicks the fallen Duryodhana, and Yudhishthira stops him
st.mbh.yudhishthira_weeps_for_duryodhana.lesson: Even a defeated enemy is not to be humiliated; a win over one's own kin is half a grief.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_weeps_for_duryodhana.summary: Thirteen years of humiliation end with Duryodhana on the ground, thighs broken by a blow below the belt. Bhima dances around him, reminds him of every insult, and puts his foot on his head. The victory they prayed for is in front of them and it looks like this.

st.mbh.duryodhana_last_words.title: Duryodhana's last speech: 'Who has had a better end than I?'
st.mbh.duryodhana_last_words.lesson: A man can meet death without flinching and still never have seen his own fault.
st.mbh.duryodhana_last_words.summary: He lies in the dust with both thighs broken, alone, propped on his arms. Krishna lists his wrongs to his face. He is going to die slowly through the night.

st.mbh.balarama_stays_out.title: Balarama loves both sides and goes on pilgrimage
st.mbh.balarama_stays_out.lesson: Standing apart from a family war keeps one's affection for both sides, and gives up any part in its outcome.
st.mbh.balarama_stays_out.summary: Both Bhima and Duryodhana learned the mace from him. His own brother has taken one side. He tried for peace and failed. He says, 'I cannot bear to watch the Kurus destroyed', and leaves for a pilgrimage along the Sarasvati for the whole length of the war.

st.mbh.trita_in_the_well.title: Trita, left in a well by his brothers
st.mbh.trita_in_the_well.lesson: The one who is abandoned can still act from where he has fallen, and what is done with a whole mind reaches its mark.
st.mbh.trita_in_the_well.summary: Three brothers are driving home a herd of cattle earned by the youngest one's learning. The elder two walk behind and talk: he can always earn more; why should we not keep these? At night a wolf startles Trita and he falls into a dry well. He shouts. His brothers hear him, and keep walking with the cows.

st.mbh.mankanaka_dances.title: Mankanaka dances at his own achievement
st.mbh.mankanaka_dances.lesson: However far one has come, someone has gone further; delight in one's own attainment is the point where it stalls.
st.mbh.mankanaka_dances.summary: After years of austerity living on leaves, the sage cuts his finger on a blade of grass and plant sap flows out instead of blood. He is so delighted with what he has become that he begins to dance, and cannot stop. Everything around him starts dancing too.

st.mbh.sarasvata_keeps_the_learning.title: The boy who kept studying through the twelve-year drought
st.mbh.sarasvata_keeps_the_learning.lesson: What is practised daily through the lean years is what survives them; knowledge, not age, makes the teacher.
st.mbh.sarasvata_keeps_the_learning.summary: A drought lasts twelve years. The great sages scatter in every direction to find food, and in the struggle to survive they forget what they had learned. One young man, the son of the river Sarasvati, is about to leave too.

st.mbh.ashvatthama_cannot_sleep.title: Ashvatthama cannot sleep, and Kripa says 'wait until morning'
st.mbh.ashvatthama_cannot_sleep.lesson: Anger at night passes for clear thinking; no decision made in it should be carried out before morning and before asking the wise.
st.mbh.ashvatthama_cannot_sleep.summary: Three survivors hide under a banyan at night. Two fall asleep from exhaustion. The third lies awake, burning: his father was killed by a lie while unarmed, his king lies with broken thighs. In the dark he watches an owl drop silently into a tree of sleeping crows and kill them one by one. He thinks: this is how.

st.mbh.victors_defeated_by_carelessness.title: 'We who won have lost': the night after victory
st.mbh.victors_defeated_by_carelessness.lesson: Heedlessness after success undoes what effort won.
st.mbh.victors_defeated_by_carelessness.summary: The war is over and won. For the first night in eighteen days the camp sleeps without guards on edge. The five brothers happen to be elsewhere. At dawn a single surviving charioteer arrives with the news that everyone in the camp, the sons, the allies, the whole remaining army, was killed in their beds.

st.mbh.draupadi_lets_ashvatthama_live.title: Draupadi and the man who killed her sons
st.mbh.draupadi_lets_ashvatthama_live.lesson: The wronged may rightly demand an answer; having received it, the great stop short of the last cruelty.
st.mbh.draupadi_lets_ashvatthama_live.summary: She waited thirteen years for justice and got it, and on the same night all five of her sons were killed asleep, along with her brothers. She arrives 'shaking like a plantain in the wind', sits down on the ground and says she will not eat or rise until the killer is brought down and the jewel he was born with is brought to her.

st.mbh.weapon_that_cannot_be_recalled.title: Arjuna can call his weapon back; Ashvatthama cannot
st.mbh.weapon_that_cannot_be_recalled.lesson: What is released in fear and anger cannot be called back; only the self-controlled can withdraw what they send out.
st.mbh.weapon_that_cannot_be_recalled.summary: Cornered, in terror of Bhima, he picks up a blade of grass and turns it into the most destructive weapon there is, 'for the destruction of the Pandavas'. Arjuna releases the same weapon only to neutralise it. Two sages step between the two fires and order both men to withdraw them.

st.mbh.vidura_man_in_the_well.title: Vidura's parable: the man in the well, licking honey
st.mbh.vidura_man_in_the_well.lesson: Life hangs by a thread that time is gnawing, and people forget it for a drop of honey; seeing this clearly is where freedom begins.
st.mbh.vidura_man_in_the_well.summary: The old king has lost a hundred sons in eighteen days and lies on the ground. He asks his brother Vidura: how is a man to live with this? Vidura tells him a story. A man lost in a forest full of beasts runs and falls into a hidden well. He hangs head down, caught in creepers. Below is a great serpent. At the rim stands an elephant. A black rat and a white rat are gnawing the root he hangs from. Bees swarm round a hive above him, and from it honey drips into his mouth.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_crushes_iron_bhima.title: Dhritarashtra crushes the iron Bhima
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_crushes_iron_bhima.lesson: Grief carries a rage that wants someone to break; let it spend itself where it harms no one, and then look at one's own part.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_crushes_iron_bhima.summary: The victors come to pay respects to the blind old king whose sons they have killed. He embraces Yudhishthira and weeps. Then he asks for Bhima, the one who killed all hundred with his own hands. The king's arms are said to have the strength of ten thousand elephants.

st.mbh.gandhari_holds_back_her_curse.title: Gandhari holds back her curse, and asks one question
st.mbh.gandhari_holds_back_her_curse.lesson: Even righteous anger can be held by remembering what one has always stood for; and a grief may ask a question that has no answer.
st.mbh.gandhari_holds_back_her_curse.summary: She has kept a cloth over her eyes for a lifetime and has power stored up from it. All hundred of her sons are dead. As the Pandavas approach she makes up her mind to curse them. Vyasa arrives first and reminds her: for eighteen days, when your son asked your blessing, you said only 'where dharma is, there is victory'. Your word has come true.

st.mbh.gandhari_comforts_draupadi.title: Two mothers who have lost all their sons
st.mbh.gandhari_comforts_draupadi.lesson: The one who is equally wounded can console where no teaching can.
st.mbh.gandhari_comforts_draupadi.summary: Draupadi falls at Kunti's feet crying: where have all your grandsons gone, why do they not come to you today; what is a kingdom to me without my children? Standing beside them is Gandhari, mother of the men who dragged Draupadi by the hair, who has herself lost a hundred sons to Draupadi's husbands.

st.mbh.gandhari_curses_krishna.title: Gandhari's curse, and Krishna's answer
st.mbh.gandhari_curses_krishna.lesson: Grief may accuse even the Lord, and he bears it; what is to come to each, comes, and he does not exempt himself.
st.mbh.gandhari_curses_krishna.summary: Given sight for a day, she walks the field with Krishna and shows him, one by one: there is Duryodhana, and his wife wiping the blood from his face; there is young Uttara trying to fit Abhimanyu's body back together; there my daughter searches for her husband's head. Then she turns on him.

st.mbh.kunti_tells_too_late.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
st.mbh.kunti_tells_too_late.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.kunti_tells_too_late.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.

st.mbh.narada_many_causes_of_karnas_deat.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
st.mbh.narada_many_causes_of_karnas_deat.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.narada_many_causes_of_karnas_deat.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_victory_like_defeat.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
st.mbh.yudhishthira_victory_like_defeat.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_victory_like_defeat.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.

st.mbh.family_argues_yudhishthira_back.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
st.mbh.family_argues_yudhishthira_back.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.family_argues_yudhishthira_back.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.

st.mbh.janaka_and_his_queen.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
st.mbh.janaka_and_his_queen.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.janaka_and_his_queen.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_ashamed_before_bhish.title: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows
st.mbh.yudhishthira_ashamed_before_bhish.lesson: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_ashamed_before_bhish.summary: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.

st.mbh.krishna_asks_bhishma_to_teach.title: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows
st.mbh.krishna_asks_bhishma_to_teach.lesson: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.
st.mbh.krishna_asks_bhishma_to_teach.summary: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.

st.mbh.krishna_family_troubles.title: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron
st.mbh.krishna_family_troubles.lesson: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.
st.mbh.krishna_family_troubles.summary: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.

st.mbh.sage_and_the_crow.title: The sage, the crow and the corrupt officers
st.mbh.sage_and_the_crow.lesson: The one who guards what is common will be attacked by those who steal it; speak for the friend's good, and secure your own safety as you do.
st.mbh.sage_and_the_crow.summary: A sage sees that the young king of Kosala is being robbed by his own officials. He goes round the kingdom with a crow in a cage, saying the crow tells him everything, and learns who is taking what. Then he walks into court and names them, one by one, in front of the king.

st.mbh.kshemadarshi_fallen_prince.title: Kalakavrikshiya consoles the fallen prince
st.mbh.kshemadarshi_fallen_prince.lesson: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.
st.mbh.kshemadarshi_fallen_prince.summary: Prince Kshemadarshi has lost his kingdom and wealth. The sage Kalakavrikshiya tells him grief has no power to restore what is gone, to want what is within reach, and to make peace with others' good fortune.

st.mbh.honest_jackal_framed.title: The honest minister who was framed, cleared, and left anyway
st.mbh.honest_jackal_framed.lesson: Trust once broken by a hasty accusation does not return to what it was; the honourable may decline to stay.
st.mbh.honest_jackal_framed.summary: A jackal who has vowed to live cleanly is begged by the tiger king to be his minister. He agrees on conditions: listen to me in private, and never punish me on someone's word without checking. He serves well, and the old staff, whose thieving he has ended, plant the king's own meat in his den. The king, hungry and angry, orders him killed.

st.mbh.lazy_camel.title: The camel who got a long neck and stopped walking
st.mbh.lazy_camel.lesson: A convenience used as a reason to stop exerting oneself becomes the cause of ruin.
st.mbh.lazy_camel.summary: A camel earns a boon by long austerity and asks for a neck a hundred leagues long, so that he can graze without getting up. He gets it. From then on he does not go anywhere.

st.mbh.river_and_the_reeds.title: The river and the reeds
st.mbh.river_and_the_reeds.lesson: Bend with the flood and you stand again after it passes.
st.mbh.river_and_the_reeds.summary: The Ocean asks the rivers why they uproot great trees but never the reeds. Ganga answers: the reed bends when the flood comes and stands again after; the rigid tree breaks.

st.mbh.dog_who_became_a_sharabha.title: The dog who was raised up and turned on the one who raised him
st.mbh.dog_who_became_a_sharabha.lesson: One raised by another's kindness who turns on that kindness loses what he was given.
st.mbh.dog_who_became_a_sharabha.summary: A gentle sage lives in the forest and a dog stays near him out of devotion. A leopard comes for the dog; it runs to the sage, and he turns it into a leopard. A tiger comes; he makes it a tiger. Then an elephant, a lion, and at last a sharabha, the most fearsome of beasts.

st.mbh.three_fish.title: Three fish and the draining pond
st.mbh.three_fish.lesson: Act before the danger arrives, or act fast when it does; the one who keeps saying 'later' is lost.
st.mbh.three_fish.summary: Three friends live in a shallow pond. Fishermen begin cutting channels to drain it. The first fish says: trouble is coming for all of us, let us leave now by the outflow while we can. The third says: well said, but there is no hurry. The second says: when the time comes I will think of something.

st.mbh.cat_and_mouse_truce.title: The cat and the mouse
st.mbh.cat_and_mouse_truce.lesson: Sometimes you must cooperate with a rival; do it with clear eyes.
st.mbh.cat_and_mouse_truce.summary: Caught between a mongoose, an owl and a trapped cat, the mouse Palita makes a deal: he will gnaw the cat free if the cat protects him. Both keep the bargain, then part warily.

st.mbh.pujani_leaves.title: Pujani the bird leaves the palace
st.mbh.pujani_leaves.lesson: After real mutual injury, kind words do not restore trust; it is wise to part.
st.mbh.pujani_leaves.summary: A bird has lived for years in the king's inner rooms. Her chick and the king's little son are born together and she brings both of them fruit every day. One day the child, playing roughly, kills the chick. She comes home to find it dead.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_will_starve_himself.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
st.mbh.yudhishthira_will_starve_himself.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_will_starve_himself.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.

st.mbh.senajit_and_the_logs_in_the_sea.title: King Senajit and the brahmin's consolation
st.mbh.senajit_and_the_logs_in_the_sea.lesson: No one suffers forever. Meet what comes with an undefeated heart.
st.mbh.senajit_and_the_logs_in_the_sea.summary: King Senajit is crushed by his son's death. A brahmin comforts him: everyone suffers, no sorrow lasts forever, effort beats idleness, and whatever we call 'mine' becomes a source of pain.

st.mbh.pingala_stops_waiting.title: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting
st.mbh.pingala_stops_waiting.lesson: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
st.mbh.pingala_stops_waiting.summary: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.

st.mbh.janaka_mithila_burns.title: Mithila is on fire, and the king says nothing of his is burning
st.mbh.janaka_mithila_burns.lesson: One who holds nothing as 'mine' loses nothing when it burns, and so can act without fear.
st.mbh.janaka_mithila_burns.summary: Janaka is tested. His city of Mithila is set ablaze in front of him and the people crowd round to see what their king will do as everything he owns goes up in flames.

st.mbh.manki_and_the_two_young_bulls.title: Manki's song: desire, I know your root
st.mbh.manki_and_the_two_young_bulls.lesson: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
st.mbh.manki_and_the_two_young_bulls.summary: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.

st.mbh.medhavin_wakes_his_father.title: Medhavin: the son who woke his father
st.mbh.medhavin_wakes_his_father.lesson: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.
st.mbh.medhavin_wakes_his_father.summary: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.

st.mbh.kashyapa_and_the_jackal.title: Kashyapa and the jackal: the gift of hands
st.mbh.kashyapa_and_the_jackal.lesson: You already have what others long for. Craving is a fire that more fuel only feeds.
st.mbh.kashyapa_and_the_jackal.summary: A young brahmin, Kashyapa, knocked down by a rich man's chariot, wants to die in humiliation. A jackal tells him how lucky he is to have hands and a human life, and that craving grows like fire fed with wood. The jackal is Indra.

st.mbh.bali_after_the_fall.title: Bali and Indra: the fortune that moves on
st.mbh.bali_after_the_fall.lesson: Success is on loan. Don't gloat in a good season or despair in a bad one.
st.mbh.bali_after_the_fall.summary: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his defeated rival Bali living as a donkey in an empty house and mocks him. Bali calmly answers that fortune has lived with a thousand Indras before, that time gives and takes, and that this is a season for calm.

st.mbh.vishvamitra_and_the_dogs_meat.title: Starving in a famine, the great sage steals dog's meat from an outcaste's hut
st.mbh.vishvamitra_and_the_dogs_meat.lesson: In real extremity, staying alive is itself a duty; the code bends for the crisis and returns after it.
st.mbh.vishvamitra_and_the_dogs_meat.summary: A twelve-year drought has emptied the land. Vishvamitra, a great sage, wanders starving. He has found no food for a long time and sees no way to stay alive (12.141.62). At night he creeps into a chandala's hut to steal the haunch of a dog hanging there, and the owner wakes.

st.mbh.jajali_and_tuladhara.title: Tuladhara and Jajali: the merchant who taught the ascetic
st.mbh.jajali_and_tuladhara.lesson: Goodness is everyday fairness and friendliness, not spiritual display.
st.mbh.jajali_and_tuladhara.summary: The ascetic Jajali, proud because birds nest in his matted hair, is told to learn from a trader in Varanasi. Tuladhara teaches that right living is being a friend to all in thought, word and deed, and dealing fairly.

st.mbh.vyasa_runs_after_shuka.title: Vyasa runs after his grown son calling 'Son!', and only the echo answers
st.mbh.vyasa_runs_after_shuka.lesson: A parent can be proud of a child's freedom and still ache at being left; both are true, and grace meets the ache.
st.mbh.vyasa_runs_after_shuka.summary: Vyasa raised his son Shuka himself, taught him everything, and sent him to Janaka to finish his learning. Now Shuka, fully free, rises from the mountain and leaves for good. Vyasa, the greatest sage of his age, follows him with love, calling 'Son!' (12.341.19).

st.mbh.death_weeps.title: Death is created, and the first thing she does is weep
st.mbh.death_weeps.lesson: Death comes at its time to every being and is no one's cruelty; seeing this, grief can loosen.
st.mbh.death_weeps.summary: Brahma, angry that the world is overcrowded, begins to burn it. Shiva pleads for the creatures. To relieve the earth, a woman arises from Brahma's body and is told she will take the lives of all beings. She stands with folded hands and weeps. How can one like me be made for such cruel work, she asks; I fear wrongdoing; let me not take children, the old and the innocent (12.264.2-4).

st.mbh.srinjaya_and_the_sixteen_kings.title: The sixteen kings: Narada consoles Srinjaya
st.mbh.srinjaya_and_the_sixteen_kings.lesson: Everyone we love is mortal; you are not singled out. Grief can still be met with care.
st.mbh.srinjaya_and_the_sixteen_kings.summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira how Narada consoled King Srinjaya, whose son had died, by recounting sixteen legendary kings far greater than his son who also died. Moved, Srinjaya listens, and Narada restores the boy.

st.mbh.fowler_and_the_pigeons.title: The pigeons and the fowler
st.mbh.fowler_and_the_pigeons.lesson: Kindness can shame cruelty. Wherever the one you love is, that is home.
st.mbh.fowler_and_the_pigeons.summary: A storm-soaked fowler shelters under a tree after trapping a female pigeon. Her mate, grieving, still honours the fowler as a guest, lights a fire for him and, having nothing else, offers himself as food. The shaken fowler gives up hunting.

st.mbh.gautama_kills_his_benefactor.title: Gautama the ungrateful
st.mbh.gautama_kills_his_benefactor.lesson: Gratitude is the root of every friendship. Betraying a benefactor poisons everything after.
st.mbh.gautama_kills_his_benefactor.summary: A destitute brahmin, Gautama, is fed and sheltered by a kind crane, Rajadharma, and made rich by the crane's friend. On the way home he kills his sleeping benefactor for food. Bhishma ends: there is atonement for many wrongs, none for ingratitude.

st.mbh.chirakari_takes_his_time.title: Chirakari, the one who acts slowly
st.mbh.chirakari_takes_his_time.lesson: In anger, and when loved ones seem to have wronged you, slow down.
st.mbh.chirakari_takes_his_time.summary: In a jealous rage, the sage Gautama orders his son Chirakari to kill his mother and storms off. Chirakari, famous for slowness, weighs a father's word against a mother's worth for so long that Gautama returns, regretful, and finds them both alive.

st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.title: Hamsa Gita: the swan's teaching on speech and anger
st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.lesson: Words fly like arrows. The one who doesn't answer anger with anger stands highest.
st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.summary: Prajapati, in the form of a golden swan, answers the Sadhyas: never speak words that make others flinch, don't insult back, ride out the urges of speech and anger, and remember that we become our company.

st.mbh.the_python_sage.title: The python-sage (Ajagara vrata)
st.mbh.the_python_sage.lesson: Take what comes gladly; stop chasing what's out of reach.
st.mbh.the_python_sage.summary: Prahlada meets a sage who lives like a python, taking what comes and not chasing. The sage explains how ceasing to chase made him content.

st.mbh.sulabha_tests_janaka.title: A woman ascetic tests the king who says he is free
st.mbh.sulabha_tests_janaka.lesson: Freedom is tested by how one reacts, not by what one says about oneself.
st.mbh.sulabha_tests_janaka.summary: King Janaka is famous for saying he is liberated while still ruling. Sulabha, a wandering woman yogi, hears this and doubts it (12.325.9). She comes to his court to see for herself and, by yoga, enters his mind to test him.

st.bg.arjuna_how_could_you_have_taught_t.title: 'You were born after him. How could you have taught him?'
st.bg.arjuna_how_could_you_have_taught_t.lesson: An honest doubt, spoken to the teacher, opens the teaching instead of closing it.
st.bg.arjuna_how_could_you_have_taught_t.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago to the sun god Vivasvan, who passed it to Manu. Arjuna, who grew up with Krishna as cousin and friend, does the honest thing and objects: your birth is recent, his was ancient; how am I to understand that you taught it at the beginning?

st.mbh.gautami_and_the_serpent.title: An old mother, her son dead of snakebite, and the hunter who wants to kill the snake
st.mbh.gautami_and_the_serpent.lesson: A loss has many hands in it and none of them is the whole cause; seeing this frees both the griever and the one who blames himself.
st.mbh.gautami_and_the_serpent.summary: Yudhishthira opens the book by saying he has no peace: looking at Bhishma's arrow-pierced body, he can think only of his own wrongs; this was done to you because of me (13.1.4-6). Bhishma answers with a story. Gautami, an old woman known for her calm, finds her son dead of a snakebite (13.1.18). A hunter, Arjunaka, catches the snake, ties it up and brings it to her: tell me how to kill it.

st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.title: The parrot who stayed with the withered tree
st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.lesson: Loyalty means staying through the bad season, not only the good.
st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.summary: A hunter's poisoned arrow withers the tree where a parrot has always lived. The parrot refuses to leave it. Indra, moved by its loyalty, restores the tree.

st.mbh.upamanyu_and_the_flour_milk.title: A poor mother mixes flour in water and tells her boy it is milk
st.mbh.upamanyu_and_the_flour_milk.lesson: When you cannot give your child what they want, give them the truth and something greater to lean on.
st.mbh.upamanyu_and_the_flour_milk.summary: Upamanyu, a sage's son growing up in a forest hermitage, sees a cow being milked and cries for milk: give me milk, mother (13.45.98-99). There is none. His mother, grieving at having nothing, mixes flour in water and gives it to him and his brother as milk (13.45.100-101). Then, at a relative's house, he tastes real milk, and comes home and says: this is not milk you gave me.

st.mbh.kushika_serves_chyavana.title: A king and queen serve a guest who seems determined to break them
st.mbh.kushika_serves_chyavana.lesson: Service without resentment, under provocation, is the strongest proof of a good heart.
st.mbh.kushika_serves_chyavana.summary: The sage Chyavana comes to King Kushika's palace and asks to be served. He sleeps for days and the king and queen must sit by him without rest. He orders a huge feast, then has it burned along with the bed and seat (13.88.21-22). He has them yoked to a chariot and drives them through the streets, striking them. Through all of it they show no anger (13.88.23).

st.mbh.the_worm_on_the_road.title: A worm runs from a cart, and Vyasa asks why it bothers to live
st.mbh.the_worm_on_the_road.lesson: Every creature clings to life; what we will regret at the end is how we treated others.
st.mbh.the_worm_on_the_road.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about those who died in the war wanting or not wanting to die, and admits that giving up life is hard for anyone (13.179.2). Bhishma tells of Vyasa seeing a worm racing across a road. Asked why, the worm says: I heard a great cart coming and was afraid it would kill me; death is painful to creatures and life is hard to get, so I run (13.179.10-14).

st.mbh.bhangashvana_and_the_two_sets_of_.title: A parent whose two families destroyed each other is offered one of them back
st.mbh.bhangashvana_and_the_two_sets_of_.lesson: A parent's love may favour one set of children, but humble truthfulness won back all of them.
st.mbh.bhangashvana_and_the_two_sets_of_.summary: King Bhangashvana, who once held a sacrifice that left Indra out, is turned into a woman by Indra's anger after bathing in a lake. He gives the kingdom to his hundred sons and goes to the forest, where as a woman she has a hundred more sons with an ascetic. She brings them to the city to share the kingdom as brothers (13.34.25). By Indra's doing, enmity rises between the two sets, and they kill each other; she is left grieving two hundred sons (13.34.33, 38).

st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.title: Bhishma asks Krishna's leave to die
st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.lesson: At the end, it is enough to say: I am yours; now let me go.
st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.summary: When the sun turns north, Bhishma, after fifty-eight nights on the arrows, takes leave of the family, asks Krishna to protect him and to give him leave to go. Krishna says there is no fault in him and lets him go; Bhishma's last words to the family are to hold to truth and kindness.

st.mbh.ganga_weeps_for_bhishma.title: A mother outlives her very old son and asks why her heart does not break
st.mbh.ganga_weeps_for_bhishma.lesson: Even a goddess grieves her child, however old; grief does not measure love, and comfort can come from those who stand with us.
st.mbh.ganga_weeps_for_bhishma.summary: Bhishma's water rites are done. The river goddess Ganga, his mother, rises from the water weeping and overwhelmed with grief (13.274.20). She recounts his greatness and says: my heart must be made of stone, for it does not break though I cannot see my beloved son (13.274.23).

st.bg.arjuna_what_does_a_steady_person_l.title: 'How does a steady person talk, sit and walk?'
st.bg.arjuna_what_does_a_steady_person_l.lesson: To grow steady, first see clearly what steadiness looks like in a person.
st.bg.arjuna_what_does_a_steady_person_l.summary: Krishna has just spoken of a mind that stands firm. Arjuna, still shaken, asks the most practical question in the book: what does such a person look like? How does he speak, how does he sit, how does he walk?

st.mbh.arjuna_forgot_the_gita.title: Arjuna, after the war, admits he has forgotten what Krishna taught him
st.mbh.arjuna_forgot_the_gita.lesson: Even what changed your life can slip away in ordinary days; go back and ask again.
st.mbh.arjuna_forgot_the_gita.summary: The war is over and the kingdom won. Arjuna and Krishna are relaxing in the great hall. Arjuna says: I came to know your greatness when the battle stood before us. But all that you told me then out of friendship, I have lost, my mind was so scattered. I keep wanting to hear it again, and you will soon go back to Dvaraka (14.17.5-7).

st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.title: Krishna on the war within
st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.lesson: The hardest battle is with your own mind, and no one else can fight it for you.
st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.summary: As Yudhishthira still grieves, Krishna tells him his real battle has begun: one fought alone, with his own mind, where 'mine' is death and 'not mine' is freedom.

st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.title: Uttanka confronts Krishna
st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.lesson: You can try your best for peace and still fail. Others' choices are not your guilt.
st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.summary: Returning home after the war, Krishna meets the sage Uttanka, who is furious that Krishna let the cousins destroy each other and threatens to curse him. Krishna explains that he tried hard for peace and was refused, and calms him.

st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.title: The golden mongoose and the handful of flour
st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.lesson: A small gift, honestly earned and given from little, outweighs the grandest show.
st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.summary: At the end of Yudhishthira's lavish horse sacrifice, a half-golden mongoose declares it worth less than a poor family's gift. In a famine, a gleaner, his wife, son and daughter-in-law each gave their last handful of flour to a hungry guest; rolling in the spilt flour turned half the mongoose to gold.

st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.title: The stillborn heir and Krishna's promise
st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.lesson: In a family's darkest hour, the women's cry is heard and the promise kept.
st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.summary: Abhimanyu's son is born dead, struck in the womb by Ashvatthama's weapon. Kunti, Subhadra and Uttara beg Krishna for help, reminding him of his promise. Krishna, on the strength of his own truthfulness, revives the child, who is named Parikshit.

st.mbh.babhruvahana_fights_his_father.title: A son comes out humbly to greet his father, and is told to fight him
st.mbh.babhruvahana_fights_his_father.lesson: A child may have to stand up to a parent in the way the parent demands; the cost can be heavy and still lead to a truer bond.
st.mbh.babhruvahana_fights_his_father.summary: Arjuna arrives in Manipura following the sacrificial horse. His son Babhruvahana, whom he has barely known, comes out humbly to welcome him with brahmins at his side. Arjuna, angry, rejects the welcome: shame on you; a warrior who meets the man who came to fight him with soft words is no man (14.79.3-7). The boy stands with his head bowed.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_asks_to_leave.title: After fifteen years as a guest in his nephew's palace, the old king asks to go
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_asks_to_leave.lesson: When the time comes, an elder may choose to lay down his place with dignity and ask forgiveness for what he could not set right.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_asks_to_leave.summary: For fifteen years Yudhishthira has treated his blind uncle as king, with every honour. But Bhima, within his hearing, keeps reminding him whose sons are dead and whose arms did it. Dhritarashtra has quietly begun eating once a day and lying on the floor. One day he tells Yudhishthira: I want to go to the forest. I am old, my sons are gone, let me do what the old should do.

st.mbh.kunti_will_not_stay.title: Her sons beg her to stay in the palace she fought for, and Kunti walks to the forest
st.mbh.kunti_will_not_stay.lesson: One who fought for others' dignity does not need to collect a reward; she can walk away when the work is done.
st.mbh.kunti_will_not_stay.summary: As Dhritarashtra and Gandhari set out, Kunti goes with them, guiding Gandhari's hand. Yudhishthira and Bhima follow her, weeping: you urged us to war through Vidula's story, you sent Krishna with words to rouse us; now that the kingdom is won, why are you leaving us?

st.mbh.vidura_enters_yudhishthira.title: Yudhishthira finds Vidura in the forest, and Vidura gives himself to him
st.mbh.vidura_enters_yudhishthira.lesson: The one who taught us can pass into us; what he was continues in the one he chose.
st.mbh.vidura_enters_yudhishthira.summary: The Pandavas visit the elders in the forest. Vidura is not there; he wanders alone, naked, wasted by austerity, living on air. Yudhishthira runs after him through the forest calling: I am Yudhishthira, your dear one. Vidura stops in a lonely place and leans against a tree.

st.mbh.night_of_the_dead.title: For one night, the dead rise out of the Ganga to meet the living
st.mbh.night_of_the_dead.lesson: Those we lost, and those we fought, are at peace beyond anger; seeing that can loosen what we carry.
st.mbh.night_of_the_dead.summary: Fifteen years after the war, the old people in the forest still grieve. Gandhari asks Vyasa: Dhritarashtra cannot sleep for his sons, Kunti longs to see Karna, Draupadi her sons. Can we see them once?

st.mbh.the_elders_in_the_forest_fire.title: News comes that his mother died in a forest fire, far from him
st.mbh.the_elders_in_the_forest_fire.lesson: A parent who chose their own path and end was not abandoned; the child's guilt can rest on that truth.
st.mbh.the_elders_in_the_forest_fire.summary: Two years later Narada comes to Hastinapura with news. Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Kunti, frail and living on almost nothing, were caught by a forest fire. Sanjaya urged them to flee. They sat down facing east in meditation and let the fire take them. Sanjaya escaped to the Himalayas.

st.mbh.the_prank_and_the_iron_pestle.title: Bored young men play a joke on visiting sages, and a whole clan begins to end
st.mbh.the_prank_and_the_iron_pestle.lesson: Prosperity that makes us careless and contemptuous plants the seed of its own end.
st.mbh.the_prank_and_the_iron_pestle.summary: Thirty-six years after the war, the Yadavas of Dvaraka are rich, safe and careless. Some young men dress Krishna's son Samba as a pregnant woman and ask three visiting sages, mockingly, what she will give birth to. The sages see through it and say: he will bear an iron pestle that will destroy your clan.

st.mbh.yadavas_destroy_each_other.title: On a drunken holiday, an old wound is reopened and a clan kills itself
st.mbh.yadavas_destroy_each_other.lesson: Grudges never laid to rest, stirred by drink and pride, can destroy a family no enemy could touch.
st.mbh.yadavas_destroy_each_other.summary: The Yadavas go to Prabhasa on the coast for a festival and drink heavily. Satyaki, drunk, sneers at Kritavarma for the night massacre of the sleeping Pandava camp years before. Kritavarma sneers back about Satyaki killing Bhurishravas when his arm was cut off. Old wounds from a war long over are torn open in front of everyone.

st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hunter_jara.title: A hunter shoots at a deer, and finds he has hit Krishna
st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hunter_jara.lesson: Even at his death Krishna comforts the one who wounded him by mistake.
st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hunter_jara.summary: After the clan is gone and Balarama has left his body, Krishna lies alone in the forest, deep in yoga. A hunter named Jara, mistaking his foot for a deer, shoots an arrow into it. He runs up and finds he has wounded the Lord. He falls at Krishna's feet in horror.

st.mbh.arjunas_bow_fails.title: The greatest archer cannot string his bow, and Vyasa tells him why
st.mbh.arjunas_bow_fails.lesson: Strength and skill are given for a season; when the season ends, know it, and let go.
st.mbh.arjunas_bow_fails.summary: Arjuna arrives at an empty Dvaraka, sees Vasudeva die of grief, and sets out to take the surviving women, children and elders to safety. On the road a band of cowherd robbers attacks. Arjuna, who once held off the whole world, can barely string the Gandiva. He cannot remember his divine weapons. His inexhaustible quivers run out. The robbers carry off many of those he was protecting while he stands there.

st.mbh.the_final_walk_who_fell.title: On the last walk, one by one they fall, and Bhima asks why
st.mbh.the_final_walk_who_fell.lesson: Each person carries some small pride to the very end; the last journey reveals it.
st.mbh.the_final_walk_who_fell.summary: The five brothers and Draupadi crown Parikshit, put on bark garments and set out on foot, walking north toward Meru, a dog following them. Arjuna throws the Gandiva into the sea when Agni asks. On the mountain, Draupadi falls. Bhima calls out: she never did wrong; why did she fall?

st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_the_dog.title: Offered heaven if he leaves the dog behind, Yudhishthira refuses
st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_the_dog.lesson: Do not abandon one who is devoted to you, not even for heaven.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_the_dog.summary: Alone now except for the dog that has followed him the whole way, Yudhishthira is met by Indra in his chariot, come to take him to heaven in his body. Yudhishthira asks for his brothers and Draupadi, and is told they are already there. As he steps up, Indra says: the dog cannot come. Leave it.

st.mbh.duryodhana_in_heaven.title: Yudhishthira reaches heaven and finds Duryodhana seated there in glory
st.mbh.duryodhana_in_heaven.lesson: Even the righteous must put down the grudge before they can rest; enmity has no place in heaven.
st.mbh.duryodhana_in_heaven.summary: Yudhishthira enters heaven expecting his brothers. Instead he sees Duryodhana, radiant, seated on a throne and honoured by the gods. He turns away in anger: I do not want to share a world with the man who dragged Draupadi into the hall and caused the death of everyone we loved. Where are my brothers?

st.mbh.stay_a_moment_in_hell.title: In the darkness, voices beg him to stay, and Yudhishthira chooses hell
st.mbh.stay_a_moment_in_hell.lesson: To stay with those you love in their pain, choosing it freely, is the last and highest test of dharma.
st.mbh.stay_a_moment_in_hell.summary: Led down a path of stench, blood and darkness, Yudhishthira cannot bear it and turns to go back. Voices call from all sides: stay a moment; while you are here a cool breeze blows and our pain eases. He asks who they are. They answer: Karna, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadi, Draupadi's sons.

st.mbh.draupadi_reminds_him_of_his_word.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
st.mbh.draupadi_reminds_him_of_his_word.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.draupadi_reminds_him_of_his_word.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.

st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.

st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.title: Tulsidas on loving our own work
st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.lesson: Notice whether you can be glad at someone else's good work, not only your own.
st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.summary: Tulsidas calls his own poetry plain and asks readers to forgive it. Along the way he notes that everyone loves their own work, that few are glad at another's success, and that most people swell only with their own rising waters.

st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.title: Tulsidas on good company and difficult people
st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.lesson: The people around you shape your judgement; choose them, and take the good from everyone.
st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.summary: Before the story begins, Tulsidas bows to good people and, with gentle irony, to troublesome ones too. He describes how each acts, why company shapes us, and how the wise take the good and leave the rest, like the swan taking milk from water.

st.rcm.sati_doubt_test_lie.title: Sati doubts, tests and hides it
st.rcm.sati_doubt_test_lie.lesson: Doubt can be honest; hiding what you did is what breaks trust.
st.rcm.sati_doubt_test_lie.summary: Sati sees Shiva bow to Ram, a grieving prince searching the forest, and cannot believe Ram is divine. Ignoring Shiva's advice, she tests Ram by taking Sita's form, is found out, and then lies to Shiva about it. Shiva quietly withdraws from her, and she lives with a guilt she cannot speak.

st.rcm.sati_years_of_silence.title: Sati doubts, tests and hides it
st.rcm.sati_years_of_silence.lesson: Doubt can be honest; hiding what you did is what breaks trust.
st.rcm.sati_years_of_silence.summary: Sati sees Shiva bow to Ram, a grieving prince searching the forest, and cannot believe Ram is divine. Ignoring Shiva's advice, she tests Ram by taking Sita's form, is found out, and then lies to Shiva about it. Shiva quietly withdraws from her, and she lives with a guilt she cannot speak.

st.rcm.sati_goes_uninvited.title: Sati goes to her father's sacrifice uninvited
st.rcm.sati_goes_uninvited.lesson: You may go to family without an invitation, but not into open hostility; listen to that warning.
st.rcm.sati_goes_uninvited.summary: Sati's father Daksha holds a great sacrifice and invites everyone except Shiva and her. Shiva warns her that going where there is hostility brings no good, but she goes. Her father ignores her and insults her husband in front of everyone, and the visit ends in catastrophe.

st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.title: Shiva's grief turns to Ram's name
st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.lesson: Grief and devotion can walk together; steady love in loss is seen.
st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.summary: After Sati is gone, Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, repeating his name. Though beyond desire, he still grieves the loss of his devotee. Seeing his steady love, Ram appears, grateful and kind, praises Shiva's vow and asks him to marry Parvati.

st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.title: Parvati holds to her choice
st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.

st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.title: Rati comes weeping to the god who burned her husband
st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.lesson: Even the one who hurt you can be approached; compassion answers grief.
st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.summary: Kama, sent by the gods to break Shiva's meditation, is burned by his third eye. His wife Rati, fainting and weeping, goes straight to Shiva and pleads. Shiva, quick to be pleased and compassionate, promises her that Kama will live on without a body and that she will meet him again when Krishna is born.

st.rcm.maina_sees_the_groom.title: Parvati's trust and Shiva's strange wedding
st.rcm.maina_sees_the_groom.lesson: Love sees past appearances; trust can comfort the people who fear for us.
st.rcm.maina_sees_the_groom.summary: The sages tease Parvati that Shiva has burned Kama and her vow is lost; she smiles and trusts him. Shiva arrives with ash, snakes and a wild band of ghosts; Parvati's mother Maina breaks down and blames herself. Parvati comforts her, Narada reveals who Parvati is, and the wedding is celebrated, with Shiva remembering Ram in his heart.

st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.title: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance
st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.lesson: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.
st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.summary: On Kailash, Parvati sits beside Shiva and, still carrying her old doubt from her life as Sati, asks how a grieving prince can be God. Shiva is moved to tears, reassures her that there is no doubt left in her heart, and explains that the formless becomes form out of love for devotees. Her confusion lifts 'like autumn heat under moonlight'.

st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.title: Narada's pride and the monkey face
st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.lesson: The moment you boast of beating a weakness, it has found another way in.
st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.summary: Narada conquers desire in meditation and cannot stop telling people about it. Vishnu creates a city and a princess's swayamvara; Narada falls for her and asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu, like a doctor refusing harmful food, gives him a monkey's face instead, and Narada is laughed out of the hall until he sees what his pride has done.

st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.title: Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life
st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.lesson: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.
st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.summary: King Manu and Queen Shatarupa realise in old age that a whole life has passed without what mattered most to them. They hand over the kingdom, go to the forest and practise austerity for years. When Vishnu offers a boon, Manu hesitates like a poor man before the wishing tree, then asks for a son like God himself.

st.rcm.pratapbhanu_false_counsellor.title: Pratapbhanu trusts a flatterer who promises he can have it all
st.rcm.pratapbhanu_false_counsellor.lesson: Ambition without a limit makes a man easy for the flatterer who tells him there is a shortcut.
st.rcm.pratapbhanu_false_counsellor.summary: A just and victorious king loses his way hunting and is taken in at a hermitage. The hermit is a king he once defeated, now in disguise. He speaks sweetly, hints at great powers, and asks what the king desires.

st.rcm.where_is_hari_to_be_found.title: The gods argue about where to go to find God
st.rcm.where_is_hari_to_be_found.lesson: God is everywhere equally and shows himself where there is love.
st.rcm.where_is_hari_to_be_found.summary: The earth is crushed under Ravana's rule and the gods gather, frightened. They want to appeal to Hari and cannot agree where he is. One says go to Vaikuntha, another says the ocean of milk.

st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.title: Kausalya and the child who ran from dinner
st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.lesson: The grandest thing about a child may be the ordinary hours of childhood itself.
st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.summary: At his birth Ram shows Kausalya his cosmic form, and she asks him instead to be simply a baby. Later scenes are pure childhood: the boy runs off mid-meal, curd on his face, dusty from play, while his father laughs and his mother chases him. When she once glimpses the whole universe in him again, she asks only to be spared that and keep her child.

st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.title: Dasharath lets his sons go
st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.lesson: Parents protect children best by letting them go when the time comes.
st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.summary: The sage Vishwamitra asks King Dasharath to send the teenage Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest rites from demons. Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, offers land, cows, treasure, even his own life instead. Vasishtha reasons with him, and he finally embraces the boys and hands them over.

st.rcm.ahalya_counts_it_grace.title: Ahalya: the long wait ends
st.rcm.ahalya_counts_it_grace.lesson: However long you have been frozen, being seen can bring you back to life.
st.rcm.ahalya_counts_it_grace.summary: On the way to Janakpur, Vishvamitra shows Ram a stone in an empty hermitage: Gautam's wife Ahalya, bearing a curse in a body of stone, longing for the dust of his feet. At his touch she rises, stands before him with folded hands, unable to speak for love, tears streaming, and asks only that her mind may always drink at his feet.

st.rcm.janak_dispassion_moved.title: Janak, the detached king, finds his heart pulled
st.rcm.janak_dispassion_moved.lesson: Detachment is not the last word; love can still surprise the one who thought he was done.
st.rcm.janak_dispassion_moved.summary: Janak is known as the king who lives in the world untouched by it. He comes to greet a visiting sage, sees two boys beside him, and something in him gives way.

st.rcm.ram_tells_lakshman_his_heart.title: Ram notices his heart is stirred and says so to his brother
st.rcm.ram_tells_lakshman_his_heart.lesson: A mind that has kept itself clean can trust its own stirring, and the right way to carry a new feeling is in the open.
st.rcm.ram_tells_lakshman_his_heart.summary: Gathering flowers for his teacher in Janak's garden, Ram hears anklets, looks up and sees Sita. He cannot look away. He is a guest, she is unmarried, and nothing has been settled.

st.rcm.sita_prays_to_gauri.title: Sita wants something she is not free to ask for
st.rcm.sita_prays_to_gauri.lesson: What cannot be said to anyone can be laid before the one who already knows the heart.
st.rcm.sita_prays_to_gauri.summary: She has seen Ram and her heart is settled on him. But her father has vowed she will marry whoever strings Shiva's bow, and that is not in her hands. She goes back into the temple.

st.rcm.sita_at_the_bow.title: Sita watches the contest that will decide her life
st.rcm.sita_at_the_bow.lesson: Whoever holds a true love for another is certain to be joined to them.
st.rcm.sita_at_the_bow.summary: Ten thousand kings have failed to move the bow. Ram rises. She looks at him, tender and young, then remembers her father's vow, and her mind churns. She cannot help and she cannot look away.

st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.title: Janaka's despair and the bow
st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.lesson: Some moments do not wait; when it is time, act.
st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.summary: Ten thousand kings fail to lift Shiva's bow, and Janaka cries out that the earth has no heroes left. Lakshman bristles; Vishwamitra sends Ram forward. Ram sees Sita's anguish, knows that rain after the crops have dried is useless, lifts the bow and breaks it in a moment.

st.rcm.sunayana_too_young.title: Sunayana fears the boy is too slight for the task
st.rcm.sunayana_too_young.lesson: Do not judge the brilliant by their size.
st.rcm.sunayana_too_young.summary: Sita's mother watches Ram walk toward the bow that defeated Ravana and Bana. She turns to her friends in distress: why does no one stop the teacher? This is a child. All our wisdom has come to nothing.

st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.title: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.lesson: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.
st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.summary: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.

st.rcm.janak_vidai.title: Janaka says goodbye to his daughter
st.rcm.janak_vidai.lesson: Even the wisest parent breaks a little when a child leaves home; that is love.
st.rcm.janak_vidai.summary: After the wedding the time comes for Sita to leave Mithila. The palace, even the pet parrots, are in tears. Janaka, known everywhere for his detachment, holds his daughter and loses all composure; his ministers have to remind him it is time.

st.rcm.dasharath_grey_hair.title: Dasharath sees a white hair and decides to hand over
st.rcm.dasharath_grey_hair.lesson: The body tells you when it is time to pass the work on; the wise act on the first sign.
st.rcm.dasharath_grey_hair.summary: The king sits in court at the height of his good fortune. By chance he takes a mirror to straighten his crown and sees that the hair by his ears has turned white.

st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.title: Ram's unease on the eve of his crowning
st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.lesson: Real affection for siblings feels uneasy when one is favoured over the rest.
st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.summary: Dasharath, noticing grey hairs, decides to crown Ram heir, and the whole city celebrates. When Vasishtha brings Ram the news, Ram's first thought is not joy but unease: the brothers were born, raised and married together, so why should only the eldest be crowned?

st.rcm.kaikeyi_mind_turned.title: Manthara poisons Kaikeyi's mind
st.rcm.kaikeyi_mind_turned.lesson: Advice that flatters your fears can turn a good heart; check who benefits from it.
st.rcm.kaikeyi_mind_turned.summary: Kaikeyi is first delighted that Ram will be crowned; she loves him like her own son. Her maid Manthara works on her slowly, with sighs, hints and sweet-sounding fears about her future, until Kaikeyi believes her enemy is her only friend and goes to the sulking chamber to demand her two boons.

st.rcm.dasharath_bound_by_his_word.title: Dasharath's two promises
st.rcm.dasharath_bound_by_his_word.lesson: Promise only what you have thought through; a rash vow can cost what you love most.
st.rcm.dasharath_bound_by_his_word.summary: Dasharath finds Kaikeyi in the sulking chamber and, eager to please her, swears by Ram to grant anything. She asks for Bharat's coronation and fourteen years of exile for Ram. Bound by his word and his love, the king spends the night begging, raging and grieving, and by morning cannot speak.

st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.title: Ram hears he is to be exiled
st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.lesson: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.
st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.summary: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.

st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.title: Kausalya lets her son go
st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.lesson: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.
st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.summary: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.

st.rcm.sita_insists_on_going.title: Sita refuses to be left behind in comfort
st.rcm.sita_insists_on_going.lesson: To one who loves, hardship shared is lighter than comfort apart; and that is for her to say.
st.rcm.sita_insists_on_going.summary: Ram, in front of his mother, explains to Sita why she must stay: the forest has thorns, heat, wild animals, bark clothes. He is kind and thorough and has already decided for her.

st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.title: Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.lesson: Home is where your people are; a good send-off gives values, not just tears.
st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.summary: Ram asks Lakshman to stay and care for their old father and grieving mothers; Lakshman cannot imagine life apart from him. He goes to his mother Sumitra, afraid she will stop him. Instead she tells him that home is wherever Ram is, as day is wherever the sun shines, and gives him one piece of advice for the road.

st.rcm.ram_leaves_the_sleeping_city.title: Ram slips away at night from people who will not let him go
st.rcm.ram_leaves_the_sleeping_city.lesson: Sometimes those who love you cannot release you, and you must go without the goodbye they want.
st.rcm.ram_leaves_the_sleeping_city.summary: The whole city has followed him to the riverbank, old and young, saying where Ram is there is Ayodhya. He reasons with them tenderly and they will not turn back. They fall asleep, worn out with grief.

st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.title: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram
st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.lesson: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.
st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.summary: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.

st.rcm.kevat_bargains.title: Kevat washes Ram's feet
st.rcm.kevat_bargains.lesson: Some exchanges can't be priced; gratitude can be payment enough.
st.rcm.kevat_bargains.summary: At the Ganga, a boatman refuses to take Ram across until he can wash his feet, joking that if the dust of those feet turned a stone into a woman, it might turn his boat, his family's livelihood, into one too. Ram laughs and agrees. On the far bank Sita offers her ring as fare, and Kevat refuses: after a lifetime of wages, today he has been paid in full.

st.rcm.sumantra_returns_alone.title: Sumantra must drive the empty chariot home and face the king
st.rcm.sumantra_returns_alone.lesson: Some duties are only heavy; the faithful do them anyway and tell it straight.
st.rcm.sumantra_returns_alone.summary: The old minister was sent with one hope: bring them back, or at least bring Sita. He has failed at both. He turns the chariot. The horses keep looking back and will not pull.

st.rcm.valmiki_where_to_live.title: Ram, homeless, asks Valmiki where he should live
st.rcm.valmiki_where_to_live.lesson: The Lord's dwelling is the heart of one who listens, serves and holds no deceit.
st.rcm.valmiki_where_to_live.summary: A few days into exile, Ram comes to Valmiki's hermitage with his wife and brother and asks a practical question: tell me a place where I may build a hut and stay a while without troubling anyone.

st.rcm.forest_people_hosts.title: The Kols and Kirats have nothing fit to offer and offer it
st.rcm.forest_people_hosts.summary: Word spreads through the forest that a prince has come to live among them. The hill people come with leaf-cups of berries, roots and honey, as if they had found treasure. They are painfully aware of who they are and who he is.

st.rcm.dasharath_last_night.title: Dasharath dies remembering a wrong he did long ago
st.rcm.dasharath_last_night.lesson: A life can end unresolved and still end in love.
st.rcm.dasharath_last_night.summary: The charioteer has come back alone. The king lies in Kaushalya's rooms asking again and again where Ram is. The night will not end; it feels as long as an age.

st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.title: Bharat comes home to grief
st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.lesson: When someone is drowning in guilt for what others did, an embrace helps more than blame.
st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.summary: Bharat returns from his uncle's home to a silent city. His mother tells him proudly what she arranged; he learns his father is dead and his brother exiled because of him. Overwhelmed with shame he goes to Kausalya, expecting blame, and she embraces him as if Ram had come back, telling him not to carry the loss as his shame.

st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.title: Bharat comes home to grief
st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.lesson: When someone is drowning in guilt for what others did, an embrace helps more than blame.
st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.summary: Bharat returns from his uncle's home to a silent city. His mother tells him proudly what she arranged; he learns his father is dead and his brother exiled because of him. Overwhelmed with shame he goes to Kausalya, expecting blame, and she embraces him as if Ram had come back, telling him not to carry the loss as his shame.

st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.title: Bharat refuses the throne
st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.
st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.

st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.title: Guha nearly fights Bharat
st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.lesson: Find out someone's intent before you prepare for war with them.
st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.summary: Seeing Bharat's army approach the Ganga, Guha assumes he is coming to kill Ram and prepares his men to die fighting. An old man reads the omens and says Bharat comes to bring Ram back. Guha agrees that fools act in haste and repent, goes to meet Bharat with gifts, and the two embrace.

st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.title: Bharadwaj lifts Bharat's shame
st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.lesson: You are not your family's mistakes; carry only what is yours.
st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.summary: At Prayag Bharat meets the sage Bharadwaj, too ashamed to speak. The sage tells him not to eat himself up over his mother's deed and that what Bharat sees as a stain is a lesson for everyone. Bharat answers that he fears neither the world's talk nor the afterlife; only the thought that Ram suffers because of him keeps him awake.

st.rcm.bharat_unmoved_by_the_feast.title: Bharat spends a night in conjured luxury and does not touch it
st.rcm.bharat_unmoved_by_the_feast.lesson: A heart given wholly to one thing can sit beside every comfort untouched.
st.rcm.bharat_unmoved_by_the_feast.summary: To honour his guest the sage summons every comfort by his powers: palaces, beds, food, garlands, music, attendants. The whole army is dazzled. Bharat is given the best of it.

st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.title: Brihaspati checks Indra's envy
st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.lesson: Your fear of someone else's goodness usually says more about your interests than theirs.
st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.summary: Indra, king of the gods, fears that Bharat's devotion will bring Ram back and spoil the gods' plans, and wants to trick him. His teacher Brihaspati tells him that the world runs on action, that harming a good person backfires, and that his anxiety comes from his own self-interest, not from Bharat.

st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.title: Lakshman assumes the worst about Bharat
st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.lesson: Think before you act on an assumption; haste turns misunderstandings into wars.
st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.summary: Forest dwellers report that Bharat is coming with an army. Lakshman, sure it is an attack, climbs a tree and swears to destroy him. A voice from the sky warns against acting in haste, and Ram explains that Bharat could never turn against him; power could not corrupt him.

st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.title: The brothers meet at Chitrakoot
st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.lesson: Forgiveness can mean going first to the person who hurt you and putting them at ease.
st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.summary: Bharat walks barefoot to Chitrakoot and falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him into his arms. Ram learns his father has died and grieves. When the queens arrive, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused it all, falls at her feet and comforts her, blaming no one.

st.rcm.ram_meets_kaikeyi_first.title: Kaikeyi burns with remorse; Ram goes to her before anyone else
st.rcm.ram_meets_kaikeyi_first.lesson: The one who was wronged can choose to lift the wrongdoer's shame, and when he does, he does it first and without ceremony.
st.rcm.ram_meets_kaikeyi_first.summary: The mothers arrive at Chitrakoot. Kaikeyi is among them, the cause of all of it, now a widow whom her own son will not look at. She sees Sita and the two brothers in their bark clothes, simple and without reproach.
