st.viv.family_starving_or_the_mission.summary: Ramakrishna has died. The dozen boys around him are laughed at, then persecuted; their own parents are furious. At the same time his father dies and the family is left 'very poor, almost starving all the time'. He is the only one who can help them.

st.viv.letter_to_mary_on_grief.title: 'I was not good enough to that person': a letter to a grieving friend
st.viv.letter_to_mary_on_grief.lesson: The feeling that we were not good enough to the one we lost is itself a form of sorrow, not a verdict.
st.viv.letter_to_mary_on_grief.summary: Mary Hale writes to tell him her father has died. It is her first grief of this kind. Her mother and sister are in sorrow too.

st.viv.ascetic_housewife_butcher.title: The proud ascetic, the housewife and the butcher
st.viv.ascetic_housewife_butcher.lesson: No honest work is beneath you; doing it well is the practice.
st.viv.ascetic_housewife_butcher.summary: A young ascetic who can burn a bird with a glance is humbled by a housewife who knows what he did, and she sends him to a butcher in the market for teaching. The butcher, doing his trade honestly and caring for his parents, teaches him the highest truth. Doing the duty in front of you, without attachment, is itself the path.

st.viv.ghost_that_must_be_kept_busy.title: Karma-Yoga 5: we help ourselves, not the world
st.viv.ghost_that_must_be_kept_busy.lesson: Helping is a privilege, not a debt someone owes you.
st.viv.ghost_that_must_be_kept_busy.summary: The world does not need our help; helping is a privilege that makes us stronger. Expecting thanks brings unhappiness, so be grateful to the one you help. The world is a moral gymnasium, and calm people do the best work.

st.viv.chicago_no_speech_prepared.title: 'Sisters and Brothers of America': Chicago, 11 September 1893
st.viv.chicago_no_speech_prepared.lesson: You can belong fully to your own tradition and still honour every other path.
st.viv.chicago_no_speech_prepared.summary: An unknown 30-year-old monk from India, with no invitation and little money, rises on the Parliament's opening day and greets the hall as 'Sisters and Brothers of America'. The audience stands and applauds for minutes. In a five-minute address he says India's faith accepts all religions as true and hopes the day marks the death-knell of fanaticism.

st.viv.sage_who_would_not_teach.title: The proud ascetic, the housewife and the butcher
st.viv.sage_who_would_not_teach.lesson: No honest work is beneath you; doing it well is the practice.
st.viv.sage_who_would_not_teach.summary: A young ascetic who can burn a bird with a glance is humbled by a housewife who knows what he did, and she sends him to a butcher in the market for teaching. The butcher, doing his trade honestly and caring for his parents, teaches him the highest truth. Doing the duty in front of you, without attachment, is itself the path.

st.viv.slandered_by_an_old_friend.title: An old friend from home tells America he is a fraud
st.viv.slandered_by_an_old_friend.lesson: When someone you trusted slanders you out of jealousy, you can name the hurt, refuse to hate, and let the work answer.
st.viv.slandered_by_an_old_friend.summary: After Chicago, some clergymen attack him. Then the blow that hurts: Mazoomdar, a respected man from Calcutta whom he counted an old friend, tells people in America he is a fraud and a rogue, and in Calcutta says he is living an unchaste life.

st.viv.boy_gopala_and_his_mother.title: A poor widow's small son is afraid to walk home through the woods
st.viv.boy_gopala_and_his_mother.lesson: A parent's faith, passed to a child, makes the child unafraid; love and faith, more than learning, bring the Lord near.
st.viv.boy_gopala_and_his_mother.summary: Gopala's mother is a widow, very poor, who has toiled at her spinning wheel for months to buy his school things. One winter afternoon he tells her he is afraid to walk home alone through the dark woods; other boys have someone to fetch them. 'Never before had she felt her widowhood, her loneliness, her poverty so bitter.'

st.vr.valmiki_grief_becomes_verse.title: Grief becomes the first verse
st.vr.valmiki_grief_becomes_verse.lesson: Grief can be turned into something that helps others; even a sage regrets words spoken in pain.
st.vr.valmiki_grief_becomes_verse.summary: Valmiki sees a hunter shoot one of a pair of mating cranes and hears the survivor cry. His grief bursts out as a curse that falls into rhythm; he regrets the words but realises they are a new kind of verse. Brahma tells him to use it to tell Ram's story.

st.vr.valmiki_asks_is_there_such_a_perso.title: Valmiki asks: is there anyone like this alive today?
st.vr.valmiki_asks_is_there_such_a_perso.lesson: It is a sound instinct to look for a life to learn from, and to ask someone who has seen more than you.
st.vr.valmiki_asks_is_there_such_a_perso.summary: Before there is any story, there is a man with a question. Valmiki has studied and practised for years, and what he wants to know is simple: is there, right now, in this world, a person who is truthful, grateful, steady in his word, kind to every creature and still strong? He asks the one visitor who has seen all the worlds.

st.vr.dasharatha_lets_ram_go_with_vishva.title: Dasharatha lets his son go
st.vr.dasharatha_lets_ram_go_with_vishva.lesson: Letting a child go out into the world can be the most loving thing a parent does.
st.vr.dasharatha_lets_ram_go_with_vishva.summary: The sage Vishvamitra asks the king for his teenage son Ram to protect a ritual. Dasharatha, who waited years for a child, refuses and offers himself and his army instead. His guru reminds him of his word and that the sage asks for Ram's own growth, and the king lets him go.

st.vr.vishvamitra_envies_the_sage_cow.title: The king who wanted the cow
st.vr.vishvamitra_envies_the_sage_cow.lesson: Envy and force cannot take what someone will not give; real power is built inside.
st.vr.vishvamitra_envies_the_sage_cow.summary: King Vishvamitra is feasted by the sage Vasishtha and covets the wish-granting cow that made it possible. Vasishtha refuses every offer; the king takes her by force and is routed, then fails again with divine weapons. Humbled, he resolves to transform himself through inner discipline instead of force.

st.vr.vishvamitra_menaka_ten_years.title: Ten years gone: Vishvamitra and Menaka
st.vr.vishvamitra_menaka_ten_years.lesson: Lost years are not the end; notice, stop blaming, and begin again.
st.vr.vishvamitra_menaka_ten_years.summary: Deep into his effort to transform himself, Vishvamitra falls for the nymph Menaka and ten years pass like a day. When he wakes up to it, he is ashamed, lets her go kindly rather than blaming her, and starts again. Brahma tells him he is not there yet: he must first master his senses.

st.vr.vishvamitra_anger_begins_again.title: Vishvamitra loses his temper, and begins again
st.vr.vishvamitra_anger_begins_again.lesson: Relapses happen; a clear vow and steady practice can make anger lose its grip, and rivals can become friends.
st.vr.vishvamitra_anger_begins_again.summary: Tested again, Vishvamitra explodes and curses the nymph Rambha, losing the fruit of his long effort. He vows not to give way to anger or speak in it, keeps a thousand-year silence, and this time obstacles shake him but anger cannot get in. He reaches his goal, and his old rival Vasishtha embraces him as a friend.

st.vr.bhagiratha_finishes_what_three_gen.title: Bhagiratha brings the Ganga down
st.vr.bhagiratha_finishes_what_three_gen.lesson: Some goals take longer than one effort or one lifetime; keep going and others' work is not wasted.
st.vr.bhagiratha_finishes_what_three_gen.summary: King Sagara's sixty thousand sons are burnt to ash; only the Ganga's water can free them. Sagara, his grandson Anshuman and Anshuman's son Dilipa each try and die without success. Bhagiratha finally persists until the river descends, and Brahma honours him for finishing what three generations began.

st.vr.shunahshepa_the_middle_son.title: Shunahshepa, the son neither parent chose to keep
st.vr.shunahshepa_the_middle_son.lesson: When those who should protect you do not, you may seek refuge elsewhere and ask plainly for what you need.
st.vr.shunahshepa_the_middle_son.summary: A king needs a human substitute for a lost sacrifice and offers a fortune for a son. The father says: I will never sell my eldest. The mother says: the youngest is my darling, I cannot part with him. The middle boy hears both sentences and understands his place in the house. He says it himself: then the middle one is sold. Take me.

st.vr.trishanku_refused_by_everyone.title: Trishanku is refused, cast out, and taken in by one man
st.vr.trishanku_refused_by_everyone.lesson: A person who has been turned away by all and comes for refuge is to be received first and judged later.
st.vr.trishanku_refused_by_everyone.summary: King Trishanku wants something no one has done, to reach heaven in his own body. His teacher says it cannot be done. He asks the teacher's sons, and they curse him for going around their father. Overnight he is an outcaste; his ministers and his people walk away. He goes alone to the one person who has no reason to help him.

st.vr.ahalya_unseen_years_and_return.title: Ahalya: years unseen, then received with honour
st.vr.ahalya_unseen_years_and_return.lesson: A person is larger than their worst act, and the honour they are shown can be the last step of their return.
st.vr.ahalya_unseen_years_and_return.summary: Ahalya made a choice she knew to be wrong; in Valmiki she recognises Indra and agrees out of curiosity. Her husband's anger falls on both. Indra is maimed. She is told she will live on in the empty hermitage, unseen by anyone, with air for food and ash for a bed, until Ram comes. The house goes quiet around her and the years begin.

st.vr.parashurama_challenges_ram.title: An angry elder challenges Ram on the road home
st.vr.parashurama_challenges_ram.lesson: Meet a challenge to your worth with what you can do, and leave the challenger his dignity.
st.vr.parashurama_challenges_ram.summary: Ram has just broken Shiva's bow and married. On the road home a terrifying figure blocks the way: Parashurama, who once emptied the earth of warriors, holding another great bow and demanding that this boy prove himself. Dasharatha begs for his son's life and is ignored. Ram is being belittled in front of his father on what should be the best week of his life.

st.vr.ram_sita_love_grows.title: Ram and Sita's early marriage
st.vr.ram_sita_love_grows.lesson: Love deepens by paying attention to who the other person really is.
st.vr.ram_sita_love_grows.summary: Back in Ayodhya after the wedding, Ram and Sita settle into married life. Valmiki notes that their love, though it began as an arranged match, deepened because each came to know and value the other; she could read his heart without words.

st.vr.ram_remembers_one_kindness.title: What Ram was like
st.vr.ram_remembers_one_kindness.lesson: Character shows in small habits: speaking first and gently, remembering kindness, forgetting slights.
st.vr.ram_remembers_one_kindness.summary: Before the crisis, Valmiki and the citizens describe the young prince: gentle in speech, unprovoked by harshness, pleased by one kindness and forgetful of a hundred wrongs, humble about his strength, attentive to ordinary people's lives.

st.vr.dasharatha_hurries_the_coronation.title: An ageing king rushes to hand over
st.vr.dasharatha_hurries_the_coronation.lesson: A right decision carried out in fear and haste can undo itself.
st.vr.dasharatha_hurries_the_coronation.summary: Dasharatha feels his age. He has ruled long, his body is tired, and his dreams have turned frightening. He wants to see his son crowned while he still can. So he decides fast, announces it for the very next day, and calls Ram back a second time at night to say: do it tomorrow, minds change.

st.vr.manthara_turns_kaikeyi.title: Kaikeyi's boons and the king's blind promise
st.vr.manthara_turns_kaikeyi.lesson: Envy grows when fed; never promise before you know what you are being asked.
st.vr.manthara_turns_kaikeyi.summary: The maid Manthara works on Queen Kaikeyi's insecurity until she is consumed by fear for her son's future. Kaikeyi makes the doting old king promise before she names her wish, then demands Ram's exile and Bharata's coronation. Bound by his word, Dasharatha pleads, rages and collapses.

st.vr.dasharatha_trapped_by_his_promise.title: Kaikeyi's boons and the king's blind promise
st.vr.dasharatha_trapped_by_his_promise.lesson: Envy grows when fed; never promise before you know what you are being asked.
st.vr.dasharatha_trapped_by_his_promise.summary: The maid Manthara works on Queen Kaikeyi's insecurity until she is consumed by fear for her son's future. Kaikeyi makes the doting old king promise before she names her wish, then demands Ram's exile and Bharata's coronation. Bound by his word, Dasharatha pleads, rages and collapses.

st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.title: Ram accepts exile
st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.lesson: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.
st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.summary: On the morning of his coronation, Ram is summoned and told by Kaikeyi that he must go into the forest for fourteen years. He agrees without anger, and is hurt only that his father could not tell him himself. He walks out showing no change of mind, already thinking of those he must comfort.

st.vr.kausalya_hoped_her_sons_time_would.title: Kausalya lets Ram go
st.vr.kausalya_hoped_her_sons_time_would.lesson: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.
st.vr.kausalya_hoped_her_sons_time_would.summary: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.

st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.title: Kausalya lets Ram go
st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.lesson: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.
st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.summary: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.

st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.title: Lakshman's fury, Ram's calm
st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.lesson: Anger at injustice is natural; decide what to do with it before it decides for you.
st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.summary: Lakshman is enraged by the injustice and wants to seize the throne by force. Ram calms him: set aside the insult, don't torment yourself, the setback may lead somewhere better. Lakshman answers that effort, not fate, decides; both views are given their due.

st.vr.sita_chooses_the_forest.title: Sita chooses to go
st.vr.sita_chooses_the_forest.lesson: A partnership means making big decisions together, and listening when the other has decided.
st.vr.sita_chooses_the_forest.summary: Ram asks Sita to stay safely in Ayodhya. She refuses, argues, laughs at his fears and insists: the hardships he lists are nothing if they face them together. Ram listens, realises he had not understood how determined she was, and agrees.

st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.title: Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.lesson: Home is the people you are with; you can carry it into any wilderness.
st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.summary: As the exiles leave, Lakshman's mother blesses him: treat Ram as your father, Sita as your mother, and the forest as home. She tells him to go happily.

st.vr.ram_gives_everything_away_trijata.title: Ram empties his house, and laughs with a poor brahmin
st.vr.ram_gives_everything_away_trijata.lesson: You can meet a great loss with open hands and even with humour.
st.vr.ram_gives_everything_away_trijata.summary: It is the day of the exile and Ram is giving away everything he owns: jewels, carts, cows, to teachers, servants, old dependants. An old, poor brahmin named Trijata, pushed by his wife, arrives late and asks for something. On the worst day of his life, Ram is in the mood for a joke.

st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.title: One more night: Ram leaves his father
st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.lesson: Goodbyes to ageing parents are hard; leave with love and a promise to return.
st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.summary: The broken king begs Ram to stay one more night so his parents can see him. Ram gently refuses, saying a promise made must be kept and he will return in fourteen years. Dasharatha embraces him and collapses.

st.vr.ram_first_night_bitterness.title: The calm one breaks, in private, on the first night across the river
st.vr.ram_first_night_bitterness.lesson: Composure in public and grief in private can belong to the same strong person.
st.vr.ram_first_night_bitterness.summary: All day Ram has been the steady one. He comforted his mother, his father, his wife, the whole city. Now it is night under a tree, Sita is asleep, and only Lakshman is awake. What he held back comes out: the king is in the grip of desire, Kaikeyi may harm our mothers, Bharata sleeps happy tonight. He tells Lakshman to go home in the morning.

st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.title: Ram slips away from the loyal crowd
st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.lesson: Leaders protect people from their troubles; they don't pull others into their own.
st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.summary: Thousands of citizens follow Ram into the wilderness, determined to bring him back. At dawn he slips away while they sleep so they will go home rather than suffer for his sake.

st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.title: Ram's messages home
st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.lesson: Even when a parent fails you, you can choose to protect their dignity.
st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.summary: The charioteer returns and delivers Ram's messages: honour our father in his old age, be kind to all three mothers including Kaikeyi. He also delivers Lakshman's furious words about their father, showing two very different ways sons respond to a parent's failure.

st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.title: Sumitra sits with Kausalya
st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.lesson: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.
st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.summary: Kausalya weeps for her son gone to the forest. Her co-queen Sumitra, whose own son has gone too, comforts her: he went for a good reason, he is not alone, and you will see him again.

st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.title: Kausalya's reproach and apology
st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.lesson: Grief makes us wound those we love; apologising quickly heals more than being right.
st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.summary: In her grief Kausalya lashes out at her husband for exiling their son. When he folds his hands and asks her forgiveness, she is horrified, apologises, and explains that grief made her speak.

st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.title: The boy at the river: Dasharatha's old guilt
st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.lesson: Carelessness can wound for decades; owning it honestly is the only way to carry it.
st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.summary: Dying of grief, Dasharatha confesses to Kausalya that as a young prince he shot at a sound in the dark and killed a boy filling water for his blind, aged parents. He took the water to them and told them the truth himself. The father cursed him to lose a son as they had, and now, longing for Ram, the king dies at midnight.

st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.title: Bharata comes home too late
st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.lesson: Missing a parent's death far from home is its own grief; let yourself feel it.
st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.summary: Bharata, living at his uncle's court, has a nightmare and is summoned home. He finds the city silent and learns from his mother that his father has died while he was away, and then that Ram is in exile because of her.

st.vr.bharata_rage_at_his_mother.title: Bharata wrongly blamed
st.vr.bharata_rage_at_his_mother.lesson: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.
st.vr.bharata_rage_at_his_mother.summary: Bharata turns on his mother in fury. Then Ram's grieving mother assumes he plotted it all, and her words cut him like a needle in a wound. He falls at her feet and swears his innocence until she believes him.

st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.title: Bharata wrongly blamed
st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.lesson: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.
st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.summary: Bharata turns on his mother in fury. Then Ram's grieving mother assumes he plotted it all, and her words cut him like a needle in a wound. He falls at her feet and swears his innocence until she believes him.

st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.title: At the pyre, and the hand that stopped
st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.lesson: Grief and rage come together; one calm person can stop a moment we'd regret forever.
st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.summary: The brothers perform their father's rites and collapse in grief; the family priest lifts them up. When Shatrughna drags Manthara before him in rage, Bharata stops him: Ram would never forgive cruelty done in his name.

st.vr.bharata_stops_shatrughna.title: At the pyre, and the hand that stopped
st.vr.bharata_stops_shatrughna.lesson: Grief and rage come together; one calm person can stop a moment we'd regret forever.
st.vr.bharata_stops_shatrughna.summary: The brothers perform their father's rites and collapse in grief; the family priest lifts them up. When Shatrughna drags Manthara before him in rage, Bharata stops him: Ram would never forgive cruelty done in his name.

st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.title: Bharata refuses the throne
st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.lesson: Not every gain is worth taking; integrity sometimes means refusing what you are handed.
st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.summary: The court offers Bharata the kingdom his mother won for him. He refuses before the whole assembly, says it belongs to his brother, and sets out with the army and the city to bring Ram back.

st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.title: Guha's suspicion and Bharata's grief
st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.lesson: Prepare if you must, but find out someone's intent before you judge them.
st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.summary: Ram's friend Guha sees Bharata's army and assumes he has come to kill Ram. He prepares to block the river but goes to meet him first. Learning Bharata's intent, he becomes his guide and shows him the grass bed where Ram slept, where Bharata vows to live as an ascetic until Ram returns.

st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.title: Lakshman suspects Bharata
st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.lesson: Don't assume the worst of family on the strength of what you see from a distance.
st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.summary: From a tree at Chitrakoot, Lakshman sees Bharata's army and is sure he has come to finish them. Ram stops him: Bharata has never wronged us; why suspect him now? And no kingdom is worth winning through wrong.

st.vr.ram_content_at_chitrakoot.title: Ram on a hillside: I do not miss the kingdom
st.vr.ram_content_at_chitrakoot.lesson: Joy does not wait for circumstances to be restored; it can be found in what is here and who is beside you.
st.vr.ram_content_at_chitrakoot.summary: Some months into exile, Ram and Sita are living in a leaf hut on Chitrakoot. He takes her walking and points things out like a host: the minerals streaking the rock, the birds, the river Mandakini below. He is a banished prince with nothing, and he is plainly enjoying himself.

st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.title: The brothers meet at Chitrakoot
st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.lesson: A rift can close in one embrace; grief shared between siblings is lighter.
st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.summary: Bharata finds Ram in bark clothes and falls weeping at his feet, blaming himself. Ram embraces him, tells him he sees no fault in him, and asks him not to blame his mother. Then Ram learns their father is dead and grieves that he was not there.

st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.title: Ram on why grief must not rule us
st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.lesson: Everything that comes together parts; let that make you gentler, not hopeless.
st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.summary: Bharata begs Ram to return and rule. Ram answers with a teaching on impermanence: everything gathered runs out, everything rising falls, people meet like logs on the ocean and drift apart. Grieve, but do not let grief overturn your duty.

st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.title: Jabali's doubt
st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.lesson: Doubt deserves a hearing; answer it with how you choose to live.
st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.summary: The priest Jabali argues that nobody belongs to anyone, rituals are empty and only the present matters, so Ram should take the throne. Ram answers that conduct, not claims, shows who we are, and that people follow the example of those who lead.

st.vr.bharata_and_the_sandals.title: The sandals: a compromise between brothers
st.vr.bharata_and_the_sandals.lesson: When neither can give way, find a form that honours both; and let go of blame.
st.vr.bharata_and_the_sandals.summary: Bharata threatens to fast at Ram's door until he returns. Ram persuades him to rise, and they reach a compromise: Bharata takes Ram's sandals to rule in his name. At parting Ram asks him to drop his resentment of their mother.

st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.title: Bharata's fourteen years at Nandigram
st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.lesson: Waiting can be active: keep faith by taking care of what was entrusted to you.
st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.summary: Bharata refuses to live in the palace. From a village hut he governs in the name of Ram's sandals, dressed as an ascetic, holding everything in trust and waiting fourteen years for his brother.

st.vr.ram_will_not_hear_kaikeyi_blamed.title: Ram will not let anyone speak ill of Kaikeyi
st.vr.ram_will_not_hear_kaikeyi_blamed.lesson: The one who was wronged may choose not to keep the wrong alive in his own house.
st.vr.ram_will_not_hear_kaikeyi_blamed.summary: If anyone has earned the right to hate Kaikeyi it is Ram. At Chitrakoot her own son cannot look at her. One winter morning in the forest Lakshman, shivering by the river, wonders aloud how a woman with such a husband and such a son turned so cruel. Ram is the injured party both times.

st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.title: Ram's questions to Bharata
st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.lesson: Good leaders consult wisely, act promptly, and listen to people with no power.
st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.summary: Meeting Bharata at Chitrakoot, Ram asks a long series of questions about how he is running the kingdom: whom he consults, how quickly he acts, whether he listens to the falsely accused.

st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.title: Sita questions the weapon
st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.lesson: Disagree with someone you love openly; advice is a sign of care.
st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.summary: Sita worries that Ram, carrying weapons among peaceful hermits, will be drawn into needless violence. She tells the story of a hermit changed by keeping a sword. Ram thanks her, saying no one advises a person they don't care about, and explains his promise to protect the sages.

st.vr.ram_thanks_lakshman_for_the_hut.title: Ram stops to thank the brother who built the hut
st.vr.ram_thanks_lakshman_for_the_hut.lesson: Say the thanks while the day is ordinary, and say exactly what the person is to you.
st.vr.ram_thanks_lakshman_for_the_hut.summary: At Panchavati Ram chooses a spot and tells Lakshman to build. Lakshman levels the ground, raises posts of bamboo, thatches the roof, then goes to the river, bathes, and brings back lotuses and fruit. He reports the work done, as he has every day for years. Ram looks at the hut for a while.

st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.title: Maricha warns Ravana
st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.lesson: Listen hardest to the advice you least want to hear.
st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.summary: Ravana asks Maricha to help him abduct Sita. Maricha, who has met Ram before, warns him again and again: flatterers are many, truth-tellers rare, and those heading for a fall reject good advice. Ravana threatens him until he agrees.

st.vr.the_golden_deer.title: The golden deer
st.vr.the_golden_deer.lesson: When something looks too perfect to be real, pause before you chase it.
st.vr.the_golden_deer.summary: A dazzling deer with a golden, jewelled hide appears near the hut. Lakshman warns that no such deer exists; it must be a trick. Sita longs for it and Ram, captivated too, gives chase, leaving the hut exposed.

st.vr.lakshman_between_an_order_and_an_a.title: Lakshman is accused by the person he is guarding
st.vr.lakshman_between_an_order_and_an_a.lesson: Fear for one we love can make us wound the very person who is protecting us.
st.vr.lakshman_between_an_order_and_an_a.summary: A cry in Ram's voice comes from the forest. Sita is frantic and tells Lakshman to go. He knows no one can hurt Ram and that the voice is a trick, and his order was to stay with her. He says so. In her terror she says the worst thing she can think of: you want him dead, you have designs on me. She says she will kill herself in front of him.

st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.title: Jatayu, old and brave
st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.lesson: Age is no reason to stop standing up for what's right; honour those who stood up for you.
st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.summary: The aged vulture Jatayu wakes to see Ravana carrying Sita off. He warns him, then fights him alone and is mortally wounded. Later Ram finds him dying, hears his news, and cremates him with the honour due a father.

st.vr.sita_drops_her_ornaments.title: Sita, carried off, does the one thing she can
st.vr.sita_drops_her_ornaments.lesson: When almost nothing is in your hands, the small thing that is can still be done.
st.vr.sita_drops_her_ornaments.summary: Sita is in the air, held by Ravana, with the forest falling away below. Jatayu is down. No one is coming. On a hilltop she notices five monkeys looking up. She has seconds, and almost nothing she can do.

st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.title: Ram's grief and Lakshman's counsel
st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.lesson: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.
st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.title: Ram's grief and Lakshman's counsel
st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.lesson: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.
st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.title: Ram's grief and Lakshman's counsel
st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.lesson: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.
st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.title: Valmiki: Ram cremates Jatayu like his father
st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.lesson: Grief for a loyal friend, even a bird, is real grief; honour it fully.
st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.summary: Jatayu dies telling Ram where Ravana went. Ram says this loss weighs on him more than Sita's abduction, that the bird is as worthy of honour as his father Dasharatha, builds the pyre himself and performs the rites as for his own kin.

st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.title: Kabandha: find a friend who understands
st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.lesson: When you are lost, look for someone who has been through the same thing.
st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.summary: Freed from a curse, the creature Kabandha tells the grieving brothers to seek out Sugriva, an exile who has also lost his wife and home. Only a friend in the same trouble, he says, can help them now.

st.vr.shabari_waits.title: Shabari's long wait
st.vr.shabari_waits.lesson: Faithful waiting, unseen by the world, is not wasted.
st.vr.shabari_waits.summary: The old ascetic woman Shabari has lived for years at Pampa after her teachers died, told that Ram would one day come. She has kept gathering forest food for him. When he arrives, she welcomes him, shows him her teachers' forest, and departs in peace.

st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.title: Grief in springtime at Pampa
st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.lesson: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.
st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.summary: At the beautiful lake of Pampa in spring, everything reminds Ram of Sita and his grief deepens. Lakshman tells him there is no strength greater than enthusiasm, and to rouse himself.

st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.
st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.

st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.
st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.

st.vr.ram_asks_a_monkey_for_help.title: The one everyone leaned on has to ask for help
st.vr.ram_asks_a_monkey_for_help.lesson: Even the one who has sheltered everyone may need shelter, and asking for it plainly is no fall.
st.vr.ram_asks_a_monkey_for_help.summary: All his life Ram has been the one others came to. Princes, sages, a whole city looked to him for protection. Now he stands before a monkey's envoy with no kingdom, no wife and no plan, and has to say: we need your master's help.

st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.title: Ram and Sugriva's friendship
st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.lesson: Two people in trouble can carry each other.
st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.summary: Ram and Sugriva swear friendship before a fire. Sugriva shows Ram the jewels Sita dropped; Ram breaks down, and Sugriva comforts him: in trouble the steady person thinks it through, and a friend is the greatest refuge.

st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.title: The cave: how two brothers fell apart
st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.lesson: Many family rifts start with a misunderstanding neither side stops to check.
st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.summary: Vali chases a demon into a cave and tells Sugriva to wait. A year later blood flows out and no voice answers; Sugriva seals the cave in grief and is made king. Vali escapes, believes he was betrayed, and refuses every apology, driving Sugriva out.

st.vr.sugriva_needs_proof_before_he_trus.title: Sugriva asks for proof, and Ram is not offended
st.vr.sugriva_needs_proof_before_he_trus.lesson: Someone who has been burned may ask for proof, and a true friend gives it without taking offence.
st.vr.sugriva_needs_proof_before_he_trus.summary: Ram has promised to deal with Vali. Sugriva wants to believe it. He has also seen Vali throw a demon's carcass a mile and put arrows through great sal trees. He has trusted once and lost everything. He cannot stake his life on a new friend's word.

st.vr.sugriva_let_down_in_the_first_duel.title: Sugriva is beaten while his ally stands watching
st.vr.sugriva_let_down_in_the_first_duel.lesson: When a friend's failure hurts you, say so to him; a true friend answers with the reason and a remedy.
st.vr.sugriva_let_down_in_the_first_duel.summary: On Ram's word, Sugriva walks up to Kishkindha and challenges the brother who terrifies him. Vali comes out and beats him bloody. Sugriva keeps looking toward the trees where Ram is hidden with his bow. No arrow comes. He runs for his life.

st.vr.tara_warns_vali.title: Tara's warning
st.vr.tara_warns_vali.lesson: Anger rushes; good counsel says wait until morning, and remember who family is.
st.vr.tara_warns_vali.summary: Sugriva roars a second challenge and Vali storms out to fight. His wife Tara stops him: drop this anger, fight tomorrow if you must, make peace with your brother, who is your own family. Vali will not listen.

st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.title: Vali's last words
st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.lesson: Rivalry seems huge until the end; then only the relationship matters.
st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.summary: Struck down by Ram's arrow during the duel, Vali rebukes Ram, then makes his peace. To Sugriva he says: don't hold my faults against me; we could not have both brotherhood and kingdom. He entrusts his son to his brother and tells Angada how to live.

st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.title: Vali's last words
st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.lesson: Rivalry seems huge until the end; then only the relationship matters.
st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.summary: Struck down by Ram's arrow during the duel, Vali rebukes Ram, then makes his peace. To Sugriva he says: don't hold my faults against me; we could not have both brotherhood and kingdom. He entrusts his son to his brother and tells Angada how to live.

st.vr.tara_widowed_asks_to_follow.title: Tara, suddenly widowed, is told to think of her son
st.vr.tara_widowed_asks_to_follow.lesson: In fresh grief a person needs to be held, and the duties come back in their own time.
st.vr.tara_widowed_asks_to_follow.summary: Tara had warned Vali not to go out to fight. An hour later he is lying on the ground with an arrow in his chest. She clings to the body and will not be moved, and everyone around her starts telling her what she must do now.

st.vr.sugriva_won_and_cannot_bear_it.title: Sugriva's remorse
st.vr.sugriva_won_and_cannot_bear_it.lesson: Winning against family rarely feels like winning.
st.vr.sugriva_won_and_cannot_bear_it.summary: Sugriva has won, but seeing Tara's grief he is crushed by remorse: how could anyone enjoy a kingdom bought with a brother's life? He remembers Vali only ever said 'don't do it again.'

st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.title: Waiting out the monsoon
st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.lesson: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.
st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.summary: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.

st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.title: Sugriva forgets his promise
st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.lesson: Comfort makes us forget our promises; a true friend reminds us in time.
st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.summary: Restored to his throne, Sugriva sinks into pleasure and forgets his promise to search for Sita. Hanuman warns him that help given late counts for little. Autumn comes; angry, Ram sends Lakshman, and Hanuman counsels the frightened Sugriva to bear harsh words and keep faith.

st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.title: Sugriva forgets his promise
st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.lesson: Comfort makes us forget our promises; a true friend reminds us in time.
st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.summary: Restored to his throne, Sugriva sinks into pleasure and forgets his promise to search for Sita. Hanuman warns him that help given late counts for little. Autumn comes; angry, Ram sends Lakshman, and Hanuman counsels the frightened Sugriva to bear harsh words and keep faith.

st.vr.tara_calms_lakshman.title: Tara calms Lakshman
st.vr.tara_calms_lakshman.lesson: A calm voice can turn a confrontation into an apology on both sides.
st.vr.tara_calms_lakshman.summary: Lakshman storms into Kishkindha, bow twanging. Tara meets him with reason and courtesy: strong people think before anger takes over; bear the slip of someone on your side. Sugriva apologises and Lakshman asks forgiveness for his own harsh words.

st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.title: Tara calms Lakshman
st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.lesson: A calm voice can turn a confrontation into an apology on both sides.
st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.summary: Lakshman storms into Kishkindha, bow twanging. Tara meets him with reason and courtesy: strong people think before anger takes over; bear the slip of someone on your side. Sugriva apologises and Lakshman asks forgiveness for his own harsh words.

st.vr.angada_deadline_missed.title: The missed deadline
st.vr.angada_deadline_missed.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.
st.vr.angada_deadline_missed.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.

st.vr.sampati_lived_on_for_a_reason.title: Sampati, the bird who could not fly
st.vr.sampati_lived_on_for_a_reason.lesson: Even when you feel useless, your experience may be exactly what someone needs.
st.vr.sampati_lived_on_for_a_reason.summary: The despairing monkeys meet Sampati, Jatayu's old brother, whose wings burnt long ago. A sage once told him to live on, because one day his knowledge would be needed. Now he tells them Sita is in Lanka, and his wings grow back.

st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.
st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.

st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.
st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.

st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.title: Hanuman's leap
st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.

st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.title: Hanuman's leap
st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.

st.vr.hanuman_uneasy_in_ravanas_chambers.title: Hanuman's unease in Ravana's chambers
st.vr.hanuman_uneasy_in_ravanas_chambers.lesson: Judge yourself by your intention and your mind's state, not only by what your eyes happened to meet while doing your duty.
st.vr.hanuman_uneasy_in_ravanas_chambers.summary: Searching Ravana's palace at night, Hanuman finds himself looking across Ravana's sleeping wives and is seized by fear that he has broken dharma. He examines his own mind, finds it unmoved, reasons that the search itself required it, and goes on searching with a clear conscience.

st.vr.hanuman_despair_and_self_talk_in_l.title: Hanuman's search and near despair
st.vr.hanuman_despair_and_self_talk_in_l.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.
st.vr.hanuman_despair_and_self_talk_in_l.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.

st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.title: Hanuman's search and near despair
st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.
st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.

st.vr.sita_blade_of_grass.title: Sita refuses Ravana
st.vr.sita_blade_of_grass.lesson: Power and money cannot buy what you refuse to sell.
st.vr.sita_blade_of_grass.summary: Ravana comes to the grove offering Sita wealth and power, and threatens her with death if she refuses. Trembling, she places a blade of grass between them and refuses: she cannot be bought, and he should return her before he destroys himself.

st.vr.sita_at_the_end_of_her_strength.title: Sita in captivity
st.vr.sita_at_the_end_of_her_strength.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.
st.vr.sita_at_the_end_of_her_strength.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.

st.vr.trijata_dream.title: Sita in captivity
st.vr.trijata_dream.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.
st.vr.trijata_dream.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.

st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.title: How Hanuman spoke to Sita
st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.lesson: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.
st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.summary: Hanuman has found Sita but she is terrified. He thinks carefully: speak in ordinary language, not court Sanskrit; don't gamble on a fight; start by gently praising Ram so she can trust him. He sings Ram's story softly from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time: joy comes to the one who stays alive.

st.vr.sita_fears_it_is_another_trick.title: How Hanuman spoke to Sita
st.vr.sita_fears_it_is_another_trick.lesson: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.
st.vr.sita_fears_it_is_another_trick.summary: Hanuman has found Sita but she is terrified. He thinks carefully: speak in ordinary language, not court Sanskrit; don't gamble on a fight; start by gently praising Ram so she can trust him. He sings Ram's story softly from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time: joy comes to the one who stays alive.

st.vr.sita_refuses_the_easy_rescue.title: How Hanuman spoke to Sita
st.vr.sita_refuses_the_easy_rescue.lesson: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.
st.vr.sita_refuses_the_easy_rescue.summary: Hanuman has found Sita but she is terrified. He thinks carefully: speak in ordinary language, not court Sanskrit; don't gamble on a fight; start by gently praising Ram so she can trust him. He sings Ram's story softly from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time: joy comes to the one who stays alive.

st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.title: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka
st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.lesson: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.summary: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.

st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.title: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka
st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.lesson: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.summary: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.

st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.title: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka
st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.lesson: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.summary: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.

st.vr.hanuman_burns_lanka_then_panics.title: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka
st.vr.hanuman_burns_lanka_then_panics.lesson: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
st.vr.hanuman_burns_lanka_then_panics.summary: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.

st.vr.monkeys_raid_the_honey_garden.title: The team comes home with good news and celebrates a little too hard
st.vr.monkeys_raid_the_honey_garden.lesson: A wise leader reads what a team's behaviour says before reacting to it.
st.vr.monkeys_raid_the_honey_garden.summary: The search party is back from Lanka with news that Sita is found. On the way home they come to Madhuvana, the king's guarded honey garden. Angada, with Jambavan's nod, lets them drink. They wreck the place and beat the guards.

st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.title: Ram thanks Hanuman
st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.lesson: When you can't repay a kindness, give what you have: thanks, and your heart.
st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.summary: Hanuman returns with Sita's jewel and her message. Ram is overwhelmed: Hanuman has saved them all, and Ram, an exile, has nothing to give in return, so he embraces him.

st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.title: Ram thanks Hanuman
st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.lesson: When you can't repay a kindness, give what you have: thanks, and your heart.
st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.summary: Hanuman returns with Sita's jewel and her message. Ram is overwhelmed: Hanuman has saved them all, and Ram, an exile, has nothing to give in return, so he embraces him.

st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.title: Vibhishana tells his brother the truth
st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.lesson: Speak the truth to family even when it costs you; leave if you must, without hatred.
st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.summary: In Ravana's war council, everyone else flatters him. Vibhishana alone says what he has seen: return Sita, avoid war. Ravana insults him as a traitor. Vibhishana says flatterers are easy to find and truth-tellers rare, wishes his brother well, and leaves.

st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.title: Ram takes in the enemy's brother
st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.lesson: Give a second chance to someone who comes to you sincerely, even across old lines.
st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.summary: Vibhishana arrives at Ram's camp. The allies suspect a spy; Hanuman reads him as sincere. Ram decides: he will not turn away anyone who comes in friendship, even with faults; whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' he will protect.

st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.title: Ram at the ocean: humble first, firm after
st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.lesson: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.
st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.summary: Ram lies on kusha grass by the shore for three days, asking the ocean for a way. Ignored, he tells Lakshman that patience is being taken for weakness and takes up his bow. The ocean rises, offers a way (Nala's bridge), and Ram releases the arrow elsewhere at its request.

st.vr.ram_lets_the_spies_go.title: Enemy spies are caught in his camp and Ram lets them walk around
st.vr.ram_lets_the_spies_go.lesson: One who is prepared and in the right need not fear being seen.
st.vr.ram_lets_the_spies_go.summary: Ravana sends two ministers, Shuka and Sarana, disguised as monkeys, to count Ram's army. Vibhishana catches them and drags them to Ram. They are terrified.

st.vr.sita_shown_a_false_head.title: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house
st.vr.sita_shown_a_false_head.lesson: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.
st.vr.sita_shown_a_false_head.summary: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.

st.vr.ravana_would_rather_break_than_ben.title: Ravana is told by the elders to make peace and says he will break before he bows
st.vr.ravana_would_rather_break_than_ben.lesson: Pride that knows itself and still will not bend brings down everything around it.
st.vr.ravana_would_rather_break_than_ben.summary: Ram's army is at the walls. Malyavan, Ravana's old maternal grandfather, counsels him in council: make peace; you have turned from dharma; the signs are against us. The king has heard this before from his brother and his ministers.

st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.title: Ram lets Ravana go to rest
st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.lesson: Real strength can afford to be generous; pride is what breaks a person.
st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.summary: In their first fight, Ram shatters Ravana's chariot, bow and crown. Instead of killing his exhausted enemy he tells him to go home, rest and come back. Ravana goes back to Lanka humbled, his pride broken.

st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.title: Kumbhakarna's loyalty
st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.lesson: You can tell family the hard truth and still stand by them; humility does, boasting talks.
st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.summary: Woken from months of sleep, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana bluntly that his pride caused this disaster and he acted in the wrong order. Then, loyal to his brother, he goes out to fight anyway, scorning boastful courtiers: the brave don't praise themselves, they act.

st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.title: Lakshman struck down
st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.lesson: When someone you love is gravely ill, remember what they mean to you, and do what can be done.
st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.summary: Ravana's spear fells Lakshman. Ram breaks down: even victory means nothing without his brother, who comforted him in every low moment. The physician Sushena sees Lakshman still breathes and sends Hanuman for the healing herbs; Hanuman brings back the mountain peak.

st.vr.ram_exhausted_before_the_last_figh.title: Ram stands exhausted and anxious before the final battle
st.vr.ram_exhausted_before_the_last_figh.lesson: Before the hardest moment, draw strength from what is greater than you, then act.
st.vr.ram_exhausted_before_the_last_figh.summary: After days of war, Ram is worn out. Ravana is in front of him, ready for the final fight. Ram stands there sunk in thought, weighed down with worry.

st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.title: Vibhishana mourns Ravana
st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.lesson: Grief for someone who wronged you is real; death ends the fight.
st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.summary: Ravana is dead. Vibhishana weeps for the brother who drove him out and hesitates to perform his rites. Ram tells him enmity ends at death and Ravana is now his to honour. Mandodari mourns: once he mastered his desires and won the world; in the end his desires mastered him.

st.vr.mandodari_grieves_a_husband_who_di.title: Mandodari mourns a husband she loved and could not save from himself
st.vr.mandodari_grieves_a_husband_who_di.lesson: One can mourn someone and still see plainly how they brought their fall upon themselves.
st.vr.mandodari_grieves_a_husband_who_di.summary: Ravana's chief queen kneels by his body on the battlefield. She was proud of him: her father a king of the danavas, her husband lord of the rakshasas, her son the conqueror of Indra. All of it is gone, because of a desire she watched him fail to let go of.

st.vr.sita_will_not_punish_her_guards.title: Sita spares her guards
st.vr.sita_will_not_punish_her_guards.lesson: Mercy toward those who hurt you is a strength, not a weakness.
st.vr.sita_will_not_punish_her_guards.summary: Hanuman brings Sita the news of victory and offers to punish the guards who tormented her. She refuses: they were following orders, and no one is without fault; show compassion even to those who wronged you.

st.vr.sita_answers_public_suspicion.title: Sita answers unjust suspicion
st.vr.sita_answers_public_suspicion.lesson: Being doubted by someone close is a deep injustice; you are allowed to name it.
st.vr.sita_answers_public_suspicion.summary: After the war Ram publicly doubts Sita. She answers with dignity: why speak to me like a stranger? After all our years together, if you don't know me, that loss is permanent. She then walks into fire to prove what should not have needed proof.

st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.title: Ram hurries home
st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.lesson: Homecoming is about people, not possessions; don't let property come between siblings.
st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.summary: Victorious, Ram refuses Lanka's honours: his heart is in a hurry to see Bharata. Near Ayodhya he sends Hanuman ahead to read Bharata's face, saying if Bharata now wants the kingdom, let him keep it.

st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.title: Bharata's fourteen-year wait ends
st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.lesson: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.summary: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.

st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.title: Valmiki: Hanuman's boon and Ram's debt
st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.lesson: The deepest gratitude hopes the other never needs your help.
st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.summary: After the coronation Ram sends his friends home, asking only to be remembered with love. Hanuman asks to live as long as Ram's story is told, so that hearing it can ease his longing. Ram rises from the throne, embraces him, grants it, and says he would give his life for each of Hanuman's services, and hopes Hanuman never falls into trouble that would let him repay it.

st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.title: King Nriga and the petitioners who waited
st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.lesson: Delay is a decision too; people waiting on you are paying for it.
st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.summary: After four days of neglecting his work, Ram calls in everyone waiting, and tells of King Nriga: two men brought him a dispute, waited for days at his gate and were never admitted, and their anger cost him dearly.

st.vr.lakshman_carries_out_the_order_he_.title: Sita left in the forest
st.vr.lakshman_carries_out_the_order_he_.lesson: Injustice from those we love is real grief; a stranger's kindness can become home.
st.vr.lakshman_carries_out_the_order_he_.summary: Hearing that people gossip about Sita's time in Lanka, Ram orders Lakshman to leave her, pregnant, near Valmiki's hermitage. Lakshman obeys in anguish. Sita grieves that she is cut off from everyone and slandered though innocent. Valmiki finds her, says he knows she is blameless, and tells her to treat his home as her own.

st.vr.sita_abandoned_and_still_herself.title: Sita left in the forest
st.vr.sita_abandoned_and_still_herself.lesson: Injustice from those we love is real grief; a stranger's kindness can become home.
st.vr.sita_abandoned_and_still_herself.summary: Hearing that people gossip about Sita's time in Lanka, Ram orders Lakshman to leave her, pregnant, near Valmiki's hermitage. Lakshman obeys in anguish. Sita grieves that she is cut off from everyone and slandered though innocent. Valmiki finds her, says he knows she is blameless, and tells her to treat his home as her own.

st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.title: Ram takes his brother's advice
st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.lesson: Leaders who change their minds on good advice earn more trust, not less.
st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.summary: Ram proposes a great imperial sacrifice. Bharata gently objects that it would bring suffering to many kings and people. Ram listens and changes course, saying good advice should be taken even from the young.

st.vr.sita_will_not_prove_herself_again.title: Sita refuses to prove herself again
st.vr.sita_will_not_prove_herself_again.lesson: There is a point where you stop proving yourself to people who will not believe you.
st.vr.sita_will_not_prove_herself_again.summary: Years later, Valmiki brings Sita before Ram's assembly. Ram admits he knew she was innocent but gave in to gossip, and asks her to swear her purity once more. Sita calls on the earth instead, and the earth takes her back; she does not return.

st.vr.lakshman_takes_the_curse_on_himsel.title: Lakshman chooses to break a rule and pay for it alone, to save everyone else
st.vr.lakshman_takes_the_curse_on_himsel.lesson: One who takes the cost on himself so that others are spared acts from a love larger than fear.
st.vr.lakshman_takes_the_curse_on_himsel.summary: Ram is in a private meeting and has vowed that anyone who interrupts will be put to death; Lakshman guards the door. The irascible sage Durvasa arrives demanding to see Ram at once, or he will curse Ram, Bharata, the city and all their descendants.

st.vr.guha_offers_everything_to_a_fallen.title: A friend offers his whole kingdom to Ram on the first night of exile
st.vr.guha_offers_everything_to_a_fallen.lesson: A true friend comes on foot at the low point and offers all; a true friend can accept love while declining gifts.
st.vr.guha_offers_everything_to_a_fallen.summary: Ram, yesterday's crown prince, arrives on the Ganga bank in bark clothes. Guha, chief of the Nishada hunters and his old friend, comes on foot to meet him and is shaken to see him like this.

st.vr.lakshman_cannot_sleep_while_ram_sl.title: Lakshman will not sleep on the first night of exile
st.vr.lakshman_cannot_sleep_while_ram_sl.lesson: When someone we love is brought low, keeping watch beside them is itself a form of love.
st.vr.lakshman_cannot_sleep_while_ram_sl.summary: On the banks of the Ganga, Ram and Sita are asleep on a bed of grass on the ground. Guha offers Lakshman a proper bed. Lakshman stands awake, watching his brother sleep in the dirt and thinking of their father at home.

st.vr.sita_faces_ravana_at_the_hut.title: Sita realises the holy man at her door is Ravana and does not shrink
st.vr.sita_faces_ravana_at_the_hut.lesson: Dignity speaks the truth to a predator even when it cannot stop him.
st.vr.sita_faces_ravana_at_the_hut.summary: She has just welcomed a mendicant into the hut, given him a seat and water, as she would any guest. Ram and Lakshman are both away. Now the guest reveals himself: he is Ravana, lord of Lanka, and she is to be his chief queen.

prasang:bg.p01.1.title: The great warriors of both armies are named
prasang:bg.p01.1.lesson: Insecurity shows in how we size up rivals before anything has happened.
prasang:bg.p01.1.summary: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened at Kurukshetra. Sanjaya describes Duryodhana going to Drona and nervously naming the great warriors on both sides.

prasang:bg.p01.2.title: The conches sound on both sides
prasang:bg.p01.2.lesson: Before any hard moment there is noise and bravado; the real test comes after.
prasang:bg.p01.2.summary: Bhishma roars and blows his conch; Krishna, Arjuna and the Pandava brothers answer with their own. The sound shakes the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.

prasang:bg.p01.3.title: Arjuna surveys the armies
prasang:bg.p01.3.lesson: Sometimes the hardest moment is simply seeing clearly who is on the other side.
prasang:bg.p01.3.summary: Arjuna asks Krishna to place the chariot between the two armies. Looking across, he sees teachers, uncles, cousins, friends and in-laws ready to fight.

prasang:bg.p01.4.title: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang:bg.p01.4.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
prasang:bg.p01.4.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.

prasang:bg.p02.1.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang:bg.p02.1.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
prasang:bg.p02.1.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.

prasang:bg.p02.2.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang:bg.p02.2.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
prasang:bg.p02.2.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.

prasang:bg.p02.3.title: Why a warrior must fight: duty
prasang:bg.p02.3.lesson: Decide from steadiness, not from fear of winning or losing.
prasang:bg.p02.3.summary: Krishna appeals to Arjuna's sense of duty and honour, then tells him to treat victory and defeat alike before he acts.

prasang:bg.p02.4.title: The yoga of action
prasang:bg.p02.4.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
prasang:bg.p02.4.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.

prasang:bg.p02.5.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang:bg.p02.5.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.
prasang:bg.p02.5.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.

prasang:bg.p03.1.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang:bg.p03.1.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.
prasang:bg.p03.1.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.

prasang:bg.p03.2.title: Why action as offering is needed
prasang:bg.p03.2.lesson: Life works by give and take; taking only for yourself breaks the cycle.
prasang:bg.p03.2.summary: Krishna describes action as offering, the mutual nourishing of humans and gods, and the wrong of taking without giving back.

prasang:bg.p03.3.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang:bg.p03.3.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.
prasang:bg.p03.3.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.

prasang:bg.p03.4.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang:bg.p03.4.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
prasang:bg.p03.4.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.

prasang:bg.p03.5.title: Restraining desire
prasang:bg.p03.5.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.
prasang:bg.p03.5.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.

prasang:bg.p04.1.title: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasang:bg.p04.1.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.
prasang:bg.p04.1.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.

prasang:bg.p04.2.title: How the great yogis live
prasang:bg.p04.2.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.
prasang:bg.p04.2.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.

prasang:bg.p04.3.title: The many kinds of offering and their fruits
prasang:bg.p04.3.lesson: Every act, even eating, can be done as an offering.
prasang:bg.p04.3.summary: Krishna lists kinds of sacrifice: of senses, breath, wealth, study, and more, and says all are born of action.

prasang:bg.p04.4.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang:bg.p04.4.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.
prasang:bg.p04.4.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.

prasang:bg.p05.1.title: Knowledge or action: the verdict
prasang:bg.p05.1.lesson: Real letting go is inner: no grudges, no grasping.
prasang:bg.p05.1.summary: Arjuna wants one clear verdict. Krishna says both lead to the good, but selfless action is better, and the true renouncer is the one who neither hates nor craves.

prasang:bg.p05.2.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang:bg.p05.2.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
prasang:bg.p05.2.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.

prasang:bg.p05.3.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang:bg.p05.3.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.
prasang:bg.p05.3.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.

prasang:bg.p05.4.title: Meditation with devotion
prasang:bg.p05.4.lesson: You are not alone: the divine is the friend of every being.
prasang:bg.p05.4.summary: A short sketch of meditation: senses withdrawn, free of desire, fear and anger, knowing the divine as the friend of all beings.

prasang:bg.p06.1.title: Action, and the one established in yoga
prasang:bg.p06.1.lesson: Quitting isn't renouncing; working without clinging is.
prasang:bg.p06.1.summary: The true renouncer is the one who does the work that ought to be done without depending on its fruit, not the one who simply stops.

prasang:bg.p06.2.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang:bg.p06.2.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
prasang:bg.p06.2.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.

prasang:bg.p06.3.title: Meditation in detail
prasang:bg.p06.3.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.
prasang:bg.p06.3.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.

prasang:bg.p06.4.title: Mastering the mind
prasang:bg.p06.4.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.
prasang:bg.p06.4.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.

prasang:bg.p06.5.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang:bg.p06.5.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.
prasang:bg.p06.5.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.

prasang:bg.p07.1.title: Knowledge with realisation
prasang:bg.p07.1.lesson: Everything is held together by one thread.
prasang:bg.p07.1.summary: Krishna promises complete knowledge and describes his lower nature (elements, mind, ego) and higher nature (life itself), on which the world is strung like pearls on a thread.

prasang:bg.p07.2.title: The Lord as the cause within all things
prasang:bg.p07.2.lesson: Strength and desire are good when free of greed and within what's right.
prasang:bg.p07.2.summary: Krishna says he is the taste in water and the light in sun and moon, strength without greed, and desire that does not oppose what is right.

prasang:bg.p07.3.title: The deluded and the devoted
prasang:bg.p07.3.lesson: Whatever brings you to the search, distress, curiosity or need, is welcome.
prasang:bg.p07.3.summary: Most are deluded by the play of qualities. Four kinds of good people turn to the divine: the distressed, the curious, those in need, and the wise.

prasang:bg.p07.4.title: Worship of other deities
prasang:bg.p07.4.lesson: Sincere faith, in whatever form, is strengthened.
prasang:bg.p07.4.summary: Those who worship other forms with faith have that faith made steady by Krishna, though their gains are limited.

prasang:bg.p07.5.title: Those who miss the Lord and those who know him
prasang:bg.p07.5.lesson: Pull and push of like and dislike are what confuse us.
prasang:bg.p07.5.summary: The deluded see only the outer form; desire and aversion confuse all beings. Those freed from confusion come to know the divine fully.

prasang:bg.p08.1.title: Arjuna's seven questions and their answers
prasang:bg.p08.1.lesson: What you dwell on shapes who you become.
prasang:bg.p08.1.summary: Krishna defines key terms and says that what one dwells on at death shapes where one goes, so remember the divine always and keep working.

prasang:bg.p08.2.title: The yoga of devotion
prasang:bg.p08.2.lesson: A mind trained by practice reaches what it rests on.
prasang:bg.p08.2.summary: Krishna describes meditating at the time of death, the cosmic days and nights of Brahma, and the imperishable beyond them.

prasang:bg.p08.3.title: The bright and the dark paths
prasang:bg.p08.3.lesson: Know your direction and stay steady.
prasang:bg.p08.3.summary: Krishna describes two paths after death, one of light leading to non-return and one of smoke leading to return.

prasang:bg.p09.1.title: Knowledge and its power
prasang:bg.p09.1.lesson: The sacred is closer than it seems.
prasang:bg.p09.1.summary: Krishna calls this the king of knowledge and says he pervades all things without being contained by them.

prasang:bg.p09.2.title: How the world arises
prasang:bg.p09.2.lesson: Change is the nature of the world.
prasang:bg.p09.2.summary: At the end of each cycle beings return to Krishna's nature, and he sends them forth again, unbound by the work.

prasang:bg.p09.3.title: Those who scorn the Lord, and how the devoted worship
prasang:bg.p09.3.lesson: Don't overlook the sacred in the ordinary.
prasang:bg.p09.3.summary: The deluded overlook the divine in human form; the great-souled worship with steady devotion.

prasang:bg.p09.4.title: The Lord as the Self of all
prasang:bg.p09.4.lesson: The divine is mother, father, friend and refuge.
prasang:bg.p09.4.summary: Krishna lists himself as the ritual, the offering, father, mother, friend, refuge, being and non-being.

prasang:bg.p09.5.title: Worship with and without desire, and their fruits
prasang:bg.p09.5.lesson: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.
prasang:bg.p09.5.summary: Those who worship for heavenly rewards return when merit runs out; those who think of him alone are carried and protected.

prasang:bg.p09.6.title: The glory of selfless devotion
prasang:bg.p09.6.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.
prasang:bg.p09.6.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.

prasang:bg.p10.1.title: The Lord's glories, and the fruit of knowing them
prasang:bg.p10.1.lesson: All our qualities have one source.
prasang:bg.p10.1.summary: Krishna says even gods don't know his origin; understanding, patience, truth, joy, fear and fearlessness all come from him.

prasang:bg.p10.2.title: The yoga of devotion and its fruit
prasang:bg.p10.2.lesson: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.
prasang:bg.p10.2.summary: Devotees talk of the divine with each other and find joy; out of compassion Krishna lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts.

prasang:bg.p10.3.title: Arjuna praises Krishna and asks to hear his glories
prasang:bg.p10.3.lesson: Curiosity about the sacred is itself a beginning.
prasang:bg.p10.3.summary: Arjuna affirms what he has heard and asks Krishna to describe his manifestations, saying he never tires of hearing.

prasang:bg.p10.4.title: Krishna describes his glories
prasang:bg.p10.4.lesson: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.
prasang:bg.p10.4.summary: Krishna lists his manifestations: among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga, and ends by saying any excellence is a spark of his splendour.

prasang:bg.p11.1.title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
prasang:bg.p11.1.lesson: Ask humbly for what you long to see.
prasang:bg.p11.1.summary: Thanking Krishna for dispelling his confusion, Arjuna asks to see his imperishable form if he is able.
