She tells the story of a hermit changed by keeping a sword. Ram thanks her, saying no one advises a person they don't care about, and explains his promise to protect the sages.

prasang:vr.p.maricha_warns.title: Maricha warns Ravana
prasang:vr.p.maricha_warns.lesson: Listen hardest to the advice you least want to hear.
prasang:vr.p.maricha_warns.summary: Ravana asks Maricha to help him abduct Sita. Maricha, who has met Ram before, warns him again and again: flatterers are many, truth-tellers rare, and those heading for a fall reject good advice. Ravana threatens him until he agrees.

prasang:vr.p.golden_deer.title: The golden deer
prasang:vr.p.golden_deer.lesson: When something looks too perfect to be real, pause before you chase it.
prasang:vr.p.golden_deer.summary: A dazzling deer with a golden, jewelled hide appears near the hut. Lakshman warns that no such deer exists; it must be a trick. Sita longs for it and Ram, captivated too, gives chase, leaving the hut exposed.

prasang:vr.p.jatayu.title: Jatayu, old and brave
prasang:vr.p.jatayu.lesson: Age is no reason to stop standing up for what's right; honour those who stood up for you.
prasang:vr.p.jatayu.summary: The aged vulture Jatayu wakes to see Ravana carrying Sita off. He warns him, then fights him alone and is mortally wounded. Later Ram finds him dying, hears his news, and cremates him with the honour due a father.

prasang:vr.p.ram_loses_sita.title: Ram's grief and Lakshman's counsel
prasang:vr.p.ram_loses_sita.lesson: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.
prasang:vr.p.ram_loses_sita.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

prasang:vr.p.kabandha.title: Kabandha: find a friend who understands
prasang:vr.p.kabandha.lesson: When you are lost, look for someone who has been through the same thing.
prasang:vr.p.kabandha.summary: Freed from a curse, the creature Kabandha tells the grieving brothers to seek out Sugriva, an exile who has also lost his wife and home. Only a friend in the same trouble, he says, can help them now.

prasang:vr.p.shabari.title: Shabari's long wait
prasang:vr.p.shabari.lesson: Faithful waiting, unseen by the world, is not wasted.
prasang:vr.p.shabari.summary: The old ascetic woman Shabari has lived for years at Pampa after her teachers died, told that Ram would one day come. She has kept gathering forest food for him. When he arrives, she welcomes him, shows him her teachers' forest, and departs in peace.

prasang:vr.p.pampa_grief.title: Grief in springtime at Pampa
prasang:vr.p.pampa_grief.lesson: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.
prasang:vr.p.pampa_grief.summary: At the beautiful lake of Pampa in spring, everything reminds Ram of Sita and his grief deepens. Lakshman tells him there is no strength greater than enthusiasm, and to rouse himself.

prasang:vr.p.sugriva_fear.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang:vr.p.sugriva_fear.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.
prasang:vr.p.sugriva_fear.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.

prasang:vr.p.friendship_pact.title: Ram and Sugriva's friendship
prasang:vr.p.friendship_pact.lesson: Two people in trouble can carry each other.
prasang:vr.p.friendship_pact.summary: Ram and Sugriva swear friendship before a fire. Sugriva shows Ram the jewels Sita dropped; Ram breaks down, and Sugriva comforts him: in trouble the steady person thinks it through, and a friend is the greatest refuge.

prasang:vr.p.cave_misunderstanding.title: The cave: how two brothers fell apart
prasang:vr.p.cave_misunderstanding.lesson: Many family rifts start with a misunderstanding neither side stops to check.
prasang:vr.p.cave_misunderstanding.summary: Vali chases a demon into a cave and tells Sugriva to wait. A year later blood flows out and no voice answers; Sugriva seals the cave in grief and is made king. Vali escapes, believes he was betrayed, and refuses every apology, driving Sugriva out.

prasang:vr.p.tara_warns_vali.title: Tara's warning
prasang:vr.p.tara_warns_vali.lesson: Anger rushes; good counsel says wait until morning, and remember who family is.
prasang:vr.p.tara_warns_vali.summary: Sugriva roars a second challenge and Vali storms out to fight. His wife Tara stops him: drop this anger, fight tomorrow if you must, make peace with your brother, who is your own family. Vali will not listen.

prasang:vr.p.vali_last_words.title: Vali's last words
prasang:vr.p.vali_last_words.lesson: Rivalry seems huge until the end; then only the relationship matters.
prasang:vr.p.vali_last_words.summary: Struck down by Ram's arrow during the duel, Vali rebukes Ram, then makes his peace. To Sugriva he says: don't hold my faults against me; we could not have both brotherhood and kingdom. He entrusts his son to his brother and tells Angada how to live.

prasang:vr.p.sugriva_remorse.title: Sugriva's remorse
prasang:vr.p.sugriva_remorse.lesson: Winning against family rarely feels like winning.
prasang:vr.p.sugriva_remorse.summary: Sugriva has won, but seeing Tara's grief he is crushed by remorse: how could anyone enjoy a kingdom bought with a brother's life? He remembers Vali only ever said 'don't do it again.'

prasang:vr.p.monsoon_wait.title: Waiting out the monsoon
prasang:vr.p.monsoon_wait.lesson: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.
prasang:vr.p.monsoon_wait.summary: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.

prasang:vr.p.sugriva_forgets.title: Sugriva forgets his promise
prasang:vr.p.sugriva_forgets.lesson: Comfort makes us forget our promises; a true friend reminds us in time.
prasang:vr.p.sugriva_forgets.summary: Restored to his throne, Sugriva sinks into pleasure and forgets his promise to search for Sita. Hanuman warns him that help given late counts for little. Autumn comes; angry, Ram sends Lakshman, and Hanuman counsels the frightened Sugriva to bear harsh words and keep faith.

prasang:vr.p.tara_calms_lakshman.title: Tara calms Lakshman
prasang:vr.p.tara_calms_lakshman.lesson: A calm voice can turn a confrontation into an apology on both sides.
prasang:vr.p.tara_calms_lakshman.summary: Lakshman storms into Kishkindha, bow twanging. Tara meets him with reason and courtesy: strong people think before anger takes over; bear the slip of someone on your side. Sugriva apologises and Lakshman asks forgiveness for his own harsh words.

prasang:vr.p.deadline_missed.title: The missed deadline
prasang:vr.p.deadline_missed.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.
prasang:vr.p.deadline_missed.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.

prasang:vr.p.sampati.title: Sampati, the bird who could not fly
prasang:vr.p.sampati.lesson: Even when you feel useless, your experience may be exactly what someone needs.
prasang:vr.p.sampati.summary: The despairing monkeys meet Sampati, Jatayu's old brother, whose wings burnt long ago. A sage once told him to live on, because one day his knowledge would be needed. Now he tells them Sita is in Lanka, and his wings grow back.

prasang:vr.p.jambavan_rouses.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
prasang:vr.p.jambavan_rouses.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.
prasang:vr.p.jambavan_rouses.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.

prasang:vr.p.hanuman_leap.title: Hanuman's leap
prasang:vr.p.hanuman_leap.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
prasang:vr.p.hanuman_leap.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.

prasang:vr.p.search_despair.title: Hanuman's search and near despair
prasang:vr.p.search_despair.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.
prasang:vr.p.search_despair.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.

prasang:vr.p.sita_refuses_ravana.title: Sita refuses Ravana
prasang:vr.p.sita_refuses_ravana.lesson: Power and money cannot buy what you refuse to sell.
prasang:vr.p.sita_refuses_ravana.summary: Ravana comes to the grove offering Sita wealth and power, and threatens her with death if she refuses. Trembling, she places a blade of grass between them and refuses: she cannot be bought, and he should return her before he destroys himself.

prasang:vr.p.sita_captivity_hope.title: Sita in captivity
prasang:vr.p.sita_captivity_hope.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.
prasang:vr.p.sita_captivity_hope.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.

prasang:vr.p.hanuman_speaks_to_sita.title: How Hanuman spoke to Sita
prasang:vr.p.hanuman_speaks_to_sita.lesson: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.
prasang:vr.p.hanuman_speaks_to_sita.summary: Hanuman has found Sita but she is terrified. He thinks carefully: speak in ordinary language, not court Sanskrit; don't gamble on a fight; start by gently praising Ram so she can trust him. He sings Ram's story softly from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time: joy comes to the one who stays alive.

prasang:vr.p.lanka_burning.title: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka
prasang:vr.p.lanka_burning.lesson: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
prasang:vr.p.lanka_burning.summary: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.

prasang:vr.p.ram_thanks_hanuman.title: Ram thanks Hanuman
prasang:vr.p.ram_thanks_hanuman.lesson: When you can't repay a kindness, give what you have: thanks, and your heart.
prasang:vr.p.ram_thanks_hanuman.summary: Hanuman returns with Sita's jewel and her message. Ram is overwhelmed: Hanuman has saved them all, and Ram, an exile, has nothing to give in return, so he embraces him.

prasang:vr.p.vibhishana_counsel.title: Vibhishana tells his brother the truth
prasang:vr.p.vibhishana_counsel.lesson: Speak the truth to family even when it costs you; leave if you must, without hatred.
prasang:vr.p.vibhishana_counsel.summary: In Ravana's war council, everyone else flatters him. Vibhishana alone says what he has seen: return Sita, avoid war. Ravana insults him as a traitor. Vibhishana says flatterers are easy to find and truth-tellers rare, wishes his brother well, and leaves.

prasang:vr.p.refuge.title: Ram takes in the enemy's brother
prasang:vr.p.refuge.lesson: Give a second chance to someone who comes to you sincerely, even across old lines.
prasang:vr.p.refuge.summary: Vibhishana arrives at Ram's camp. The allies suspect a spy; Hanuman reads him as sincere. Ram decides: he will not turn away anyone who comes in friendship, even with faults; whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' he will protect.

prasang:vr.p.bridge.title: Building the bridge
prasang:vr.p.bridge.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.
prasang:vr.p.bridge.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.

prasang:vr.p.sarama.title: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house
prasang:vr.p.sarama.lesson: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.
prasang:vr.p.sarama.summary: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.

prasang:vr.p.ravana_let_go.title: Ram lets Ravana go to rest
prasang:vr.p.ravana_let_go.lesson: Real strength can afford to be generous; pride is what breaks a person.
prasang:vr.p.ravana_let_go.summary: In their first fight, Ram shatters Ravana's chariot, bow and crown. Instead of killing his exhausted enemy he tells him to go home, rest and come back. Ravana goes back to Lanka humbled, his pride broken.

prasang:vr.p.kumbhakarna.title: Kumbhakarna's loyalty
prasang:vr.p.kumbhakarna.lesson: You can tell family the hard truth and still stand by them; humility does, boasting talks.
prasang:vr.p.kumbhakarna.summary: Woken from months of sleep, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana bluntly that his pride caused this disaster and he acted in the wrong order. Then, loyal to his brother, he goes out to fight anyway, scorning boastful courtiers: the brave don't praise themselves, they act.

prasang:vr.p.lakshman_struck.title: Lakshman struck down
prasang:vr.p.lakshman_struck.lesson: When someone you love is gravely ill, remember what they mean to you, and do what can be done.
prasang:vr.p.lakshman_struck.summary: Ravana's spear fells Lakshman. Ram breaks down: even victory means nothing without his brother, who comforted him in every low moment. The physician Sushena sees Lakshman still breathes and sends Hanuman for the healing herbs; Hanuman brings back the mountain peak.

prasang:vr.p.vibhishana_grieves.title: Vibhishana mourns Ravana
prasang:vr.p.vibhishana_grieves.lesson: Grief for someone who wronged you is real; death ends the fight.
prasang:vr.p.vibhishana_grieves.summary: Ravana is dead. Vibhishana weeps for the brother who drove him out and hesitates to perform his rites. Ram tells him enmity ends at death and Ravana is now his to honour. Mandodari mourns: once he mastered his desires and won the world; in the end his desires mastered him.

prasang:vr.p.sita_spares_guards.title: Sita spares her guards
prasang:vr.p.sita_spares_guards.lesson: Mercy toward those who hurt you is a strength, not a weakness.
prasang:vr.p.sita_spares_guards.summary: Hanuman brings Sita the news of victory and offers to punish the guards who tormented her. She refuses: they were following orders, and no one is without fault; show compassion even to those who wronged you.

prasang:vr.p.sita_answers_suspicion.title: Sita answers unjust suspicion
prasang:vr.p.sita_answers_suspicion.lesson: Being doubted by someone close is a deep injustice; you are allowed to name it.
prasang:vr.p.sita_answers_suspicion.summary: After the war Ram publicly doubts Sita. She answers with dignity: why speak to me like a stranger? After all our years together, if you don't know me, that loss is permanent. She then walks into fire to prove what should not have needed proof.

prasang:vr.p.ram_hurries_home.title: Ram hurries home
prasang:vr.p.ram_hurries_home.lesson: Homecoming is about people, not possessions; don't let property come between siblings.
prasang:vr.p.ram_hurries_home.summary: Victorious, Ram refuses Lanka's honours: his heart is in a hurry to see Bharata. Near Ayodhya he sends Hanuman ahead to read Bharata's face, saying if Bharata now wants the kingdom, let him keep it.

prasang:vr.p.bharata_waits.title: Bharata's fourteen-year wait ends
prasang:vr.p.bharata_waits.lesson: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
prasang:vr.p.bharata_waits.summary: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.

prasang:vr.p.ram_takes_advice.title: Ram takes his brother's advice
prasang:vr.p.ram_takes_advice.lesson: Leaders who change their minds on good advice earn more trust, not less.
prasang:vr.p.ram_takes_advice.summary: Ram proposes a great imperial sacrifice. Bharata gently objects that it would bring suffering to many kings and people. Ram listens and changes course, saying good advice should be taken even from the young.

prasang:vr.p.nriga.title: King Nriga and the petitioners who waited
prasang:vr.p.nriga.lesson: Delay is a decision too; people waiting on you are paying for it.
prasang:vr.p.nriga.summary: After four days of neglecting his work, Ram calls in everyone waiting, and tells of King Nriga: two men brought him a dispute, waited for days at his gate and were never admitted, and their anger cost him dearly.

prasang:vr.p.sita_left_in_forest.title: Sita left in the forest
prasang:vr.p.sita_left_in_forest.lesson: Injustice from those we love is real grief; a stranger's kindness can become home.
prasang:vr.p.sita_left_in_forest.summary: Hearing that people gossip about Sita's time in Lanka, Ram orders Lakshman to leave her, pregnant, near Valmiki's hermitage. Lakshman obeys in anguish. Sita grieves that she is cut off from everyone and slandered though innocent. Valmiki finds her, says he knows she is blameless, and tells her to treat his home as her own.

prasang:vr.p.sita_returns_to_earth.title: Sita refuses to prove herself again
prasang:vr.p.sita_returns_to_earth.lesson: There is a point where you stop proving yourself to people who will not believe you.
prasang:vr.p.sita_returns_to_earth.summary: Years later, Valmiki brings Sita before Ram's assembly. Ram admits he knew she was innocent but gave in to gossip, and asks her to swear her purity once more. Sita calls on the earth instead, and the earth takes her back; she does not return.

prasang:rcm.p.sant_asant.title: Tulsidas on good company and difficult people
prasang:rcm.p.sant_asant.lesson: The people around you shape your judgement; choose them, and take the good from everyone.
prasang:rcm.p.sant_asant.summary: Before the story begins, Tulsidas bows to good people and, with gentle irony, to troublesome ones too. He describes how each acts, why company shapes us, and how the wise take the good and leave the rest, like the swan taking milk from water.

prasang:rcm.p.tulsi_humility.title: Tulsidas on loving our own work
prasang:rcm.p.tulsi_humility.lesson: Notice whether you can be glad at someone else's good work, not only your own.
prasang:rcm.p.tulsi_humility.summary: Tulsidas calls his own poetry plain and asks readers to forgive it. Along the way he notes that everyone loves their own work, that few are glad at another's success, and that most people swell only with their own rising waters.

prasang:rcm.p.sati_doubt.title: Sati doubts, tests and hides it
prasang:rcm.p.sati_doubt.lesson: Doubt can be honest; hiding what you did is what breaks trust.
prasang:rcm.p.sati_doubt.summary: Sati sees Shiva bow to Ram, a grieving prince searching the forest, and cannot believe Ram is divine. Ignoring Shiva's advice, she tests Ram by taking Sita's form, is found out, and then lies to Shiva about it. Shiva quietly withdraws from her, and she lives with a guilt she cannot speak.

prasang:rcm.p.daksha_yajna.title: Sati goes to her father's sacrifice uninvited
prasang:rcm.p.daksha_yajna.lesson: You may go to family without an invitation, but not into open hostility; listen to that warning.
prasang:rcm.p.daksha_yajna.summary: Sati's father Daksha holds a great sacrifice and invites everyone except Shiva and her. Shiva warns her that going where there is hostility brings no good, but she goes. Her father ignores her and insults her husband in front of everyone, and the visit ends in catastrophe.

prasang:rcm.p.parvati_tapas.title: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang:rcm.p.parvati_tapas.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
prasang:rcm.p.parvati_tapas.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.

prasang:rcm.p.narada_pride.title: Narada's pride and the monkey face
prasang:rcm.p.narada_pride.lesson: The moment you boast of beating a weakness, it has found another way in.
prasang:rcm.p.narada_pride.summary: Narada conquers desire in meditation and cannot stop telling people about it. Vishnu creates a city and a princess's swayamvara; Narada falls for her and asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu, like a doctor refusing harmful food, gives him a monkey's face instead, and Narada is laughed out of the hall until he sees what his pride has done.

prasang:rcm.p.manu_shatarupa.title: Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life
prasang:rcm.p.manu_shatarupa.lesson: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.
prasang:rcm.p.manu_shatarupa.summary: King Manu and Queen Shatarupa realise in old age that a whole life has passed without what mattered most to them. They hand over the kingdom, go to the forest and practise austerity for years. When Vishnu offers a boon, Manu hesitates like a poor man before the wishing tree, then asks for a son like God himself.

prasang:rcm.p.ram_childhood.title: Kausalya and the child who ran from dinner
prasang:rcm.p.ram_childhood.lesson: The grandest thing about a child may be the ordinary hours of childhood itself.
prasang:rcm.p.ram_childhood.summary: At his birth Ram shows Kausalya his cosmic form, and she asks him instead to be simply a baby. Later scenes are pure childhood: the boy runs off mid-meal, curd on his face, dusty from play, while his father laughs and his mother chases him. When she once glimpses the whole universe in him again, she asks only to be spared that and keep her child.

prasang:rcm.p.vishwamitra.title: Dasharath lets his sons go
prasang:rcm.p.vishwamitra.lesson: Parents protect children best by letting them go when the time comes.
prasang:rcm.p.vishwamitra.summary: The sage Vishwamitra asks King Dasharath to send the teenage Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest rites from demons. Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, offers land, cows, treasure, even his own life instead. Vasishtha reasons with him, and he finally embraces the boys and hands them over.

prasang:rcm.p.bow.title: Janaka's despair and the bow
prasang:rcm.p.bow.lesson: Some moments do not wait; when it is time, act.
prasang:rcm.p.bow.summary: Ten thousand kings fail to lift Shiva's bow, and Janaka cries out that the earth has no heroes left. Lakshman bristles; Vishwamitra sends Ram forward. Ram sees Sita's anguish, knows that rain after the crops have dried is useless, lifts the bow and breaks it in a moment.

prasang:rcm.p.parashurama.title: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
prasang:rcm.p.parashurama.lesson: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.
prasang:rcm.p.parashurama.summary: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.

prasang:rcm.p.janaka_vidai.title: Janaka says goodbye to his daughter
prasang:rcm.p.janaka_vidai.lesson: Even the wisest parent breaks a little when a child leaves home; that is love.
prasang:rcm.p.janaka_vidai.summary: After the wedding the time comes for Sita to leave Mithila. The palace, even the pet parrots, are in tears. Janaka, known everywhere for his detachment, holds his daughter and loses all composure; his ministers have to remind him it is time.

prasang:rcm.p.coronation_eve.title: Ram's unease on the eve of his crowning
prasang:rcm.p.coronation_eve.lesson: Real affection for siblings feels uneasy when one is favoured over the rest.
prasang:rcm.p.coronation_eve.summary: Dasharath, noticing grey hairs, decides to crown Ram heir, and the whole city celebrates. When Vasishtha brings Ram the news, Ram's first thought is not joy but unease: the brothers were born, raised and married together, so why should only the eldest be crowned?

prasang:rcm.p.manthara.title: Manthara poisons Kaikeyi's mind
prasang:rcm.p.manthara.lesson: Advice that flatters your fears can turn a good heart; check who benefits from it.
prasang:rcm.p.manthara.summary: Kaikeyi is first delighted that Ram will be crowned; she loves him like her own son. Her maid Manthara works on her slowly, with sighs, hints and sweet-sounding fears about her future, until Kaikeyi believes her enemy is her only friend and goes to the sulking chamber to demand her two boons.

prasang:rcm.p.dasharath_promise.title: Dasharath's two promises
prasang:rcm.p.dasharath_promise.lesson: Promise only what you have thought through; a rash vow can cost what you love most.
prasang:rcm.p.dasharath_promise.summary: Dasharath finds Kaikeyi in the sulking chamber and, eager to please her, swears by Ram to grant anything. She asks for Bharat's coronation and fourteen years of exile for Ram. Bound by his word and his love, the king spends the night begging, raging and grieving, and by morning cannot speak.

prasang:rcm.p.exile_order.title: Ram hears he is to be exiled
prasang:rcm.p.exile_order.lesson: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.
prasang:rcm.p.exile_order.summary: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.

prasang:rcm.p.ram_kausalya.title: Kausalya lets her son go
prasang:rcm.p.ram_kausalya.lesson: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.
prasang:rcm.p.ram_kausalya.summary: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.

prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_sumitra.title: Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_sumitra.lesson: Home is where your people are; a good send-off gives values, not just tears.
prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_sumitra.summary: Ram asks Lakshman to stay and care for their old father and grieving mothers; Lakshman cannot imagine life apart from him. He goes to his mother Sumitra, afraid she will stop him. Instead she tells him that home is wherever Ram is, as day is wherever the sun shines, and gives him one piece of advice for the road.

prasang:rcm.p.nishad_lakshman.title: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram
prasang:rcm.p.nishad_lakshman.lesson: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.
prasang:rcm.p.nishad_lakshman.summary: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.

prasang:rcm.p.kevat.title: Kevat washes Ram's feet
prasang:rcm.p.kevat.lesson: Some exchanges can't be priced; gratitude can be payment enough.
prasang:rcm.p.kevat.summary: At the Ganga, a boatman refuses to take Ram across until he can wash his feet, joking that if the dust of those feet turned a stone into a woman, it might turn his boat, his family's livelihood, into one too. Ram laughs and agrees. On the far bank Sita offers her ring as fare, and Kevat refuses: after a lifetime of wages, today he has been paid in full.

prasang:rcm.p.bharat_return.title: Bharat comes home to grief
prasang:rcm.p.bharat_return.lesson: When someone is drowning in guilt for what others did, an embrace helps more than blame.
prasang:rcm.p.bharat_return.summary: Bharat returns from his uncle's home to a silent city. His mother tells him proudly what she arranged; he learns his father is dead and his brother exiled because of him. Overwhelmed with shame he goes to Kausalya, expecting blame, and she embraces him as if Ram had come back, telling him not to carry the loss as his shame.

prasang:rcm.p.vasishtha_bharat.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang:rcm.p.vasishtha_bharat.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.
prasang:rcm.p.vasishtha_bharat.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.

prasang:rcm.p.nishad_suspicion.title: Guha nearly fights Bharat
prasang:rcm.p.nishad_suspicion.lesson: Find out someone's intent before you prepare for war with them.
prasang:rcm.p.nishad_suspicion.summary: Seeing Bharat's army approach the Ganga, Guha assumes he is coming to kill Ram and prepares his men to die fighting. An old man reads the omens and says Bharat comes to bring Ram back. Guha agrees that fools act in haste and repent, goes to meet Bharat with gifts, and the two embrace.

prasang:rcm.p.bharadwaj.title: Bharadwaj lifts Bharat's shame
prasang:rcm.p.bharadwaj.lesson: You are not your family's mistakes; carry only what is yours.
prasang:rcm.p.bharadwaj.summary: At Prayag Bharat meets the sage Bharadwaj, too ashamed to speak. The sage tells him not to eat himself up over his mother's deed and that what Bharat sees as a stain is a lesson for everyone. Bharat answers that he fears neither the world's talk nor the afterlife; only the thought that Ram suffers because of him keeps him awake.

prasang:rcm.p.indra_brihaspati.title: Brihaspati checks Indra's envy
prasang:rcm.p.indra_brihaspati.lesson: Your fear of someone else's goodness usually says more about your interests than theirs.
prasang:rcm.p.indra_brihaspati.summary: Indra, king of the gods, fears that Bharat's devotion will bring Ram back and spoil the gods' plans, and wants to trick him. His teacher Brihaspati tells him that the world runs on action, that harming a good person backfires, and that his anxiety comes from his own self-interest, not from Bharat.

prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_anger.title: Lakshman assumes the worst about Bharat
prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_anger.lesson: Think before you act on an assumption; haste turns misunderstandings into wars.
prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_anger.summary: Forest dwellers report that Bharat is coming with an army. Lakshman, sure it is an attack, climbs a tree and swears to destroy him. A voice from the sky warns against acting in haste, and Ram explains that Bharat could never turn against him; power could not corrupt him.

prasang:rcm.p.chitrakoot_meeting.title: The brothers meet at Chitrakoot
prasang:rcm.p.chitrakoot_meeting.lesson: Forgiveness can mean going first to the person who hurt you and putting them at ease.
prasang:rcm.p.chitrakoot_meeting.summary: Bharat walks barefoot to Chitrakoot and falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him into his arms. Ram learns his father has died and grieves. When the queens arrive, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused it all, falls at her feet and comforts her, blaming no one.

prasang:rcm.p.chitrakoot_assembly.title: The family council at Chitrakoot
prasang:rcm.p.chitrakoot_assembly.lesson: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.
prasang:rcm.p.chitrakoot_assembly.summary: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.

prasang:rcm.p.janaka_chitrakoot.title: Janaka's family joins the council
prasang:rcm.p.janaka_chitrakoot.lesson: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.
prasang:rcm.p.janaka_chitrakoot.summary: Sita's parents arrive and the two families grieve together. Kausalya tells Sunayana that people, like gold, are proved by time. Janaka asks Bharat to decide, and Bharat declines: duty and self-interest pull apart, hatred is blind and love cannot reason, so he will follow Ram's wish. His few words leave the whole court in awe.

prasang:rcm.p.ram_bharat_resolution.title: Ram and Bharat settle it
prasang:rcm.p.ram_bharat_resolution.lesson: A good resolution gives each person a role and something to hold on to.
prasang:rcm.p.ram_bharat_resolution.summary: Ram tells Bharat that keeping their father's word is the duty of both brothers, and that the leader must be like the mouth, taking in only to nourish the whole body. He asks him to rule in his place, knowing it is the harder task. Bharat accepts, asking only for Ram's sandals to keep him going.

prasang:rcm.p.paduka.title: Bharat rules from a hut for fourteen years
prasang:rcm.p.paduka.lesson: You can live amid plenty without being owned by it.
prasang:rcm.p.paduka.summary: Bharat places Ram's sandals on the throne and lives outside the city in a hut, sleeping on grass, fasting, governing only as a caretaker. The palace's riches are all around him and do not touch him, like a bee in a champak garden.

prasang:rcm.p.maricha.title: Maricha caught between two deaths
prasang:rcm.p.maricha.lesson: A boss who threatens you into wrongdoing leaves no good option; see it early.
prasang:rcm.p.maricha.summary: Ravana orders his uncle Maricha to become a golden deer to lure Ram away. Maricha warns him that Ram cannot be defeated, but Ravana threatens him. Seeing death either way, Maricha reasons that it never pays to cross a powerful master, and chooses death at Ram's hands over death at Ravana's.

prasang:rcm.p.jatayu.title: Jatayu's last fight and Ram's grief
prasang:rcm.p.jatayu.lesson: Standing up for someone matters, even when you cannot win.
prasang:rcm.p.jatayu.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut and searches the forest, asking birds and trees if they have seen Sita. He finds the old vulture Jatayu dying; he had fought Ravana alone to stop the abduction. Ram tells him that for one whose heart is set on others' good, nothing is out of reach, and performs his funeral rites himself, as a son would.

prasang:rcm.p.shabari.title: Ram visits Shabari
prasang:rcm.p.shabari.lesson: What counts is the heart you bring, not who you are on paper.
prasang:rcm.p.shabari.summary: An old forest woman, Shabari, has waited years for Ram. When he comes she washes his feet and feeds him roots and fruit, and he praises every bite. He tells her he recognises only the bond of devotion and describes nine forms of it, ending with contentment, not hunting faults, and being simple and without guile.

prasang:rcm.p.pampa.title: Ram at Pampa on desire, anger and greed
prasang:rcm.p.pampa.lesson: Desire, anger and greed can unsettle anyone; knowing that is half the defence.
prasang:rcm.p.pampa.summary: Grieving, Ram walks with Lakshman through spring forests by Lake Pampa and describes the season as an army of desire. He names desire, anger and greed as three forces that can unsettle even the wisest mind in a moment, and notes that fruit-laden trees bow, as generous people do when they prosper.

prasang:rcm.p.marks_of_good.title: Ram tells Narada the marks of a good person
prasang:rcm.p.marks_of_good.lesson: Good people are uncomfortable with their own praise and glad at others'.
prasang:rcm.p.marks_of_good.summary: Narada asks Ram what marks a truly good person. Ram lists them: free of the six inner enemies, content, steady, generous with respect and seeking none, squirming at their own praise and glad at others', even-tempered and simple with everyone.

prasang:rcm.p.friendship_pact.title: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang:rcm.p.friendship_pact.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.
prasang:rcm.p.friendship_pact.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.

prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_bali.title: Sugriva and Bali: brothers split by a misunderstanding
prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_bali.lesson: Brothers can become enemies over one misread moment; ask before you assume betrayal.
prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_bali.summary: Bali chased a demon into a cave and told Sugriva to wait a fortnight. Sugriva waited a month; blood flowed out, he assumed Bali dead, sealed the cave and was made king. Bali fought his way out, decided his brother had betrayed him, and drove him out. Later, safe with Ram, Sugriva says that if he fought his brother even in a dream he'd be ashamed on waking.

prasang:rcm.p.tara.title: Ram consoles Tara
prasang:rcm.p.tara.lesson: Grief needs time; later, perspective on what is lost and what endures can comfort.
prasang:rcm.p.tara.summary: After Bali's death his wife Tara weeps over his body. Ram speaks to her gently: the body is made of five elements and lies here before her, but the self is not only this body; for whom is she weeping? Comforted, she asks for devotion, and Bali's son Angad is made heir.

prasang:rcm.p.seasons.title: Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
prasang:rcm.p.seasons.lesson: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.
prasang:rcm.p.seasons.summary: Waiting out the rains on a mountain, Ram points out lessons to Lakshman in each sight: clouds bow low when full, mountains take the rain as the steady take harsh words, small streams swagger, ponds fill drop by drop, autumn sun dries the puddles as contentment dries greed, and fish panic as the water shrinks.

prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_forgets.title: Sugriva forgets his promise
prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_forgets.lesson: Success and comfort make us forget who helped us; admit it quickly and make it right.
prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_forgets.summary: The rains end and Sugriva, now king, has forgotten his promise to search for Sita. Ram is hurt; Lakshman storms into the city in anger. Hanuman had already nudged Sugriva, who comes out, admits that comfort intoxicated him, and sends search parties in every direction.

prasang:rcm.p.sampati.title: Sampati's burned wings
prasang:rcm.p.sampati.lesson: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.
prasang:rcm.p.sampati.summary: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.

prasang:rcm.p.jambavant.title: Jambavant reminds Hanuman of his strength
prasang:rcm.p.jambavant.lesson: Sometimes we need someone else to remind us what we can do; and the old can be that someone.
prasang:rcm.p.jambavant.summary: Nobody can leap the ocean. Old Jambavant admits honestly that he is no longer young. Then he turns to the silent Hanuman and asks why he sits quiet: what task in the world is too hard for him? Hanuman grows to the size of a mountain.

prasang:rcm.p.surasa.title: Hanuman meets Surasa on the way
prasang:rcm.p.surasa.lesson: Meet obstacles with flexibility: sometimes bigger, sometimes smaller, never stuck.
prasang:rcm.p.surasa.summary: Leaping the ocean, Hanuman refuses to rest on a friendly mountain until the work is done. Surasa blocks him and opens her jaws; he doubles his size each time she widens them, then shrinks tiny and slips in and out. A demon that catches flyers by grabbing their shadows tries the same trick, and he sees through it at once.

prasang:rcm.p.lankini.title: Lankini at the gate of Lanka
prasang:rcm.p.lankini.lesson: Carry what you love into the hard place, and the hard place changes.
prasang:rcm.p.lankini.summary: Entering Lanka at night as small as a mosquito, Hanuman is caught by Lankini, the city's guardian. One blow of his fist floors her; she remembers a prophecy that this means the city's end, and blesses him: a moment of good company outweighs heaven, and if he carries Ram in his heart, poison will turn to nectar.

prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_hanuman.title: Hanuman finds a friend in Lanka
prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_hanuman.lesson: Even in a hostile place there may be one ally; find them.
prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_hanuman.summary: Searching Lanka, Hanuman is surprised to find a house with Ram's name on it. Its owner, Vibhishan, Ravana's brother, says he lives in Lanka like a tongue among teeth. Hanuman tells him even a restless monkey like himself was given Ram's love.

prasang:rcm.p.sita_hanuman.title: Hanuman reaches Sita
prasang:rcm.p.sita_hanuman.lesson: When someone is near despair, a message that they are remembered can carry them.
prasang:rcm.p.sita_hanuman.summary: Sita, captive and threatened by Ravana, has nearly lost hope; only the guard Trijata has been kind. Hanuman drops Ram's ring from a tree, then tells her Ram's whole story. Sita says he has been her ship in a sea of separation; he gives her Ram's message that speaking of pain helps, but there is no one to tell, and asks her to wait a few days more.

prasang:rcm.p.hanuman_ravan.title: Hanuman speaks plainly to Ravana
prasang:rcm.p.hanuman_ravan.lesson: Speak truth to power calmly, and afterwards don't take the credit.
prasang:rcm.p.hanuman_ravan.summary: Bound and dragged before Ravana, Hanuman feels no shame and tells the most powerful man in the world, calmly, to return Sita: wealth with no deep source dries up like a rain-fed river. Ravana orders his tail set on fire; Hanuman burns Lanka and returns. Back before Ram, he insists none of it was his own greatness.

prasang:rcm.p.mandodari_first.title: Mandodari pleads, the ministers flatter
prasang:rcm.p.mandodari_first.lesson: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.
prasang:rcm.p.mandodari_first.summary: Mandodari takes Ravana aside and begs him to return Sita before it is too late. He laughs at her fear and goes to court, where his ministers tell him only what pleases him. Tulsidas notes that when advisers, doctors and teachers speak only to please, ruin comes quickly.

prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_counsel.title: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_counsel.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.
prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_counsel.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.

prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_refuge.title: Vibhishan crosses over
prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_refuge.lesson: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.
prasang:rcm.p.vibhishan_refuge.summary: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.

prasang:rcm.p.ocean.title: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang:rcm.p.ocean.lesson: Always ask humbly first. But don't let humility be taken for weakness.
prasang:rcm.p.ocean.summary: On Vibhishan's advice, Ram first asks the ocean politely to let his army cross, and waits three days. When nothing changes, he takes up his bow, observing that counsel to the unwilling is like seed on barren soil. The ocean appears, apologises, and shows him how to build a bridge.

prasang:rcm.p.prahasta_mandodari.title: Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again
prasang:rcm.p.prahasta_mandodari.lesson: Some people cannot hear good advice; give it, then stop beating yourself up.
prasang:rcm.p.prahasta_mandodari.summary: Mandodari, hearing the bridge is built, again begs Ravana to pick fights only where he can win, and to step back. Ravana boasts. His son Prahasta tells the court that flatterers are many and honest advisers few, and suggests first sending an envoy. Ravana insults him, and Prahasta leaves saying good advice cannot reach one set on ruin.

prasang:rcm.p.angad_court.title: Angad in Ravana's court
prasang:rcm.p.angad_court.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.
prasang:rcm.p.angad_court.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.

prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_falls.title: Lakshman falls; Hanuman brings the mountain
prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_falls.lesson: When someone you love is ill, urgency and hope go together.
prasang:rcm.p.lakshman_falls.summary: Lakshman is struck down by Meghnad's spear. The physician Sushena names a herb on a far mountain, and Hanuman races there, sees through a demon disguised as a sage, and, not recognising the herb, carries the whole peak. Over Ayodhya Bharat shoots him down by mistake, then revives him and helps him on. At midnight Ram holds Lakshman and grieves aloud for a brother who left everything for him; Hanuman arrives just in time.

prasang:rcm.p.kumbhakarna.title: Kumbhakarna fights for a brother he knows is wrong
prasang:rcm.p.kumbhakarna.lesson: Siblings can choose differently and still bless each other.
prasang:rcm.p.kumbhakarna.summary: Woken to fight, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana plainly he was wrong to take Sita and should have consulted him first. Still he goes out to fight for his brother. On the field he meets Vibhishan, who chose Ram, and instead of cursing him, he blesses him as the pride of their family.

prasang:rcm.p.dharma_ratha.title: The chariot that wins
prasang:rcm.p.dharma_ratha.lesson: Inner qualities are the real equipment for a hard fight.
prasang:rcm.p.dharma_ratha.summary: Ravana rides out in a chariot; Ram stands on foot, and Vibhishan worries. Ram describes the chariot that really wins: courage and patience as its wheels, truth and character as its flag, strength, judgement, self-control and kindness as its horses.

prasang:rcm.p.homecoming_haste.title: Ram hurries home
prasang:rcm.p.homecoming_haste.lesson: When someone at home is waiting, no comfort elsewhere can hold you.
prasang:rcm.p.homecoming_haste.summary: After the war, Vibhishan begs Ram to stay a while, bathe and rest in Lanka's palaces. Ram says all of it is his as much as Vibhishan's, but thinking of Bharat waiting at home, each moment feels like an age; if he is late, he may not find his brother alive.

prasang:rcm.p.bharat_waiting.title: The last day of waiting
prasang:rcm.p.bharat_waiting.lesson: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.
prasang:rcm.p.bharat_waiting.summary: One day is left of the fourteen years and there is no word. Bharat wonders whether Ram has forgotten him, and his mind starts to sink. Just then Hanuman arrives like a boat and says Ram is coming. Bharat says no gift could repay this news.

prasang:rcm.p.bharat_milap.title: Ram comes home
prasang:rcm.p.bharat_milap.lesson: Homecoming means gratitude to those who carried you and kindness to those ashamed to face you.
prasang:rcm.p.bharat_milap.summary: From the air Ram points out his birthplace, dearer to him than heaven. Bharat falls at his feet; Ram lifts him up and the mothers run to him like cows to their calves at dusk. Ram introduces his friends as those who carried him through the war, and seeing Kaikeyi ashamed, goes to her house first.

prasang:rcm.p.farewell_friends.title: Ram says goodbye to his friends
prasang:rcm.p.farewell_friends.lesson: Friendships made in hard times deserve to be kept; say so out loud.
prasang:rcm.p.farewell_friends.summary: After six happy months, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends home with gifts. Angad, whose father is dead, begs to stay: Ram is his father and mother now. Ram embraces him and sends him on. To the boatman Guha he says: you are a brother to me; keep visiting.

prasang:rcm.p.ram_gita_saints.title: Ram on good people and difficult people
prasang:rcm.p.ram_gita_saints.lesson: Do good, feel others' joy as your own, and refuse the pleasure of gossip.
prasang:rcm.p.ram_gita_saints.summary: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and malicious people. Ram says the good are like sandalwood that perfumes the axe that cuts it; they feel others' sorrow and joy as their own and never speak harshly. The malicious burn at others' success and feast on gossip. No duty equals doing good to others.

prasang:rcm.p.ram_gita_citizens.title: Ram's address to the citizens
prasang:rcm.p.ram_gita_citizens.lesson: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.
prasang:rcm.p.ram_gita_citizens.summary: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.

prasang:rcm.p.garuda_doubt.title: Garuda's doubt
prasang:rcm.p.garuda_doubt.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.
prasang:rcm.p.garuda_doubt.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.

prasang:rcm.p.kakbhushundi_pride.title: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
prasang:rcm.p.kakbhushundi_pride.lesson: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.
prasang:rcm.p.kakbhushundi_pride.summary: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.

prasang:rcm.p.guru_insult.title: The student who would not stand for his teacher
prasang:rcm.p.guru_insult.lesson: Respect those who teach you; and forgive like the teacher who prayed for his rude student.
prasang:rcm.p.guru_insult.summary: In an earlier life Kakbhushundi was a proud, wealthy, sharp-tongued young man whose gentle teacher kept trying to guide him. One day in the temple he refused even to rise when the teacher entered. The teacher said nothing, but a curse fell on the student; the teacher at once prayed for him, asking that he not be punished in anger. Lives later, the one thorn Kakbhushundi still carries is the memory of that teacher's gentleness.

prasang:rcm.p.lomash.title: Arguing with Lomash
prasang:rcm.p.lomash.lesson: Even calm people burn when pushed too far; take correction without bitterness.
prasang:rcm.p.lomash.summary: As a young seeker Kakbhushundi went to the sage Lomash, who taught the formless God; Kakbhushundi kept arguing for his own view until the sage, provoked again and again, lost his temper and cursed him to become a crow. Kakbhushundi took it without fear or self-pity, and the sage, regretting his anger, called him back and taught him the Ramcharitmanas.

prasang:rcm.p.garuda_questions.title: Garuda's seven questions
prasang:rcm.p.garuda_questions.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.
prasang:rcm.p.garuda_questions.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.

prasang:vr.p.ocean_humility_firmness.title: Ram at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang:vr.p.ocean_humility_firmness.lesson: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.
prasang:vr.p.ocean_humility_firmness.summary: Ram lies on kusha grass by the shore for three days, asking the ocean for a way. Ignored, he tells Lakshman that patience is being taken for weakness and takes up his bow. The ocean rises, offers a way (Nala's bridge), and Ram releases the arrow elsewhere at its request.

prasang:bh.p.niti.murkha.title: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
prasang:bh.p.niti.murkha.lesson: Spend your effort where it can land; some minds will not move, and the first one to check is yours.
prasang:bh.p.niti.murkha.summary: Twelve verses on the futility of arguing with the closed or half-educated mind, framed as satire. The poet admits his own early arrogance (Niti 8) and ends by preferring wild mountains to the company of fools.

prasang:bh.p.niti.vidvat.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang:bh.p.niti.vidvat.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
prasang:bh.p.niti.vidvat.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.

prasang:bh.p.niti.manashaurya.title: Nitishatakam: Honour and spirit
prasang:bh.p.niti.manashaurya.lesson: Keep your dignity without needing to win every fight.
prasang:bh.p.niti.manashaurya.summary: Images of the lion and the elephant celebrate self-respect and inborn spirit. Some verses lean toward intolerance of insult, a warrior-king ideal.

prasang:bh.p.niti.artha.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang:bh.p.niti.artha.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.
prasang:bh.p.niti.artha.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.

prasang:bh.p.niti.durjana.title: Nitishatakam: On the wicked
prasang:bh.p.niti.durjana.lesson: Recognise spite for what it is, keep your distance, and stop taking it personally.
prasang:bh.p.niti.durjana.summary: A field guide to toxic people: the brilliant but cruel, the spiteful critic who turns every virtue into a fault, the boss nobody can please, and friendships that shrink like morning shade.

prasang:bh.p.niti.sujana.title: Nitishatakam: On the good
prasang:bh.p.niti.sujana.lesson: Be soft in good times and firm in bad ones, and let your good deeds stay quiet.
prasang:bh.p.niti.sujana.summary: Portraits of good people: steady in trouble, humble in success, giving in secret and speaking of others' kindness aloud. Company, the verses say, makes us what we are.

prasang:bh.p.niti.paropakara.title: Nitishatakam: On helping others
prasang:bh.p.niti.paropakara.lesson: Success should make you bow lower; real ornaments are listening, giving and helping.
prasang:bh.p.niti.paropakara.summary: Verses on generosity and friendship: trees bow with fruit, the hand shines by giving, a true friend keeps you from wrong and stays in trouble. Four kinds of people, from the selfless to those who harm for nothing.

prasang:bh.p.niti.dhairya.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang:bh.p.niti.dhairya.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.
prasang:bh.p.niti.dhairya.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.

prasang:bh.p.niti.daiva.title: Nitishatakam: On fate
prasang:bh.p.niti.daiva.lesson: Not everything is in your hands; that is a reason to act wisely, not to stop acting.
prasang:bh.p.niti.daiva.summary: Bhartrihari voices the case for fate with fables (Indra defeated, the rat that fed a starving snake, the bald man under the palm). Even here he insists one should still act after careful thought.

prasang:bh.p.niti.karma.title: Nitishatakam: On action
prasang:bh.p.niti.karma.lesson: Your actions are the one thing fate itself must answer to.
prasang:bh.p.niti.karma.summary: The answer to the fate section: even fate only delivers the fruit of actions, so bow to action itself. Weigh outcomes before rash deeds, keep steady under humiliation, and speak kindly. The closing verses are miscellaneous maxims in some editions.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.trishna.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.trishna.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.trishna.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.vishaya.title: Vairagyashatakam: The mockery of giving up pleasures
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.vishaya.lesson: Let go before you are forced to, and stop calling relief happiness.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.vishaya.summary: Pleasures will leave us anyway; letting them go freely brings peace, being dragged from them brings torment. We are worse than the moth, because we know the flame burns.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.yachna.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of begging and servility
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.yachna.lesson: Keep your dignity; ask for help for others before you ever grovel for yourself.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.yachna.summary: On the humiliation of begging favours from the rich: only hungry children could make a proud man ask. Contentment, not wealth, is real joy.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.bhoga.title: Vairagyashatakam: On the instability of pleasures
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.bhoga.lesson: Everything you hold carries fear; hold it more lightly.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.bhoga.summary: Everything carries its own fear, health is uprooted, life leaks like water from a cracked pot. Only dispassion is fearless.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.kala.title: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.kala.lesson: Time is passing while you're busy; notice it before it's gone.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.kala.summary: Time empties cities, houses and courts; the busy never notice it passing; parents and childhood friends become memories. The section ends with life as a play and death as the curtain.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.yati_nripati.title: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.yati_nripati.lesson: When the mind is content, nobody is richer than you.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.yati_nripati.summary: An ascetic tells a king who ignores him that learning equals wealth, that contentment in bark equals contentment in silk, and that pride over a few towns is a fever.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.manas.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.manas.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.manas.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.nitya.title: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.nitya.lesson: Do what matters most while you still can.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.nitya.summary: Weighing what lasts: religion without inner peace is trading; old age can bring neglect; act while healthy, not when the house is on fire. The poet admits not knowing how to spend a short life.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.shiva.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.shiva.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.shiva.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.

prasang:bh.p.vairagya.avadhuta.title: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.avadhuta.lesson: Let others' labels and small things pass; contentment makes you rich.
prasang:bh.p.vairagya.avadhuta.summary: Portraits of the wandering sage: unbothered when people argue over his caste, sleeping under the sky like a king, and finally bidding farewell to the five elements.

prasang:bh.p.story.amaraphala.title: The fruit of immortality (legend of Bhartrihari's renunciation)
prasang:bh.p.story.amaraphala.lesson: Betrayal can break you, or it can wake you up to what lasts.
prasang:bh.p.story.amaraphala.summary: A legend, not history. A poor brahmin is given a fruit of immortality and, thinking a long life of poverty useless, gives it to King Bhartrihari of Ujjain. The king gives it to his beloved queen; it passes from lover to lover and returns to his hands. Heartbroken, he speaks 'yam cintayami' (Niti 2), hands the throne to his brother Vikrama and becomes a renunciant.

prasang:yv.p.karunya_two_wings.title: Karunya stops acting: knowledge and action as two wings
prasang:yv.p.karunya_two_wings.lesson: Don't freeze while you wait to be sure. Understanding and action have to fly together.
prasang:yv.p.karunya_two_wings.summary: A student asks the sage Agastya whether freedom comes from action or from knowledge. Agastya answers with a story: young Karunya, confused by two scriptures, simply stopped doing anything, and his father had to show him that understanding and action work together.

prasang:yv.p.ram_despondency.title: Rama comes home from his pilgrimage and loses interest in everything
prasang:yv.p.ram_despondency.lesson: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.
prasang:yv.p.ram_despondency.summary: Sixteen-year-old Rama returns from a long pilgrimage and quietly withdraws: he stops eating properly, stops laughing, ignores his duties and sits alone. His attendants tell the worried king. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha say this is not illness or weakness but the first stirring of real questions, and ask that Rama be brought to them.

prasang:yv.p.ram_lament.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang:yv.p.ram_lament.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
prasang:yv.p.ram_lament.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.

prasang:yv.p.ram_questions.title: Rama asks how to live in the world without being crushed by it
prasang:yv.p.ram_questions.lesson: The real question isn't whether to quit life, but how to live it without being swallowed.
prasang:yv.p.ram_questions.summary: After his lament Rama turns to questions. How did King Janaka and others stay free while running kingdoms? How can a person work in the world untouched, like water on a lotus leaf? He asks for one practical skill that lets him work without sorrow.

prasang:yv.p.paurusha.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang:yv.p.paurusha.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.
prasang:yv.p.paurusha.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.

prasang:yv.p.four_gatekeepers.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang:yv.p.four_gatekeepers.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.
prasang:yv.p.four_gatekeepers.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.

prasang:yv.p.lila.title: Queen Lila fears losing her husband
prasang:yv.p.lila.lesson: Love brings the fear of loss; trying to control death only deepens the fear.
prasang:yv.p.lila.summary: Queen Lila loves her husband so much that she cannot bear the thought of his death. The wise tell her that nothing wins immortality, so she prays to the goddess Sarasvati instead. When the king dies, Sarasvati begins to show her that life and death are not what they seem.

prasang:yv.p.janaka.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang:yv.p.janaka.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
prasang:yv.p.janaka.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.

prasang:yv.p.punya_pavana.title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
prasang:yv.p.punya_pavana.lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.
prasang:yv.p.punya_pavana.summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.

prasang:yv.p.bali.title: Bali tires of endless days and asks his father's riddle
prasang:yv.p.bali.lesson: When life feels like a loop, the work is not more of it but mastering the mind that runs it.
prasang:yv.p.bali.summary: The demon king Bali has ruled the three worlds for ages. One day at his window he realises he is doing the same things day after day, night after night, and asks what any of it adds up to. He remembers a riddle his father Virochana once told him: a vast realm ruled by a silent king and an all-powerful minister. The minister is the mind; win it over, by practice, and everything is won.

prasang:yv.p.prahlada.title: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals
prasang:yv.p.prahlada.lesson: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.
prasang:yv.p.prahlada.summary: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.

prasang:yv.p.bhasa_vilasa.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang:yv.p.bhasa_vilasa.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.
prasang:yv.p.bhasa_vilasa.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.

prasang:yv.p.bhushunda.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
prasang:yv.p.bhushunda.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
prasang:yv.p.bhushunda.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.

prasang:yv.p.chudala.title: Queen Chudala teaches her husband what renunciation really is
prasang:yv.p.chudala.lesson: Running away doesn't free you; letting go inside does. Sometimes the teacher is the person beside you.
prasang:yv.p.chudala.summary: Queen Chudala finds inner peace, but her husband, King Shikhidhvaja, doesn't believe her. Restless, he leaves his kingdom for the forest. Chudala rules wisely in his absence and visits him disguised as a young sage, Kumbha, who shows him that giving up kingdom, home and body is not renunciation; letting go of the clinging mind is. Freed, he returns home and rules beside her.

prasang:yv.p.three_vows.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang:yv.p.three_vows.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.
prasang:yv.p.three_vows.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.

prasang:viv.p.chicago.welcome.title: 'Sisters and Brothers of America': Chicago, 11 September 1893
prasang:viv.p.chicago.welcome.lesson: You can belong fully to your own tradition and still honour every other path.
prasang:viv.p.chicago.welcome.summary: An unknown 30-year-old monk from India, with no invitation and little money, rises on the Parliament's opening day and greets the hall as 'Sisters and Brothers of America'. The audience stands and applauds for minutes. In a five-minute address he says India's faith accepts all religions as true and hopes the day marks the death-knell of fanaticism.

prasang:viv.p.chicago.frog.title: The frog in the well (Chicago, 15 September 1893)
prasang:viv.p.chicago.frog.lesson: Before you judge another faith or culture, check the size of your own well.
prasang:viv.p.chicago.frog.summary: Asked why religions quarrel, he tells of a frog who has lived all its life in a well. When a frog from the sea arrives and describes the ocean, the well-frog refuses to believe anything can be bigger than his well and drives the visitor out. Each of us, he says, sits in a little well and calls it the world.

prasang:viv.p.chicago.paper_on_hinduism.title: 'Children of immortal bliss': the Paper on Hinduism (Chicago, 19 September 1893)
prasang:viv.p.chicago.paper_on_hinduism.lesson: You are not a sinner to be fixed; you are a soul to be uncovered.
prasang:viv.p.chicago.paper_on_hinduism.summary: In his main paper he explains Hindu ideas to an American audience that had heard them mostly from critics. He refuses to call anyone a sinner, quoting the Upanishad's 'children of immortal bliss', and describes religions as stages of one search, travelling 'from truth to truth'.

prasang:viv.p.chicago.final_session.title: 'Help and not fight': the closing address (Chicago, 27 September 1893)
prasang:viv.p.chicago.final_session.lesson: Take in what is good from others, and keep growing as yourself.
prasang:viv.p.chicago.final_session.summary: On the last day he says no one should hope for unity through one religion's triumph. A seed takes in earth, air and water but grows into its own plant; so each faith should take in the others' spirit and grow by its own law.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.character.title: Karma-Yoga 1: how work makes character
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.character.lesson: Character is built in ordinary actions, and you are building it right now.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.character.summary: He defines karma as work and says character is the sum of the impressions our actions leave. Misery teaches as much as joy, and character shows in small daily actions, not big moments. The ideal worker finds calm in the middle of intense activity.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.each_is_great.title: Karma-Yoga 2: each is great in his own place
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.each_is_great.lesson: Measure yourself by your own ideal, not by someone else's.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.each_is_great.summary: Duty differs from person to person, so no one should be judged by another's standard. Hating yourself for not meeting someone else's ideal only weakens you. He ends with the story of a king who learns that the householder and the monk are each great in their own place.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.secret_of_work.title: Karma-Yoga 3: the secret of work
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.secret_of_work.lesson: Work like a master, not a slave; give without keeping accounts.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.secret_of_work.summary: The Gita's central idea is to work hard without being attached. Selfish work is slave's work; real love brings no pain; giving without expecting a return frees us. He closes with the Mahabharata story of the mongoose and the poor family's gift.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.duty.title: Karma-Yoga 4: what is duty?
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.duty.lesson: See others through their own eyes, and let love turn duty into something lighter.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.duty.summary: Duty cannot be defined from outside, since customs differ, so we should see others' duties through their eyes. Duty becomes sweet only through love, and small irritations are best met by forbearance. He passes on Pavhari Baba's secret: join the end and the means into one.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.vyadha.title: The proud ascetic, the housewife and the butcher
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.vyadha.lesson: No honest work is beneath you; doing it well is the practice.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.vyadha.summary: A young ascetic who can burn a bird with a glance is humbled by a housewife who knows what he did, and she sends him to a butcher in the market for teaching. The butcher, doing his trade honestly and caring for his parents, teaches him the highest truth. Doing the duty in front of you, without attachment, is itself the path.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.help_ourselves.title: Karma-Yoga 5: we help ourselves, not the world
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.help_ourselves.lesson: Helping is a privilege, not a debt someone owes you.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.help_ourselves.summary: The world does not need our help; helping is a privilege that makes us stronger. Expecting thanks brings unhappiness, so be grateful to the one you help. The world is a moral gymnasium, and calm people do the best work.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.non_attachment.title: Karma-Yoga 6: non-attachment
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.non_attachment.lesson: Care fully, but let go of the idea that everything depends on you.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.non_attachment.summary: All work mixes good and evil, so the way out is not to stop working but to stop clinging. The belief that others depend on us is the root of attachment and pain. Stand as a witness and keep working.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.freedom.title: Karma-Yoga 7: freedom
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.freedom.lesson: Be at rest, be free, and work.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.freedom.summary: Misery comes from attachment, not work. He attacks duty that has become a compulsion and asks for work done freely. The greatest people often die unknown, so seek no praise.

prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.ideal.title: Karma-Yoga 8: the ideal of Karma-Yoga
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.ideal.lesson: You don't have to escape your life to find peace; learn to work inside it.
prasang:viv.p.karma_yoga.ideal.summary: Every path, whether work, love, meditation or knowledge, leads to the same freedom. Do not flee the world-machine; learn the secret of work from inside it. He holds up the Buddha as the ideal worker who acted without personal motive.

prasang:viv.p.raja_yoga.monkey_mind.title: The drunken monkey: taming a restless mind
prasang:viv.p.raja_yoga.monkey_mind.lesson: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.
prasang:viv.p.raja_yoga.monkey_mind.summary: The mind is a monkey made drunk by desire, stung by jealousy and possessed by pride. The first practice is to sit and watch it without fighting; each day it grows calmer. Then take up one idea and let it fill your life.

prasang:viv.p.raja_yoga.summary.title: 'This is the whole of religion'
prasang:viv.p.raja_yoga.summary.lesson: Religion is growth from within; forms are helpers, not the point.
prasang:viv.p.raja_yoga.summary.summary: In one paragraph he sums up his teaching: each soul is potentially divine, and the goal is to bring that out through work, worship, mental discipline or philosophy. Doctrines, rituals, books and temples are secondary.

prasang:viv.p.work_and_its_secret.title: Work and its secret (Los Angeles, 1900)
prasang:viv.p.work_and_its_secret.lesson: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.
prasang:viv.p.work_and_its_secret.summary: His greatest lesson, he says, was to attend to the means as much as the end. Most failures come from neglecting the means, and most sorrow from clinging to what is already failing. Weakness invites misery, yet a heart that refuses to love also loses life's joys.

prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.faith.title: Practical Vedanta 1: faith in yourself (London, 1896)
prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.faith.lesson: Stop rehearsing your weakness; think of your strength and act.
