prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.faith.summary: Vedanta must work in ordinary life. Calm minds do the most work, angry ones break themselves. The new religion calls the person who does not believe in himself the atheist, and the remedy for weakness is to think of strength, not brood over weakness.

prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.temple_o.title: Practical Vedanta 2: the temple of the human body
prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.temple_o.lesson: Treat the person in front of you as sacred.
prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.temple_o.summary: Retelling Upanishadic stories such as Satyakama's, he argues that God is to be seen in every person. Real help comes from within, and we should look at others with sympathy, since they walk the road we walked.

prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.mistakes.title: Practical Vedanta 4: mistakes and light
prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.mistakes.lesson: Don't mourn the darkness; strike a match.
prasang:viv.p.practical_vedanta.mistakes.summary: He admits he has made many mistakes and would not be who he is without them. Weeping over darkness does not remove it; striking a match does. Build character instead of brooding over past wrongs.

prasang:viv.p.universal_religion.vessels.title: Cups, jars and buckets: the ideal of a universal religion
prasang:viv.p.universal_religion.vessels.lesson: Let each person, and each child, grow in their own shape.
prasang:viv.p.universal_religion.vessels.summary: Truth can be expressed in a hundred thousand ways, like water taking the shape of each vessel. His plan is 'Do not destroy': help if you can, never attack sincere convictions. No one can make another spiritual, just as no one makes a plant grow; we can only remove obstacles.

prasang:viv.p.universal_religion.pasaden.title: Many photographs of one sun (Pasadena, 1900)
prasang:viv.p.universal_religion.pasaden.lesson: Disagreement between thinking people is natural, not a threat.
prasang:viv.p.universal_religion.pasaden.summary: Speaking in a Universalist church, he welcomes sects because difference is a sign of thinking. Truth seen from different standpoints looks different, like photographs of one church from four corners. Spiritual ideas must reach each person in their own language.

prasang:viv.p.jnana.realisation.title: Nachiketa and the razor's edge (London, 1896)
prasang:viv.p.jnana.realisation.lesson: The way is long; don't despair, keep walking.
prasang:viv.p.jnana.realisation.summary: He reads the Katha Upanishad to a London audience: the boy Nachiketa, sent to Death, refuses every reward until he learns what lies beyond death. The path is like a razor's edge, long and hard, but he urges: struggle on, awake, arise.

prasang:viv.p.jnana.god_in_everything.title: Never mind failures (London, 1896)
prasang:viv.p.jnana.god_in_everything.lesson: Failure is part of the path; try once more.
prasang:viv.p.jnana.god_in_everything.summary: Fill the mind with the highest thoughts. Failures are natural, even the beauty of life; hold the ideal a thousand times, and if you fail a thousand times, try once more.

prasang:viv.p.calcutta_1897.title: Homecoming in Calcutta: 'Be not afraid' (1897)
prasang:viv.p.calcutta_1897.lesson: Fear is the main obstacle; act without it.
prasang:viv.p.calcutta_1897.summary: Back in his home city after four years in the West, he tells the young men of Calcutta that fear is the greatest superstition and fearlessness brings heaven in a moment. He ends with the Katha Upanishad's call, arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.

prasang:viv.p.kumbakonam.title: 'Awake from this hypnotism of weakness' (Kumbakonam, 1897)
prasang:viv.p.kumbakonam.lesson: Arise, awake: no one is really weak.
prasang:viv.p.kumbakonam.summary: In South India on his return, he quotes Katha 1.3.14 in Sanskrit and renders it 'Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached'. He asks his listeners to wake from the hypnotism of weakness, since no one is really weak.

prasang:viv.p.lahore.common_bases.title: Learn from all, imitate none (Lahore, 1897)
prasang:viv.p.lahore.common_bases.lesson: Absorb the best of where you live, and grow into yourself.
prasang:viv.p.lahore.common_bases.summary: Speaking to rival reform and orthodox groups, he looks for common ground. Religion must be realised, not repeated like a parrot. Learn everything good from others, as a seed takes in earth, air and water, but grow into your own tree and do not become others.

prasang:viv.p.jaffna.title: 'Whatever you think, that you will be' (Jaffna, 1897)
prasang:viv.p.jaffna.lesson: Thoughts shape us, so teach yourself and your children strength.
prasang:viv.p.jaffna.summary: On his first tour after the West he summarises Vedanta for the Hindus of Jaffna. Thinking yourself weak makes you weak; children should be raised strong and told of the glory of the soul. Learn to serve before you lead.

prasang:viv.p.madras.plan_of_campaign.title: 'Reject it as poison' (Madras, 1897)
prasang:viv.p.madras.plan_of_campaign.lesson: Judge ideas, and habits, by whether they make you stronger.
prasang:viv.p.madras.plan_of_campaign.summary: He answers critics who claimed others made his American success, noting how quickly sympathy vanishes when you dare to differ. His test of truth: whatever makes you weak in body, mind or spirit, reject as poison.

prasang:viv.p.letter.brave_boys.title: 'To my brave boys' (letter from New York, 1894)
prasang:viv.p.letter.brave_boys.lesson: Lead by serving, refuse gossip, and keep struggling.
prasang:viv.p.letter.brave_boys.summary: Writing to his young supporters in Madras, he says love, sincerity and patience are all they need. Struggle was his motto in the dark and still is in the light. Be the servant while leading, never listen to gossip about a friend, and have infinite patience.

prasang:viv.p.letter.khetri_1895.title: Ridicule, opposition, acceptance (letter to Khetri, 1895)
prasang:viv.p.letter.khetri_1895.lesson: Ridicule and opposition are stages, not verdicts.
prasang:viv.p.letter.khetri_1895.summary: Facing opposition from some clergy in America, he writes to his friend the Maharaja that every work passes through ridicule, opposition and then acceptance. Anyone ahead of their time will be misunderstood, so he will stay steady.

prasang:viv.p.letter.nanjunda_rao.title: 'Read the last lines whenever you feel worried or jealous' (1896)
prasang:viv.p.letter.nanjunda_rao.lesson: Expect slow success, stay steady, and drop jealousy.
prasang:viv.p.letter.nanjunda_rao.summary: The day before sailing for England, he sends a young doctor starting a magazine a few lines: go on bravely, don't expect success in a day or a year, hold to the highest, avoid jealousy. He tells him to reread them whenever worry or jealousy returns.

prasang:viv.p.letter.sympathy_1893.title: A letter to a grieving friend (Bombay, 1893)
prasang:viv.p.letter.sympathy_1893.lesson: Under the storm of grief there is a deeper calm; it is all right that the heart resists.
prasang:viv.p.letter.sympathy_1893.summary: Just before sailing for America, he writes to a friend struck by a terrible family loss. Quoting Job, Jesus and the Gita, he says that under the waves there is a depth of calm. He also admits the heart's agony fights against resignation, and prays for strength.

prasang:viv.p.letter.joe_1900.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang:viv.p.letter.joe_1900.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.
prasang:viv.p.letter.joe_1900.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.

prasang:viv.p.poem.hold_on.title: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang:viv.p.poem.hold_on.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.
prasang:viv.p.poem.hold_on.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.

prasang:viv.p.poem.requiescat.title: 'Requiescat in pace': for J. J. Goodwin (1898)
prasang:viv.p.poem.requiescat.lesson: Love can bless the one who has gone and let memory fill the gap.
prasang:viv.p.poem.requiescat.summary: When his English stenographer and devoted friend Goodwin died young in India, he wrote this farewell. It sends the soul on with blessing and says sweet remembrance fills the place left behind.

prasang:viv.p.concentration_detachment.title: Concentration and detachment
prasang:viv.p.concentration_detachment.lesson: Train the mind to focus and to let go; both matter.
prasang:viv.p.concentration_detachment.summary: All success depends on concentration, but along with it we must build the power to detach, since most suffering comes from a mind stuck on something it cannot let go. If he were educated again, he would train concentration and detachment rather than collect facts.

prasang:viv.p.inspired_talks.title: Inspired Talks at Thousand Island Park (June 1895)
prasang:viv.p.inspired_talks.lesson: Guard your thoughts; take what comes without clutching.
prasang:viv.p.inspired_talks.summary: In a summer retreat on an island in the St. Lawrence River, he taught a dozen students daily; Sarah Ellen Waldo took notes. Short sayings: thoughts live and travel far, so guard them; neither seek nor avoid, take what comes.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.vibhishan_refuge.title: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.vibhishan_refuge.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.vibhishan_refuge.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.

prasang:vr.p.bhakti.refuge.title: Valmiki: Ram's vow of refuge and the dove
prasang:vr.p.bhakti.refuge.lesson: Refuge is a vow, not a reward for the deserving: once someone says 'I'm yours', they are safe.
prasang:vr.p.bhakti.refuge.summary: Vibhishana arrives in the sky over Ram's camp. Sugriva argues he should be killed as a spy; Hanuman and Ram disagree. Ram tells the story of a dove that sheltered the hunter who had caught its mate, cites the sage Kandu on protecting whoever asks for shelter, and makes his vow: whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' gets safety from all beings, even if it were Ravana himself.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kevat.title: Kevat washes Ram's feet
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kevat.lesson: Love can be playful and stubborn; God enjoys being loved that way.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kevat.summary: At the Ganga the boatman refuses to row Ram across unless he can first wash his feet, joking that their dust turned a stone into a woman and might turn his boat into one too. Ram, whose name carries the world across, smiles and pleads with him. Afterwards the boatman refuses Sita's ring: today, he says, he has been paid in full.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shabari.title: Shabari's wait and the nine forms of devotion
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shabari.lesson: Your simple offering is enough; love, not status, is the only kinship that counts.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shabari.summary: An old woman of the forest has waited years for Ram on her teacher's word. When he comes she falls at his feet, washes them, and feeds him fruit he praises again and again. She says she does not know how to praise him; he answers that he recognises only the kinship of devotion, teaches her the nine forms of devotion, and tells her that whoever has even one of them is most dear to him.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.jatayu.title: Jatayu dies in Ram's lap
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.jatayu.lesson: Nothing you do for love is small; it is honoured like family.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.jatayu.summary: Searching for Sita, Ram finds the old vulture who fought Ravana to save her, dying. Ram touches his head and the bird's pain leaves. Jatayu refuses Ram's offer to heal him: the one whose name people pray to say at death is in front of his eyes. He asks only for devotion, and Ram, in tears, performs his last rites with his own hands.

prasang:vr.p.bhakti.jatayu.title: Valmiki: Ram cremates Jatayu like his father
prasang:vr.p.bhakti.jatayu.lesson: Grief for a loyal friend, even a bird, is real grief; honour it fully.
prasang:vr.p.bhakti.jatayu.summary: Jatayu dies telling Ram where Ravana went. Ram says this loss weighs on him more than Sita's abduction, that the bird is as worthy of honour as his father Dasharatha, builds the pyre himself and performs the rites as for his own kin.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_meets_ram.title: Hanuman meets Ram
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_meets_ram.lesson: You don't need the right method; being his is enough, and he weeps to have you back.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_meets_ram.summary: Sent by a frightened Sugriva, Hanuman goes disguised as a brahmin to question two strangers. When Ram names himself, Hanuman recognises his Lord, falls at his feet speechless, then gently complains that Ram forgot him. He says he knows no method of worship and relies on Ram as a child relies on its mother. Ram lifts him up, holds him, cools him with his own tears, and tells him he is twice as dear as Lakshman.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sugriva.title: Sugriva: frightened, lifted, forgetful, forgiven
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sugriva.lesson: Fear is heard, failure is forgiven, and then you get back to the work.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sugriva.summary: Sugriva, exiled and robbed by his brother, lives in fear even where Bali cannot reach him. Ram hears him and takes his side; after a first beating, Ram's touch takes the pain away, and Sugriva is made king. Then comfort makes him forget his promise to search for Sita. When he apologises, Ram smiles, says he is as dear as Bharat, and sends him back to work.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.bharat.title: Bharat's love: the boon, the meeting, the sandals
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.bharat.lesson: Love can be lived as responsibility: do the work in the name of the one you love.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.bharat.summary: Bharat, blamed for his mother's plot, asks the holy rivers for nothing but love for Ram, life after life; they tell him he torments himself for nothing. Walking toward Ram, shame slows him and remembering Ram's nature speeds him up. He falls at Ram's feet and Ram lifts him by force into an embrace. He returns with Ram's sandals and for fourteen years runs the kingdom from a hut, asking the sandals' leave for every task.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sutikshna.title: Sutikshna runs to meet Ram
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sutikshna.lesson: You don't have to feel qualified; the one with nowhere else to go is the one he loves.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sutikshna.summary: A young sage hears Ram is near and runs out, sure he has no devotion, wisdom or discipline worth anything, trusting only that Ram loves those with nowhere else to go. Lost in love he wanders, dances, forgets the way; Ram watches from behind a tree, then lifts him up and holds him. Asked for a boon, the sage says only: may this one pride never leave me, that I am his.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_vibhishan.title: Hanuman finds a devotee in Lanka
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_vibhishan.lesson: In a hostile place, one friend who shares your faith can be enough.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_vibhishan.summary: Searching Lanka by night, Hanuman wonders how a good person could live there, then hears someone wake saying 'Ram, Ram'. Vibhishan fears he has no practice or love worth Ram's notice; Hanuman, joking that no one wants to hear a monkey's name before breakfast, says that Ram showed kindness even to him, and weeps remembering it. The two talk of Ram late into the night and find a rest beyond words.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.ram_owes_hanuman.title: Ram cannot repay Hanuman
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.ram_owes_hanuman.lesson: Do the work, give away the credit, and ask only to keep loving.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.ram_owes_hanuman.summary: Back from Lanka, Hanuman tells Ram how Sita survives: his name guards her day and night. Ram, in tears, asks whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers that the only calamity is forgetting him. Ram says he can never repay Hanuman and cannot even look him in the face; Hanuman falls at his feet and will not get up. Offered anything, he asks only for unwavering devotion, and credits every deed to Ram.

prasang:vr.p.bhakti.hanuman_boon.title: Valmiki: Hanuman's boon and Ram's debt
prasang:vr.p.bhakti.hanuman_boon.lesson: The deepest gratitude hopes the other never needs your help.
prasang:vr.p.bhakti.hanuman_boon.summary: After the coronation Ram sends his friends home, asking only to be remembered with love. Hanuman asks to live as long as Ram's story is told, so that hearing it can ease his longing. Ram rises from the throne, embraces him, grants it, and says he would give his life for each of Hanuman's services, and hopes Hanuman never falls into trouble that would let him repay it.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.jayant.title: Jayant the crow: shelter for the offender
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.jayant.lesson: Consequences may remain, but the one who turns back is still taken in.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.jayant.summary: Indra's son, disguised as a crow, pecks Sita's foot to test Ram's power. Ram's straw arrow chases him through every world; no god will shelter him. Narada sends him back to Ram, where he falls at his feet admitting he reaped what he sowed. Ram lets him go with the loss of one eye.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.spear.title: Ram takes the spear meant for Vibhishan
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.spear.lesson: A promise of shelter is kept with one's own body.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.spear.summary: In the final battle Ravana hurls a deadly spear at his brother Vibhishan. Remembering his vow to break the pain of those who come to him, Ram pushes Vibhishan behind him and takes the spear on himself.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.farewell.title: The friends who couldn't leave
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.farewell.lesson: Pure love moves God more than any practice; it can even change his plans.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.farewell.summary: Vibhishan showers jewels from the flying chariot; the monkeys put them in their mouths and spit them out, and Ram, whom sages cannot reach in meditation, laughs with them. He thanks them, tells them to go home and remember him without fear. They stand weeping, unable to speak or leave, so he changes his plan and takes them all to Ayodhya.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kakbhushundi.title: The child Ram and the crow
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kakbhushundi.lesson: You are loved for loving, not for being impressive.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kakbhushundi.summary: The crow-sage Kakbhushundi, after being humbled by the child Ram's play, receives his boon. Ram tells him devotees are always dear to him, that status counts for nothing without love, and gives the parable of a father with many gifted sons whose dearest son is the one who simply loves him, though skilled at nothing. Then the Lord goes back to being a hungry baby and cries until his mother runs to him.

prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.petition.title: Tulsidas's petition is signed
prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.petition.lesson: After all the pleading, the book ends held: you were already noticed.
prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.petition.summary: Tulsidas wrote the Vinay Patrika as a petition to Ram's court. In the last two padas he asks Hanuman, Bharat and Lakshman to mention him at the right moment. Lakshman, reading Hanuman's mind and Bharat's wish, speaks up: one servant has kept faith in the name even in this age. The court agrees, Ram smiles, says he has already taken note, and signs.

prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.tulsidas_life.title: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps
prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.tulsidas_life.lesson: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.tulsidas_life.summary: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shiva_parvati.title: Shiva answers Parvati's doubt
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shiva_parvati.lesson: Honest doubt, asked humbly, is welcomed; the answer is love.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shiva_parvati.summary: Parvati, who in a past life as Sati doubted that a grieving prince could be God, now asks Shiva humbly: how can the formless one take a body? Shiva praises her question, bows to the child Ram, and answers that the formless becomes embodied out of love for devotees, and comes whenever good people suffer.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.ahalya.title: Ahalya: the long wait ends
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.ahalya.lesson: However long you have been frozen, being seen can bring you back to life.
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.ahalya.summary: On the way to Janakpur, Vishvamitra shows Ram a stone in an empty hermitage: Gautam's wife Ahalya, bearing a curse in a body of stone, longing for the dust of his feet. At his touch she rises, stands before him with folded hands, unable to speak for love, tears streaming, and asks only that her mind may always drink at his feet.

prasang:mbh.p.k.draupadi_durvasa.title: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens
prasang:mbh.p.k.draupadi_durvasa.lesson: When you have nothing left to offer, calling out is enough; help can come from a single leaf.
prasang:mbh.p.k.draupadi_durvasa.summary: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.

prasang:mbh.p.k.draupadi_kamyaka.title: Draupadi tells Krishna her sorrow
prasang:mbh.p.k.draupadi_kamyaka.lesson: You can bring God your rawest pain, even your sense of being abandoned, and be heard.
prasang:mbh.p.k.draupadi_kamyaka.summary: Krishna visits the exiled Pandavas in the Kamyaka forest and tells Arjuna 'you are mine and I am yours'. Draupadi then comes to him 'seeking refuge with the refuge', tells him, out of closeness, everything done to her in the dice-hall and since, and weeps that she has no one, not even him. Krishna promises she will see justice.

prasang:mbh.p.k.vidura_hospitality.title: Krishna refuses the king's feast and eats at Vidura's house
prasang:mbh.p.k.vidura_hospitality.lesson: God accepts love, not lavishness; a simple meal given with devotion is the real feast.
prasang:mbh.p.k.vidura_hospitality.summary: On his peace mission to Hastinapura, Krishna declines Duryodhana's lavish banquet: food is shared out of love or out of need, and here there is neither. He goes instead to Vidura's modest house, eats the simple food offered with devotion, and that night Vidura tells him he cannot describe the joy of seeing him.

prasang:mbh.p.k.krishna_bhishma.title: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows
prasang:mbh.p.k.krishna_bhishma.lesson: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.
prasang:mbh.p.k.krishna_bhishma.summary: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.

prasang:mbh.p.k.bhishma_departure.title: Bhishma asks Krishna's leave to die
prasang:mbh.p.k.bhishma_departure.lesson: At the end, it is enough to say: I am yours; now let me go.
prasang:mbh.p.k.bhishma_departure.summary: When the sun turns north, Bhishma, after fifty-eight nights on the arrows, takes leave of the family, asks Krishna to protect him and to give him leave to go. Krishna says there is no fault in him and lets him go; Bhishma's last words to the family are to hold to truth and kindness.

prasang:mbh.p.k.markandeya_child.title: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf
prasang:mbh.p.k.markandeya_child.lesson: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
prasang:mbh.p.k.markandeya_child.summary: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.

prasang:mbh.p.k.parikshit.title: The stillborn heir and Krishna's promise
prasang:mbh.p.k.parikshit.lesson: In a family's darkest hour, the women's cry is heard and the promise kept.
prasang:mbh.p.k.parikshit.summary: Abhimanyu's son is born dead, struck in the womb by Ashvatthama's weapon. Kunti, Subhadra and Uttara beg Krishna for help, reminding him of his promise. Krishna, on the strength of his own truthfulness, revives the child, who is named Parikshit.

prasang:mbh.p.k.sahasranama_frame.title: Yudhishthira's question: what is the one refuge?
prasang:mbh.p.k.sahasranama_frame.lesson: After every rule has been explained, the last question is simply: whom do I turn to?
prasang:mbh.p.k.sahasranama_frame.summary: After all the teachings on dharma, Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for the one god, the one refuge, the best dharma. Bhishma answers: praising the imperishable Vishnu with devotion, the purest of the pure and father of beings, and gives the thousand names. In the closing dialogue the Lord says one sincere verse is enough.

prasang:sur.p.k.gajendra.title: The elephant who finally called (as Surdas sings it)
prasang:sur.p.k.gajendra.lesson: Fight with everything you have; when your strength runs out, call. Help comes running.
prasang:sur.p.k.gajendra.summary: An elephant king is seized by a crocodile in a lake and struggles for a thousand years with all his strength and his herd. Only when his strength is gone does he call out to Hari, who leaves his mount behind and runs barefoot to free him. Surdas returns to the story again and again (vp.11, 21, 241, 256).

prasang:sur.p.k.sudama.title: Sudama at Krishna's door (as Surdas sings it)
prasang:sur.p.k.sudama.lesson: Old friendship and love do not check your bank balance at the door.
prasang:sur.p.k.sudama.summary: Krishna's poor childhood friend Sudama walks to Dwaraka with a handful of rice, ashamed of his poverty. Seeing him from far off, Krishna runs to him and touches his feet, and receives his little gift as if it were everything.

prasang:up.p.shvet_inquiry_to_refuge.title: Shvetashvatara: from 'what governs our lives?' to refuge
prasang:up.p.shvet_inquiry_to_refuge.lesson: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.
prasang:up.p.shvet_inquiry_to_refuge.summary: Seekers ask what causes the world and governs their joys and sorrows. Through meditation they come to see one Lord, Rudra-Shiva, hidden in every heart; the Upanishad moves from inquiry to recognition to a prayer of refuge (6.18) and ends on grace and love of God (6.21, 6.23).

prasang:up.p.devi_who_are_you.title: The gods ask the Goddess: who are you?
prasang:up.p.devi_who_are_you.lesson: The Mother who is everything is also near enough to be called on in fear.
prasang:up.p.devi_who_are_you.summary: All the gods come to the Goddess and ask who she is. She answers that she is the highest reality, the source of nature and spirit. The gods bow, praise her as the Mother who protects on every side, and take refuge in her as Durga, who carries beings through hard places.

prasang:rcm.p.shiva_grief_name.title: Shiva's grief turns to Ram's name
prasang:rcm.p.shiva_grief_name.lesson: Grief and devotion can walk together; steady love in loss is seen.
prasang:rcm.p.shiva_grief_name.summary: After Sati is gone, Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, repeating his name. Though beyond desire, he still grieves the loss of his devotee. Seeing his steady love, Ram appears, grateful and kind, praises Shiva's vow and asks him to marry Parvati.

prasang:rcm.p.rati_shiva_grace.title: Rati comes weeping to the god who burned her husband
prasang:rcm.p.rati_shiva_grace.lesson: Even the one who hurt you can be approached; compassion answers grief.
prasang:rcm.p.rati_shiva_grace.summary: Kama, sent by the gods to break Shiva's meditation, is burned by his third eye. His wife Rati, fainting and weeping, goes straight to Shiva and pleads. Shiva, quick to be pleased and compassionate, promises her that Kama will live on without a body and that she will meet him again when Krishna is born.

prasang:rcm.p.shiva_wedding.title: Parvati's trust and Shiva's strange wedding
prasang:rcm.p.shiva_wedding.lesson: Love sees past appearances; trust can comfort the people who fear for us.
prasang:rcm.p.shiva_wedding.summary: The sages tease Parvati that Shiva has burned Kama and her vow is lost; she smiles and trusts him. Shiva arrives with ash, snakes and a wild band of ghosts; Parvati's mother Maina breaks down and blames herself. Parvati comforts her, Narada reveals who Parvati is, and the wedding is celebrated, with Shiva remembering Ram in his heart.

prasang:rcm.p.shiva_parvati_samvad.title: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance
prasang:rcm.p.shiva_parvati_samvad.lesson: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.
prasang:rcm.p.shiva_parvati_samvad.summary: On Kailash, Parvati sits beside Shiva and, still carrying her old doubt from her life as Sati, asks how a grieving prince can be God. Shiva is moved to tears, reassures her that there is no doubt left in her heart, and explains that the formless becomes form out of love for devotees. Her confusion lifts 'like autumn heat under moonlight'.

prasang:yv.p.prahlada_refuge.title: Prahlada, alone after defeat, takes refuge in Narayana
prasang:yv.p.prahlada_refuge.lesson: Refuge is open to anyone, whatever their past; devotion kept up daily changes the mind.
prasang:yv.p.prahlada_refuge.summary: With his father killed and his people beaten, the young demon prince Prahlada sees no way out except to take refuge in the very god he feared. He worships Vishnu in mind and in his shrine; the gods doubt a demon can be devoted, but Vishnu tells them he is ready. Vishnu appears, Prahlada sings a hymn of refuge, sinks into realisation and is gently woken to rule with a steady mind.

prasang:yv.p.shiva_true_worship.title: Shiva teaches Vasishtha what worship really is
prasang:yv.p.shiva_true_worship.lesson: Worship can be carried into every hour as calm, kindness and gladness.
prasang:yv.p.shiva_true_worship.summary: Shiva and Parvati visit Vasishtha's hermitage; Vasishtha tells Shiva that remembering him has filled his life. Asked how God should be worshipped, Shiva says the true God is awareness itself; its flowers are understanding, evenness and calm, and real worship runs through walking, standing, waking and sleeping, offered with equanimity, compassion and gladness.

prasang:dheesh_gita.p.seers_find_peace.title: Learned seers find no peace and go to Ganesha
prasang:dheesh_gita.p.seers_find_peace.lesson: Learning alone may not settle the heart; turning to God can.
prasang:dheesh_gita.p.seers_find_peace.summary: Seers who had received all the Vedas still found no peace, so they went to Ganesha's world and took refuge in him. Ganesha tells them that though he has no form, loving devotees see him in the form they long for, and that knowing his highest form brings lasting peace.

prasang:surya_gita.p.vision_and_bhakti.title: Overwhelmed sages ask the Sun for a gentle form, and learn devotion
prasang:surya_gita.p.vision_and_bhakti.lesson: When the vastness is too much, love is a door small enough to walk through.
prasang:surya_gita.p.vision_and_bhakti.summary: The sages ask Surya to show his cosmic form; seeing it, they lose their peace and take refuge, asking for his gentle form again. Surya tells them to fix their minds on him; they admit their minds are restless as wind, and he teaches that devotion is simply the love we feel for friends and family turned toward God.

prasang:shambhu_gita.p.pitris_hymn.title: The ancestors' hymn to Shiva and his easy way
prasang:shambhu_gita.p.pitris_hymn.lesson: You can hand over the outcome and still keep working, with devotion woven through.
prasang:shambhu_gita.p.pitris_hymn.summary: Bewildered by Shiva's limitless form, the ancestors praise him and finally hand him the outcome: do whatever is truly good for us. Shiva tells them their work needs a mind joined to him, then gives an easy way: see him everywhere, even in a loving embrace, so devotion never lapses amid hard work.

prasang:shakti_gita.p.gods_praise_mother.title: The victorious gods praise the Mother's grace
prasang:shakti_gita.p.gods_praise_mother.lesson: Grace is not earned by praise; even the clumsy prayer is held.
prasang:shakti_gita.p.gods_praise_mother.summary: After their victory over the demons, the gods praise the Mother, admit their words cannot reach her, and ask forgiveness, adding that even forgiveness comes from her grace. They describe her taking form for devotees' sake and never letting go of those who love her feet.

prasang:vr.p.hanuman_chambers_unease.title: Hanuman's unease in Ravana's chambers
prasang:vr.p.hanuman_chambers_unease.lesson: Judge yourself by your intention and your mind's state, not only by what your eyes happened to meet while doing your duty.
prasang:vr.p.hanuman_chambers_unease.summary: Searching Ravana's palace at night, Hanuman finds himself looking across Ravana's sleeping wives and is seized by fear that he has broken dharma. He examines his own mind, finds it unmoved, reasons that the search itself required it, and goes on searching with a clear conscience.
